b_rows_sample.anchor: D-1 · The four unforced operations, and with them ℛ's shape. Are Transform, Merge, Split, Reintroduce mandatory or optional? ... Recommendation: (c) or (d).
b_rows_sample.statement: Decision D-1: whether Transform, Merge, Split, Reintroduce are mandatory or optional operations, which determines what the universal quantifier over operations ranges over (hence whether congruence and global minimality are provable) and whether R must recover fields from the corpus's r=(E1,E2,T,R,Q,E,Sigma,tau) 8-tuple; recommends option (c) Transform-only or (d) open-ended-with-mandatory-core, with a caveat that restoring a bare, policy-unparameterized Sigma field into r would be ill-typed.

b_rows_sample.anchor: D-2 · Type the referent of humanActRef? ... Recommendation: (b) — smallest change that closes a failure already on the record, and it extends the existing Grant rather than creating a second mechanism (ES-005.4).
b_rows_sample.statement: Decision D-2: whether to give the human act referenced by Grant.humanActRef its own identity (status quo; add actId while keeping free text; a fully structured act record; or make grantId globally unique only), recommending option (b) as the smallest change closing an already-realized production failure while extending rather than duplicating the existing Grant mechanism.

b_rows_sample.anchor: D-3′ · Residue only — rule instance or rule version? ... Recommendation: rule version — it composes with Policy=(id,version) and makes replay deterministic. Low stakes; defer if you prefer.
b_rows_sample.statement: Decision D-3' (the sole residue of D-3): whether Step 157.22's Method field references a rule instance or a rule version, recommending rule version since it composes with Policy=(id,version) and makes replay deterministic, flagged as low-stakes and deferrable.

b_rows_sample.anchor: GN-73 records a MATERIAL COLLISION WITH THE RATIFIED LANE, raised by another session and awaiting you: the policy-change loop was closed twice, differently — ratified I-11 + R-1 (v0.2, GN-19) and again by the 2026-08-30 audit — "two unreconciled resolutions of one problem (ES-005.4)".
b_rows_sample.statement: A standing governance item not owned by this pass: GN-73 flags that the policy-change loop has been closed twice by two different, unreconciled resolutions (ratified I-11+R-1 at v0.2/GN-19, and again by the 2026-08-30 audit), a material collision awaiting human/governance reconciliation.

group_evidence.why_grouped: labels share the notation 'D-0'

a_rows_sample.anchor: A decision-ready state is the Knowledge State presented to the Knower in a form that is comprehensible, actionable, and faithful to the underlying epistemic structure, enabling the Knower to make an informed decision.
a_rows_sample.statement: Original Q24 definition (later corrected): a decision-ready state IS the Knowledge State presented to the Knower in comprehensible, actionable, faithful form. Key boxed claims: Presentation ≠ Dump of Raw Data; Presentation = Structured, Epistemically Qualified, Purpose-Tailored View; Presentation must preserve the epistemic status of each assertion.

a_rows_sample.anchor: P_t = \text{Present}(K_t, I_t, U_t, \Delta_t, Q_t, C_t, N_t, \text{Format})
a_rows_sample.statement: The Presentation Function: Present maps (K,I,U,Δ,Q,C,N,F) to a presentation P_t; nine presentation components listed (State Summary, Key Findings, Gaps and Conflicts, Ideal Comparison, Risks and Implications, Recommendations, Epistemic Status, Provenance, History); five presentation layers (Executive Summary, Epistemic State, Comparison with Ideal, Risks and Implications, Recommendations), each with purpose/content/format.

type_signature.domain: K x I x U x Δ x Q x C x N x Format

a_rows_sample.anchor: Decision Context:\n   "You are deciding whether to participate in the battle."
a_rows_sample.statement: Presentation formats illustrated with the Arjuna case: Natural Language Summary, Structured View (assertion/status/evidence/conflict table), Visual View (graph with a conflict warning), and Comparative View (dimension/current/ideal/gap table); repeated in section 8 as 'The Arjuna Example: Presentation' with an executive summary, epistemic state view and comparative view.

a_rows_sample.anchor: | **Very Strong** | Very High Confidence | 🟢 |
a_rows_sample.statement: Epistemic status indicator vocabularies for UI: Confidence Indicators (Very Strong/Strong/Moderate/Weak/None with colors), Conflict Indicators (None/Potential/Active/Resolved), Gap Indicators (Missing Dimension/Unknown Value/Missing Evidence/Stale Knowledge).

a_rows_sample.anchor: Q(P_t) = w_F \cdot \text{Fidelity} + w_C \cdot \text{Comprehensibility} + w_A \cdot \text{Actionability} + w_M \cdot \text{Completeness}
a_rows_sample.statement: Original presentation quality criteria (Fidelity, Comprehensibility, Actionability, Completeness, each in [0,1]) combined into a single weighted Presentation Quality Score Q(P_t); four original invariants: Presentation ≠ Raw Data; must preserve epistemic status; must be comprehensible; must be actionable.

a_rows_sample.anchor: This is the complete mathematical specification of KnowledgeOS.
a_rows_sample.statement: Original document's closing claim, later retracted: a 24-item list of the 'complete KnowledgeOS model' (Observation, Dimension, Proposition, Assertion, Evidence, Epistemic State, Knowledge State, Understanding State, Domain State, Ideal State, Coherence, Conflict, Gap, Distance, Zero/Lord/Sārathi Lens, Transition, History, Complete System State, Discrepancy, Prioritization, Decision-Ready State, Presentation) is declared 'the complete mathematical specification of KnowledgeOS'.

a_rows_sample.anchor: S_t \xrightarrow{\text{evaluate}} D_t \xrightarrow{\text{project}} P_t
a_rows_sample.statement: Fundamental correction: presentation must not become part of the epistemic state itself; it is a projection for a Knower/purpose/decision/format. Pipeline corrected to S_t --evaluate--> D_t --project--> P_t, where S_t is the complete internal state, D_t the decision-ready assessment/posture, P_t the human-facing projection. Establishes P_t ≠ D_t and P_t ≠ S_t: presentation is a view/projection, not another knowledge object.

a_rows_sample.anchor: A decision-ready state exists before presentation.
a_rows_sample.statement: Corrected definition: 'A decision-ready state is an evaluated system state in which the knowledge relevant to a specific decision satisfies the applicable decision criteria. Presentation is the projection of that state into a form usable by the Knower.' Formalized as DecisionReady(S_t,D,P,C) followed by P_t = Present(DecisionReadyState, Knower, Format), preserving the Q23 distinction.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Presentation = Epistemically\ Qualified\ Projection
a_rows_sample.statement: Deeper DDD point: Present() must not be understood as 'turn database objects into UI' but as a semantic projection that decides what is relevant, critical, uncertain, conflicting, missing, evidenced, recommendation-vs-fact, and inference-vs-observation. Presentation = Epistemically Qualified Projection.

a_rows_sample.anchor: \Pi_{N,D,P,C,F}
a_rows_sample.statement: New concept: Presentation Projection Π_{N,D,P,C,F} parameterized by Knower N, Decision D, Purpose P, Context C, Format F, giving P_t = Π_{N,D,P,C,F}(S_t). Enables two different Knowers to receive different presentations of the same underlying state without KnowledgeOS holding two different Knowledge States.

a_rows_sample.anchor: CriticalEpistemicDistinctions(S_t) \subseteq Preserved(P_t)
a_rows_sample.statement: Presentation is loss-aware: as a projection it may lose information but must not lose epistemically important distinctions — e.g. Observed/Reported/Inferred/Assumed must not all collapse into 'FACT', and Strong/Weak/No evidence must not all collapse into 'CONFIDENT'. Defines EpistemicFidelity(P_t,S_t) and requires CriticalEpistemicDistinctions(S_t) ⊆ Preserved(P_t) as one of the most important invariants of the presentation architecture.

a_rows_sample.anchor: ConfidenceIndicator = DerivedView(\Sigma)
a_rows_sample.statement: Recommends removing 'Confidence' (Very Strong/Strong/Moderate/Weak/None) as the primary presentation model because it risks collapsing the multidimensional epistemic state established in Q16 (Acquisition ≠ Support ≠ Uncertainty ≠ Validity). A table example shows presenting each claim's Acquisition/Support/Uncertainty/Validity separately; a UI may then derive a simplified indicator: ConfidenceIndicator = DerivedView(Σ), not Confidence = Σ.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Fidelity(P_t,S_t)=Required
a_rows_sample.statement: Rejects the original weighted Presentation Quality Score Q(P_t) as formal theory because it again permits compensation: a presentation could score 95% comprehensibility/actionability/completeness while misrepresenting one critical epistemic status, and still get a high score — unacceptable. Replaces with hard presentation invariants: Fidelity(P_t,S_t)=Required, CriticalEpistemicStatusPreserved(P_t,S_t), DecisionRelevantInformationPreserved(P_t,D); optional metrics may still assess quality afterward.

a_rows_sample.anchor: CompleteForDecision(P_t,D)
a_rows_sample.statement: Completeness should be formalized as decision-relative, CompleteForDecision(P_t,D), not generic Complete(P_t), since a presentation can deliberately omit decision-irrelevant information; expressed generally as Relevance = f(Knower, Purpose, Decision, Context).

a_rows_sample.anchor:
Decision
ightarrow
Knowledge
ightarrow
Evidence
ightarrow
Discrepancy
ightarrow
Action
a_rows_sample.statement: Keeps the five presentation layers but re-semanticizes them: Layer 1 Decision (what decision is supported), Layer 2 Evidence/Knowledge (what do we know), Layer 3 Epistemic qualification (how do we know it), Layer 4 Discrepancy/Risk (what remains uncertain/problematic), Layer 5 Guidance (what should the Knower consider next) — giving the progression Decision→Knowledge→Evidence→Discrepancy→Action.

a_rows_sample.anchor: CurrentState \neq History
a_rows_sample.statement: History should not be dumped into the main presentation but disclosed progressively: primary view answers 'what is the state now?', user can expand to 'how did we arrive here?'. CurrentState ≠ History, but History -> ExplanationOfCurrentState.

a_rows_sample.anchor:
KnowledgeOS Core

Owns:

K,\Sigma,E,G,C,\Delta,I,S
a_rows_sample.statement: Introduces three bounded responsibilities/contexts: KnowledgeOS Core (owns K,Σ,E,G,C,Δ,I,S), Epistemic Orchestration (owns Zero, Lord, Sārathi, Prioritization, Transition), and Presentation/Interaction (owns Projection, View, Format, Explanation, Interaction), with a layered diagram Core -> Epistemic Assessment -> Decision State -> Presentation Projection -> (Executive/Detailed/Graph views).

a_rows_sample.anchor: D_t = Evaluate(S_t,P,D,C,Policy)
a_rows_sample.statement: Revised mathematical model: D_t = Evaluate(S_t,P,D,C,Policy); P_t = Π(S_t,D_t,N,F); with P_t ≢ S_t and P_t ≢ D_t, and P_t defined as 'human-oriented projection of S_t under D_t'.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Presentation \neq RawData
a_rows_sample.statement: Nine new presentation invariants recommended to be frozen: Presentation ≠ RawData; Presentation ≠ KnowledgeState; Presentation ≠ Decision; Recommendation ≠ Fact; Candidate ≠ Knowledge; Presentation must preserve critical epistemic distinctions; Presentation must preserve provenance for decision-relevant claims; Presentation completeness is decision-relative; Presentation is a projection, not a mutation of the Knowledge State.

a_rows_sample.anchor: ConceptualCompleteness \neq FormalCompleteness
a_rows_sample.statement: Retracts the original document's closing claim that the 24-question model is 'the complete mathematical specification of KnowledgeOS'; proposes calling it instead 'KnowledgeOS Epistemic Model — Conceptual and Formal Specification', listing items still needing formalization: exact ontology/type system, proposition semantics, evidence model, inference semantics, conflict algebra, gap detection semantics, Ideal State construction, discrepancy semantics, decision criteria, transition semantics, authorization/governance, persistence semantics, concurrency/versioning, presentation projection semantics. States ConceptualCompleteness ≠ FormalCompleteness.

b_rows_sample.anchor: the opposite of belief is not necessarily disbelief; the proper opposite can be conscious ignorance or doubt. Deliberate doubt can amount to a 'not proven' verdict because the evidence does not determine either side. ... NOT_PROVEN != REJECTED.
b_rows_sample.statement: Whately's doubt-is-not-disbelief distinction motivates preserving BELIEF/DISBELIEF/DOUBT/IGNORANCE/INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE as potentially distinct states and adding a NOT_PROVEN state distinct from REJECTED to the epistemic-state model.

b_rows_sample.anchor: DDD says we should separate dimensions. ... Claim: EpistemicStanding, EvidenceCondition, AuthorityStanding, OperationalDisposition. ... Otherwise we create a combinatorial state machine.
b_rows_sample.statement: Self-correction of the previously proposed single combined epistemic-state list into four independent Claim-attached dimensions (EpistemicStanding, EvidenceCondition, AuthorityStanding, OperationalDisposition), avoiding a combinatorial single state machine.

b_rows_sample.anchor: UNKNOWN does not necessarily mean: Nobody knows. It can mean: The current inquiry has not established an epistemically sufficient standing for this proposition. ... UNKNOWN_TO_US while KNOWN_BY_SOURCE_A or KNOWN_IN_CONTEXT_B.
b_rows_sample.statement: Refines UNKNOWN to mean 'the current inquiry has not established sufficient epistemic standing', distinct from 'nobody knows'; proposes UNKNOWN_TO_US as compatible with KNOWN_BY_SOURCE_A or KNOWN_IN_CONTEXT_B, connecting back to Russell's acquaintance/description distinction and Davidson on interpretation.

b_rows_sample.anchor: CriticalEpistemicDistinctions(S_t) \subseteq Preserved(P_t)
b_rows_sample.statement: Presentation is loss-aware: as a projection it may lose information but must not lose epistemically important distinctions — e.g. Observed/Reported/Inferred/Assumed must not all collapse into 'FACT', and Strong/Weak/No evidence must not all collapse into 'CONFIDENT'. Defines EpistemicFidelity(P_t,S_t) and requires CriticalEpistemicDistinctions(S_t) ⊆ Preserved(P_t) as one of the most important invariants of the presentation architecture.

b_rows_sample.anchor: ConfidenceIndicator = DerivedView(\Sigma)
b_rows_sample.statement: Recommends removing 'Confidence' (Very Strong/Strong/Moderate/Weak/None) as the primary presentation model because it risks collapsing the multidimensional epistemic state established in Q16 (Acquisition ≠ Support ≠ Uncertainty ≠ Validity). A table example shows presenting each claim's Acquisition/Support/Uncertainty/Validity separately; a UI may then derive a simplified indicator: ConfidenceIndicator = DerivedView(Σ), not Confidence = Σ.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Support \neq Probability
b_rows_sample.statement: Extends the earlier Q16 correction (Support ≠ Truth, Support ≠ Resolution) with Support ≠ Probability unless a probabilistic model is explicitly defined — 'Strong evidence' does not mathematically mean P(True)=0.95 unless the system has actually defined that probability semantics.

b_rows_sample.anchor: UncertaintyType \neq UncertaintyMagnitude
b_rows_sample.statement: Uncertainty vocabulary (None/Low/Moderate/High/VeryHigh) is acceptable as a policy vocabulary but not yet a mathematical quantity — the theory has not decided whether uncertainty means lack of information, ambiguity, variance between sources, probability, confidence, or epistemic indeterminacy; flags UncertaintyType ≠ UncertaintyMagnitude as a future question.

b_rows_sample.anchor: StrongSupport \not\Rightarrow Current
b_rows_sample.statement: Validity should be separated into TemporalValidity(A,t) and EpistemicStatus(A): a fact can be strongly supported but temporally expired, so StrongSupport ⇏ Current.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Evidence = (Source,\ Content,\ Relevance,\ Reliability,\ Time,\ Provenance)
b_rows_sample.statement: Evidence needs its own model rather than being just 'E': Evidence = (Source, Content, Relevance, Reliability, Time, Provenance), plus an EvidenceRelation(A,E) since evidence may support, weaken, contradict, qualify, or contextualize an assertion. Establishes Evidence ≠ Support — Support is a relation/assessment between evidence and assertion, called 'a significant missing DDD object'.

b_rows_sample.anchor: HierarchyOfFaculties \neq EpistemicConfidence
b_rows_sample.statement: Chapter 3 (verses 40, 43) orders Senses<Mind<Intelligence<Self as distinct faculties, tempting an 'epistemic ladder' reading; explicitly rejects that reading (reaffirming the earlier rejection of Unknown<Observed<Confirmed<Resolved as a universal ladder): HierarchyOfFaculties ≠ EpistemicConfidence — the text describes different faculties/levels of operation, not better evidence. Abstracts a non-theological CognitiveCapability = {Perception, Interpretation, Reasoning, Judgment, Orientation}, explicitly kept out of Σ_A and placed in the actor/agent model instead.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Knowledge \neq Understanding
b_rows_sample.statement: Called 'perhaps the most important validation of the entire KnowledgeOS concept': a person can act on FalseInterpretation while possessing many correct facts (Arjuna's opening situation), giving Knowledge ≠ Understanding and CorrectFacts ⇏ CorrectDecision. Formally defines Understanding U=(ConceptualModel,Relations,Implications,NormativeMeaning,DecisionConsequences,Uncertainty): Knowledge = 'what is represented', Understanding = 'what does it mean, imply and require in this context'.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Understanding = Interpretation of relationships among known propositions in context
b_rows_sample.statement: Confirms K≠U (Knowledge ≠ Understanding, validated by Arjuna's opening bewilderment despite already having heard distinctions) but corrects the previous U=(ConceptualModel,Relations,Implications,NormativeMeaning,DecisionConsequences,Uncertainty) tuple as too implementation-oriented; redefines Understanding as 'interpretation of relationships among known propositions in context', from which implications, consequences, applicability and normative significance are derived facets.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Gītā hierarchy \neq KnowledgeOS epistemic hierarchy
b_rows_sample.statement: Names 'perhaps the most important correction': the Senses<Mind<Intelligence<Self hierarchy (verses 40,43) is a metaphysical faculty hierarchy from the source, not evidence for an Observation<Interpretation<Reasoning<Truth epistemic-confidence ladder — that would be 'our invention, not the text'. Similarly the smoke/dust/embryo covering analogy should not become a software confidence scale; the only legitimate architectural extraction is 'AccessToKnowledgeCanBeObscuredToDifferentDegrees', with the exact ontology left to the source's own philosophical model.

b_rows_sample.anchor:
Information 
eq Evidence 
eq Belief 
eq Knowledge 
eq Understanding
b_rows_sample.statement: Endorses the book's knowledge/understanding distinction (understanding requires coherent explanatory grasp) and extends the research lattice to a five-term chain Information ≠ Evidence ≠ Belief ≠ Knowledge ≠ Understanding, explicitly flagged as 'a research distinction, not yet a Core object model'. Evaluates the book summary's proposed relation set (observes, measures, knows, understands, complements, constitutes, limits) one by one, rejecting 'constitutes(measurement,knowledge)' as too theory-laden to become a Kernel relation until measurement is shown universally necessary.

b_rows_sample.anchor: U_{sem}\neq U_{epi}\neq U_{dom}
b_rows_sample.statement: Rejects InterpretationConfidence=EpistemicSupport (an LLM can be extremely confident in an incorrect interpretation) and introduces three distinct uncertainties: Semantic uncertainty U_sem (what does the source mean?), Epistemic uncertainty U_epi (how well supported is the proposition?), Domain uncertainty U_dom (what is actually true in the domain?) — U_sem≠U_epi≠U_dom, 'a significant strengthening of our earlier four-dimensional epistemic model'. Also states Ambiguity ≠ Error: multiple candidate meanings (e.g. 'Nexus is running' as OperationalStatus/Process/NexusService running) should be preserved until context resolves them — ambiguity is itself a valid epistemic state.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Unknown ... Hypothesized ... Reported ... WeaklySupported ... ModeratelySupported ... StronglySupported ... Confirmed ... Conflicting ... Stale ... Invalidated ... Absent
b_rows_sample.statement: Expands the epistemic state space Σ into an eleven-value enumeration with worked examples: Unknown (dimension exists, value unknown), Hypothesized (candidate proposed, unevaluated), Reported (source reported, unverified), WeaklySupported, ModeratelySupported, StronglySupported, Confirmed (verified via multiple independent sources), Conflicting (multiple sources disagree), Stale (once known, may no longer be current), Invalidated (believed then disproven), Absent (determined not to exist). Defines the Admission Boundary formally: Admit:CandidateAssertion×Evidence×Rules×Context->Assertion, explicitly NOT requiring StronglySupported, Confirmed, or Truth — 'admission means this proposition is now part of the Knowledge State, with an explicit epistemic status', a much lower and more defensible boundary than a truth-threshold.

type_signature.domain: candidate assertion x evidence x rules x context

b_rows_sample.anchor: Support = f(E,\Pi,C,\mathcal R)
b_rows_sample.statement: Rejects Support=|E| (evidence count) since evidence differs in relevance, reliability, independence, freshness, provenance, directness, context: Support=f(E,Π,C,R). Requires an explicit evidence-dependency graph to detect non-independent evidence — e.g. if Document->LLM (the LLM derived its answer from the document), the LLM's output is not independent evidence even though it appears as a fourth source alongside DB/Monitoring/Document — 'evidence independence must be explicitly modelled', flagged as important for Zero.

Evidence ≠ EvidenceQuality: even a poor-quality observation-proposition pair can be an evidence relation; quality is evaluated separately as a 7-dimensional vector Q_E=(Reliability,Relevance,Directness,Independence,Freshness,Reproducibility,ProvenanceQuality) rather than a single confidence number — 'much more faithful than confidence=0.87'. EvidenceType≠EvidenceStrength (a direct measurement can be wrong; a mathematical derivation can be extremely strong; an official document can be stale), and EvidenceQuality=f(E,P,C,R) since e.g. a direct runtime observation may dominate for 'what is running now?' while an official architecture document may dominate for 'what was officially approved?' — no universal ranking exists.

b_rows_sample.anchor: E_1 \succeq_{P,C,R} E_2
b_rows_sample.statement: Rejects a universal total ordering E_1>E_2 in favor of a partial comparison E_1≽_{P,C,R}E_2 ('under proposition P, context C and rule R, E_1 is at least as suitable as E_2'), since evidence can be genuinely incomparable (e.g. a direct runtime measurement vs an official governance decision). Evidence quality vectors are compared via a policy ComparisonRule(P,C)->Ordering rather than collapsed to a scalar average (e.g. Q(E_1)=(0.95,0.98,1.0,...) is NOT reduced to Q(E)=0.94) — different policies weight different dimensions (directness/freshness for runtime state; authority/provenance for governance compliance).

type_signature.domain: evidence pairs x proposition x context x rule

b_rows_sample.anchor: Reliability(E) = f(Source, ObservationMethod, Environment, Configuration, Context, Provenance)
b_rows_sample.statement: Corrects Reliability from a property of the source alone to Reliability=f(Source,ObservationMethod,Environment,Configuration,Context,Provenance): even an 'official Nexus database' can produce an unreliable observation if queried against the wrong environment, a stale replica, or a broken synchronization. Corrects Completeness similarly to be proposition-relative — Completeness(E,P,C,ρ), not Completeness(E) — since a version field alone may be complete for 'what is the version?' but radically incomplete for 'is Nexus ready for migration?'.

b_aliases: separate dimensions, not one combinatorial state machine

group_evidence.why_grouped: labels co-occur in the same contribution's labels[] 2 separate times across the corpus

a_rows_sample.anchor: External theories are not candidates for the KnowledgeOS Kernel. They are mathematical regimes that may model particular aspects of a KnowledgeOS state.
a_rows_sample.statement: States the governing hierarchy for all external-theory comparisons: external theories are candidate regimes over aspects of a KnowledgeOS state, never candidates for the Kernel itself; endorses DEL's own conclusion (DEL not-cong K_t; DEL is not a foundation for Sigma; DEL may model particular epistemic regimes over parts of K_t) as fully consistent with this hierarchy and with independently-reached Dretske/probability/information-theory/revision-theory conclusions.

a_rows_sample.anchor: K_t should not be identified with a Kripke model or possible-world set. Status: research conclusion / compatibility constraint, not yet kernel theorem.
a_rows_sample.statement: Confirms the DEL document's rejection of K_t as a Kripke pointed model (M,w) strengthens (without proving) the corpus's independently-developed atomic-tuple direction k_i=(O,d_i,v_i,t,E_i,C_i,p_i,q_i); explicitly records the possible-worlds rejection as a research conclusion/compatibility constraint, not a kernel theorem.

a_rows_sample.anchor: DEL is a theory of epistemic state transition. Dretske is much closer to a theory of information acquisition. Those are complementary research regimes.
a_rows_sample.statement: Distinguishes DEL (models Epistemic-State -> [event] -> Epistemic-State', i.e. epistemic state transition) from Dretske (models information acquisition, World->Observation->Channel->Signal->Information->Determination->K_t) as complementary rather than competing regimes, strengthening the chain Observation->Signal/Evidence->Information->Inference/Determination->K_t with probability appearing inside epistemic evaluation rather than defining knowledge.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Candidate structural correspondence: Q_t and A_i can occupy analogous gating roles over a proposition carrier, but semantic equivalence has not been demonstrated.
a_rows_sample.statement: Disputes and downgrades the DEL document's claimed EXACT correspondence Q_t cong A_i to a weaker 'candidate structural correspondence': Q_t (things asked) and A_i (things the agent is aware of) are not semantically identical, since a proposition can be asked-but-not-understood, known-but-never-explicitly-asked, aware-of-but-not-queried, queried-and-forgotten, or queried-but-outside-awareness; an isomorphism may exist between their underlying carrier sets in a deliberately constructed representation, but that is weaker than concept-level equivalence.

a_rows_sample.anchor: KnowledgeOS cannot simply interpret conflict as ordinary logical inconsistency of K. Conflict belongs at a different layer.
a_rows_sample.statement: Reinforces the DEL document's Conflict-vs-D-axiom incompatibility with a concrete illustration: Evidence_1 supporting phi and Evidence_2 refuting phi can coexist as Sigma=(1,1) Conflict without requiring the logically impossible K-phi AND K-not-phi, since Conflict is an evidentiary/status-layer phenomenon rather than an ordinary modal-logic inconsistency -- called 'a much healthier model.'

a_rows_sample.anchor: KnowledgeOS state != deductive closure ... KnowledgeOS must distinguish stored/asserted knowledge from consequences that could be derived.
a_rows_sample.statement: Endorses the logical-omniscience mismatch (A != Cn(A), measured Cn(.)=0) as support for a design principle: KnowledgeOS must keep stored/asserted knowledge distinct from derivable consequences, and further distinct from determined knowledge, awareness, information, and evidence -- none of these may be collapsed into each other.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Truth(pre(e)) != Authorized(e). ... KnowledgeOS Kernel != Governance.
a_rows_sample.statement: Confirms governance (LLM proposes -> Lord evaluates -> Governance authorizes -> Executor acts) sits entirely outside DEL's semantics, since a DEL event precondition is a truth condition, not a permission condition; states this as Truth(pre(e)) != Authorized(e) and Epistemic-Update != Governance-Authorization, reinforcing the architectural separation KnowledgeOS-Kernel != Governance.

a_rows_sample.anchor: The claim that product update "only ever restricts W" is technically too crude. ... KnowledgeOS Revision != standard DEL product update because KnowledgeOS revision includes EventAddition + StateReDerivation and explicitly allows correction, retraction, refutation, reinterpretation, model revision.
a_rows_sample.statement: Corrects the DEL document's falsifier for its Revision hypothesis (DEL-H5): a DEL product update creates worlds of form (w,e) subject to the event precondition, which is not literally a pure restriction W' subset-of W in the same carrier (only public announcement is close to pure restriction); proposes keeping the conclusion (KnowledgeOS Revision != standard DEL product update) but grounding it instead in a semantic mismatch between DEL update and KnowledgeOS's richer revision repertoire (retraction, correction, reinterpretation, model revision).

a_rows_sample.anchor: Dretske/information theory: How does information get from observation to an epistemic state? ... Probability/statistics: How uncertain is an epistemic claim? ... Dynamic Epistemic Logic: How does an epistemic state change under epistemic events? ... Decision theory: Given K_t, what should we do? ...
a_rows_sample.statement: Assigns each of five external theories a distinct, non-overlapping explanatory job within the research stack (Dretske/information theory: acquisition; Probability/statistics: uncertainty, with P!=Knowledge; DEL: epistemic-state transition under events; Decision theory: action selection given K_t, a*=argmax_a EU(a|K_t); Belief revision: state change under new/conflicting information), organized around a central Knowledge State K_t layer with Zero/Decision/Revision below it and Governance kept as an explicitly separate authorization layer outside the mathematical stack.

a_rows_sample.anchor: External theories are candidate regimes over aspects of KnowledgeOS, not candidates for the KnowledgeOS Kernel itself. ... I would be careful with the word substrate. It risks creating the impression that we have already established what the substrate is. We have not.
a_rows_sample.statement: Proposes correcting a referenced '00' document's wording ('these are regimes over a substrate, not the substrate') because 'substrate' risks implying the KnowledgeOS Kernel is already known, when it remains an open research problem (candidate minimal kernels like {Observe, Discriminate, Qualify, Transform, ...} are still under investigation); restates the principle as 'external theories are candidate regimes over aspects of KnowledgeOS, not candidates for the Kernel itself.'

a_rows_sample.anchor: Observation != Evidence; Evidence != Information; Information != Probability; Probability != Determination; Determination != Knowledge; Knowledge != Ideal State; Knowledge != Truth; Decision != Action; Proposal != Decision; Epistemic Update != Governance Authorization.
a_rows_sample.statement: Compiles a ten-item non-collapse chain as the biggest conceptual gain of the comparison, drawn from several independent directions (DEL, Dretske, the corpus's own governance model): Observation!=Evidence!=Information!=Probability!=Determination!=Knowledge!=IdealState!=Truth, plus Decision!=Action, Proposal!=Decision, and EpistemicUpdate!=GovernanceAuthorization; reaffirms K_t as 'a structured, time-indexed epistemic state', not a possible-world model.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Q_t cong 𝒜_i (the awareness set) ... Two frameworks, independently, reached the same repair for the same defect
b_rows_sample.statement: The single exact correspondence found: KnowledgeOS's Q_t (subset of asked propositions) and Fagin-Halpern's awareness set A_i(w) (subset of propositions the agent is aware of) are both subsets of the proposition space gating what can be explicitly held, neither truth-apt, with identity maps between them in both directions; notes the corpus's own Fagin extraction called Chapter 9's awareness treatment 'extremely valuable' on 2026-08-25, before Q_t existed (Step 281, 2026-08-30) -- offered as the strongest structural evidence that the correspondence is real, since two independently-developed frameworks reached the same repair for the same defect.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Sigma(phi)=(1,0) not-implies phi. Therefore Sigma cannot be read as K_i. ... contradicts a boxed corpus result.
b_rows_sample.statement: Decisive incompatibility: DEL's S5/T semantics impose veridicality (K_i-phi implies phi), but the corpus's Closure-03 result 'Admission is not a truth function' means an admitted/supported assertion can be false and must be retained precisely to explain how it came to be wrong; therefore mapping the corpus's Supported/Refuted status pair Sigma onto the knowledge operator K_i imports veridicality and contradicts a boxed corpus result -- the weaker KD45 (belief, no T) avoids this but fails on a separate ground (Conflict/D).

b_rows_sample.anchor: Conflict is a well-formed KnowledgeOS state and an inconsistency in every normal epistemic logic with D.
b_rows_sample.statement: Decisive incompatibility: under axiom D (present in both KD45 and S5), K_i-phi AND K_i-not-phi is unsatisfiable, but the corpus treats Sigma=(1,1) Conflict as a normal, persistent state with no rule forcing its resolution; hosting Conflict therefore requires dropping axiom D entirely, i.e. moving to a paraconsistent or non-adjunctive epistemic logic, which is a different framework from DEL.

b_rows_sample.anchor: V is total: every proposition has a truth value at every world. So DEL can express ignorance but cannot distinguish M1 not-asked / M2 asked-absent / M3 asked-insufficient. All three collapse. This is exactly Critical Failure #7.
b_rows_sample.statement: Sharpens the corpus's own prior 'pi problem' critique of DEL: because DEL's valuation V is total, the framework can express bare ignorance (not-K-phi and not-K-not-phi) but cannot distinguish 'not asked', 'asked and absent', and 'asked and insufficient' -- exactly the corpus's Critical Failure #7 empirically found at Step 280; notes both frameworks fix this the same way (KnowledgeOS via Q_t, DEL via the awareness set A_i).

b_rows_sample.anchor: K_i is closed under consequence. Measured: Cn(.) = 0 occurrences in both lanes. A is a set of asserted items, not a theory. ... A is a belief base, not a belief set.
b_rows_sample.statement: Logical omniscience (DEL's K_i is closed under valid consequence) is incompatible with the corpus's unclosed assertion set: measured zero occurrences of a consequence-closure operator Cn(.) in the corpus, so the corpus's assertion set A is a belief base (a set of individually asserted items) rather than a belief set (closed under entailment) -- a structural carrier-level mismatch prior to any consideration of dynamics.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Admission is governed -- LLM proposes; Lord evaluates; Governance authorizes. DEL has no place to attach an authority predicate to an update.
b_rows_sample.statement: Notes DEL's accessibility relation ~i is fixed by the model with nothing gating what an agent may come to know, while the corpus's admission process is explicitly governed (LLM proposes, Lord evaluates, Governance authorizes); DEL's pre(e) is a truth condition, not a permission condition, so DEL has no primitive for attaching authority/permission to an epistemic update -- listed as a missing primitive DEL would need to host KnowledgeOS.

b_rows_sample.anchor: provenance on events | an authority/permission predicate on updates | evidence as a relation | a non-adjunctive or paraconsistent K | a goal state | partial valuation
b_rows_sample.statement: Lists six primitives DEL would need to add to host KnowledgeOS (event provenance -- source/method/time; an authority/permission predicate on updates; evidence as an explicit relation Evidence(O,P,C,R); a non-adjunctive/paraconsistent knowledge operator to host Conflict; a goal/Ideal-State construct; partial valuation to avoid the pi problem without bolting on awareness), and four primitives KnowledgeOS would need to host DEL (a world set W -- explicitly declined by the corpus; an accessibility relation -- 0 occurrences in the canon; a total valuation V -- contradicted by Unknown as a first-class value; multi-agent indexing -- the Knower space N is listed as an undefined symbol in the TG-register).

b_rows_sample.anchor: DEL-H1 ... DEL-H2 ... DEL-H3 ... DEL-H4 ... DEL-H5
b_rows_sample.statement: States five falsifiable hypotheses with named falsifiers: DEL-H1 (Q_t cong A_i is an exact isomorphism, falsified by a non-representable Q_t state or an unreconstructible awareness structure); DEL-H2 (no sound embedding of Sigma into any normal modal logic with D preserves Conflict as satisfiable, falsified by exhibiting one); DEL-H3 (the corpus's M1/M2/M3 missingness distinction under Q_t is exactly the explicit/implicit-knowledge distinction, falsified by a fourth Q_t-distinction with no awareness counterpart); DEL-H4 (adopting S5 for Sigma would falsify a boxed corpus result, trivially checkable); DEL-H5 (the corpus's Revision = EventAddition + StateReDerivation is not DEL's product update, since product update only ever restricts W, falsified by exhibiting a RevisionType that is a pure restriction).

b_rows_sample.anchor: PARTIALLY COMPATIBLE — as a regime over Q_t, not as a foundation for Sigma ... This sharpens it: the regime it can support is awareness, and the part it cannot support is Sigma.
b_rows_sample.statement: Final verdict: DEL is partially compatible with KnowledgeOS -- exact and compatible at one point (Q_t cong A_i, independently converged upon), incompatible at the centre (Sigma is not K_i because of veridicality, and Conflict is an inconsistency under D), and carrier-mismatched (belief base vs belief set); explicitly reconciled with, and sharpening, the corpus's own 2026-08-25 position that DEL may be 'a reasoning regime KnowledgeOS may support; not the Kernel' -- the supportable regime is specifically awareness, not Sigma.

a_notations: External theories are candidate regimes over aspects of KnowledgeOS, not candidates for the Kernel itself

group_evidence.why_grouped: explicit agent-stated uncertainty: 'del-review-and-correction-against-separation-rule' POSSIBLY relates to 'del-theory-compatibility-analysis' (batch B0056). Note: A critical second-pass review of the '01 Dynamic Epistemic Logic' theory-compatibility document (this batch's del-theory-compatibility-analysis) against an unread-in-this-batch '00 Method, Provenance, and the Separation Rule' document and the K_t/Dretske research line: endorses most of 01's findings (K_t is not a Kripke possible-world model; Evidence/Determination have no DEL counterpart; Ideal State is neither Truth nor the actual world; Zero is richer than DEL ignorance; Sigma!=K_i; Conflict is incompatible with normal K under D; logical omniscience mismatches the corpus's non-deductively-closed assertion set; governance authorization is a different semantic category from a DEL event's truth-valued precondition) but explicitly DOWNGRADES 01's claimed EXACT correspondence Q_t cong A_i to a weaker 'candidate structural correspondence' (Q_t and A_i can occupy analogous gating roles but are not semantically identical: a proposition can be asked-but-not-understood, known-but-never-asked, aware-of-but-not-queried, queried-and-forgotten, or queried-but-outside-awareness), and separately argues 01's falsifier for DEL-H5 ('product update only ever restricts W') is technically too crude, proposing a stronger semantic-mismatch argument based on KnowledgeOS revision's retraction/correction/reinterpretation/model-revision repertoire instead. Assigns each external theory a distinct non-overlapping job (Dretske/information theory: how information gets from observation to an epistemic state; Probability/statistics: how uncertain a claim is; DEL: how an epistemic state changes under epistemic events; Decision theory: what to do given K_t; Belief revision: how a state changes under new/conflicting information), concluding 'External theories are candidate regimes over aspects of KnowledgeOS, not candidates for the Kernel itself' -- explicitly cautioning against the word 'substrate' implying the Kernel is already known -- and compiling a ten-item non-collapse chain (Observation!=Evidence!=Information!=Probability!=Determination!=Knowledge!=IdealState!=Truth; Decision!=Action; Proposal!=Decision; EpistemicUpdate!=GovernanceAuthorization).

b_rows_sample.statement: EXP-3: two structurally identical states (K(H_calm), K(H_stormy)) are indistinguishable under K=(A,R) for a minimal/full operation set as coded, but become distinguishable once a plausible history-sensitive predicate (ever_contested) is added; therefore 'K=(A,R) is the minimal sufficient state' is not a theorem of the corpus but a consequence of an unstated choice of the operation set O. [Note: the second-order investigation (S1754/S1756) later argues ever_contested is a class-4 audit/history operation the corpus's own taxonomy excludes from this congruence test, correcting this experiment's inference though not its arithmetic.]

b_rows_sample.anchor:
> *"Zero is computable, total and terminating over finite R, **RELATIVE to per-requirement
> evaluators**.
b_rows_sample.statement: Computational closure is assessed CONDITIONALLY CLOSED: everything executed and computable (membership, equality, StructuralValid, contradiction detection, supersession, replay, lineage, Zero — 8/8 tests) is computable only relative to per-requirement evaluators (Γ semantics, HumanAuthorization oracles) that are themselves not established; the theory is computable down to its oracles, and the oracles are where the epistemics live.

b_rows_sample.anchor: G-01 as stated in the first-order pass is wrong in its premise and wrong in its inference.
b_rows_sample.statement: Corrects the first-order claim that O is never enumerated: Step 256 s256.2 enumerates nine operations and Step 259 s259.7 adds six more, for 15 named operations; and the '≡ is unconstructed' claim is not independent -- Step 259 s259.18 states the ∀T∈T-incompleteness problem verbatim, and Step 254 already writes Minimality(K|T).

b_rows_sample.anchor: K* = the coarsest abstraction congruent for T_class-1 and expressive for I_mandatory
b_rows_sample.statement: Recommended (not fact) formulation of the canonical Knowledge State: K* = the coarsest abstraction congruent for the class-1 transformation set T_class-1 and expressive for the mandatory invariant set I_mandatory, both declared per deployment -- consistent with s254's Minimality(K|T) and s259.15-16's Congruent_tested (never Congruent_global).

b_rows_sample.anchor: G-54 | Split has no semantic-preservation invariant (256.10 states the requirement and supplies none) | 1 ... G-55 ... G-56 ... G-57 ... G-58
b_rows_sample.statement: Five new gaps added by the second-order pass: G-54 (Split has no semantic-preservation invariant, s256.10), G-55 (merge-provenance invariant s265.11 not expressible in terminal A), G-56 (congruence necessary but not sufficient; invariant-expressibility is an uncomposed second criterion), G-57 (humanAct/humanActRef untyped prose, 79 strings/0 typed objects), G-58 (Determination lost in DDD->formalization band transition, unrecorded, third instance of this failure mode).

b_rows_sample.statement: All five remaining CRITICAL theoretical holes (G-06 Sigma>=5 axes, G-25 Unknown homeless, G-27 Insufficient missing, G-11 evidence layer no inputs, G-12 no empirical relational structure) converge on the single object Sigma, matching the corpus's own Step 271 s271.35 marking Sigma RED and s271.36 commissioning the non-existent Step 272 to derive it.

b_rows_sample.statement: Full classification of all 17 corpus-named operations per s259.7's five-class scheme: Class 1 state transformation (Add, Remove, Revise, Transform, Supersede, Merge, Split, Reject, Withdraw, Promote, Reintroduce), Class 2 epistemic assessment (Validate, Assess), Class 3 governance (Authorize), Class 4 audit/history (Replay, EverContested, RevisionCount); Class 5 observation has no named member.

IE-4 | '≡ is unconstructed.' | Overstated. ... ON-1 | 'the dependency graph is cyclic.' | True as drawn, but ... G-31 | 'the aggregate boundary is never fixed.'
b_rows_sample.statement: Five further first-order findings corrected rather than withdrawn: G-01's premise (O is enumerated, 15 named ops), the KG-4/EXP-3 inference (invalid per class-4/class-1 distinction), IE-4 (≡ IS constructible relative to T, overstated as unconstructed), ON-1 (graph is acyclic once the Authority->Assertion edge is removed per implementation evidence), and G-31 (the Knowledge/Determination/Decision aggregate boundary IS fixed at s157/165/173, s173.5 calling their merge 'another dangerous merge').

b_rows_sample.anchor: |O_forced| = 14 ... forced-but-unnamed (new): ['Derive', 'Determine', 'Qualify'] ... |lower| = 14  |upper| = 18  |undetermined band| = 4
b_rows_sample.statement: Raw execution output validating oderive.py's reported 14-element forced lower bound, the finding that Derive/Determine/Qualify are forced-but-unnamed in the corpus's own registries, and the 14/18/4 lower/upper/undetermined-band split.

b_rows_sample.anchor: My independent/14-INDEPENDENT-VERDICT.md stated: 'Step 272 does not exist… the theory was interrupted.' That was true at 21:19 and is now false. The corpus contains # step 272 … whose body is STEP 273
b_rows_sample.statement: This session's own prior verdict ('Step 272 does not exist') is explicitly superseded: the corpus now contains a file headed '# step 272' whose body is actually Step 273 (Canonical Knowledge-State Sufficiency and Minimality), including a s273.31 'Important correction to Step 272' -- the research track had resumed and run ahead of every verification track.

b_rows_sample.anchor: An operation o is MANDATORY iff removing o makes some corpus-stated non-collapse law INEXPRESSIBLE ... This is a derivation, not a preference: the laws are corpus text, the forcing relation is entailment
b_rows_sample.statement: States and applies the derivation principle for operation mandatoriness: an operation is mandatory iff its removal makes some corpus-stated non-collapse law (e.g. 'Remove != Withdraw', 'Determination != Decision') inexpressible; encodes 26 such laws (with repetition-count weights as evidence weight, e.g. 'Expression != Meaning' at 71) and a table of which operation(s) each law forces, e.g. 'Determination != Decision' (weight 19) forces Determine, 'Observation != Evidence' (weight 20) forces Qualify.

b_rows_sample.anchor: 'Transform', 'Merge', 'Split' are named in 256.2 and forced by NO law. ... 'Qualify' and 'Determine' ARE forced ... but appear in NEITHER 256.2 NOR 259.7. The corpus's own enumeration MISSES two operations its own laws force.
b_rows_sample.statement: Result: Transform, Merge, Split and Reintroduce are named in the corpus's own registry (s256.2/s259.7) but forced by no non-collapse law (their necessity is asserted, not entailed); conversely Qualify, Determine and Derive are forced by laws with weights 20/19/18 respectively but appear in NEITHER s256.2 nor s259.7 -- so the laws under-determine O in one direction and the corpus's own enumeration over/under-determines it in the other, making set-membership not derivable from the laws alone.

b_rows_sample.anchor: FALSE AS STATED · TRUE IN SUBSTANCE · AND THE SUBSTANCE IS SHARPER THAN EITHER. ... So the missing premise is not the ENUMERATION. It is the NORMATIVE CLOSURE -- which of the candidates are mandatory.
b_rows_sample.statement: Tests and refines the claim 'O was never explicitly defined': FALSE as stated (s256.2 enumerates 9 ops in a boxed formula, s259.7 adds Validate/Assess/Promote/Reintroduce/Replay plus a five-class partition) but TRUE in substance (s256.2 itself calls its table 'a reconstruction target, not a claim that all nine are already formally defined', and s259.18 states the ∀T∈T-incompleteness problem as its own boxed negative result, so this was never an independent discovery by any verification track) -- the missing premise is normative closure (which candidates are mandatory), not enumeration.

b_rows_sample.anchor: non-collapse laws extracted (distinct) : 26 ... operations FORCED : 14 ... Two STRUCTURES are forced as a by-product, and neither is an operation: <D_t> ... <serialize>
b_rows_sample.statement: Derivation principle (o is mandatory iff removing it makes some corpus-stated non-collapse law inexpressible) applied to 26 distinct measured non-collapse laws: 14 operations forced (Authorize weight 45; Revise/Supersede 41; Promote 26; Qualify 20; Add 19; Determine 19; Derive 18; Replay 12; Assess/Validate 11; Remove/Withdraw/Reject weight 1 each), plus two non-operation structures forced as a by-product: <D_t> (recognised-dimension set, forced by UNKNOWN != ABSENT) and <serialize> (canonical form, forced by Expression != Meaning, the corpus's most-repeated law at 71 occurrences).

b_rows_sample.anchor: Qualify, Determine, Derive are entailed by laws the corpus repeats 20, 19 and 18 times respectively -- and appear in neither §256.2 nor §259.7. ... Transform, Merge, Split, Reintroduce. The corpus never writes 'Merge != X', so nothing entails that Merge must exist.
b_rows_sample.statement: Two-sided mismatch between the derived forced set and the corpus's own named registry: Qualify, Determine, Derive are forced by frequently-repeated laws (20/19/18 occurrences) yet appear in NEITHER s256.2 nor s259.7 (a G5 promotion gap, not a G1 semantic gap); conversely Transform, Merge, Split, Reintroduce are named in the registry but forced by no non-collapse law (their necessity asserted, not entailed -- Transform's high usage, 8 of 9 kernel phases, is evidence of centrality, not mandatoriness).

b_rows_sample.anchor: |lower bound (forced)| = 14        |upper bound (named ∪ forced)| = 18 ... NOT derivable: which of the 4 band members are mandatory -- NORMATIVE -> D-1
b_rows_sample.statement: O is bounded but not determined: a 14-element lower bound and an 18-element upper bound are both derivable with no human input, along with the five-class partition and congruence rule (independently re-derivable since congruence is a property of an algebra's operations on its carrier, so an operation reading H is not an operation on K); only membership of the 4-operation undetermined band in the mandatory set is not derivable, because 'mandatory' is a normative predicate that no corpus of descriptions can entail -- this is D-1.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Linus did not start by designing 'the operating system of the world.' He started by solving a concrete problem, created a small working kernel ... 'Can we create a trusted kernel that allows digitalization robots to operate safely?'
a_rows_sample.statement: Argues KnowledgeOS should not start with an AI-driven Digitalization Robot ambition; the correct starting question is the smallest trusted kernel that later allows robots to operate safely, mirroring Linux's incremental 0.01-kernel-first history.

a_rows_sample.anchor: the robot is not the core domain. The robot is a consumer and operator of governed knowledge.
a_rows_sample.statement: States the constitutional boundary for the proposed Digitalization Robot: it consumes and operates on governed knowledge, but never becomes the core domain or an independent authority source.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Mode 1: Advisor ... Mode 2: Developer Assistant ... Mode 3: Controlled Executor ... Mode 4: Autonomous Operator
a_rows_sample.statement: Defines four graduated robot authority modes with increasing execution permission (from recommend-only to fully autonomous in limited domains), explicitly refusing to assume the robot always executes.

a_rows_sample.anchor: skill: name: Create REST API requires: [...] produces: [...] evidence: required
a_rows_sample.statement: Proposes a governed 'Robot Skill Catalog' where each skill declares its required inputs, produced artifacts, and mandatory evidence, and that the Composition Root injects interchangeable tool adapters (e.g. Kubernetes vs AWS vs Azure) behind each skill.

a_rows_sample.anchor: The robot does not only produce software. It increases the intelligence of the organization.
a_rows_sample.statement: Argues the strategic differentiator versus current AI coding agents is a closing feedback loop: the robot's work produces new organizational knowledge (an evidence package) that KnowledgeOS stores, rather than terminating at code output.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Kernel scope: 'minimal kernel, no AI' (S0167) vs the platform vision where an AI-driven Digitalization Robot is the top layer (S0171) — the corpus itself frames the robot as a distribution, keeping the kernel AI-free, so the tension is scope of the 'core' vs the 'product'.
a_rows_sample.statement: Surfaces T1: a minimal AI-free kernel proposal versus an AI-driven robot as the platform's top execution layer, resolved by the corpus's own framing (robot = distribution, kernel stays AI-free) but not formally decided.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Command → Application Boundary → Aggregate → Domain Rule → Domain Event ... no actor may 'Change Governance.' directly.
a_rows_sample.statement: Records the proposed governed command loop as the integration spine any actor (human, AI agent, or the Digitalization Robot) must issue commands through, with outcomes surfacing only as domain events, never a direct write to Governance.

a_rows_sample.anchor: The Kernel can become the part of the future brain that guarantees that whatever the brain claims to know has an accountable, identifiable, justified and historically preserved epistemic state. ... The possibility of becoming part of a future computer brain must never be used to enlarge the present Kernel boundary. Build the smallest correct epistemic core now.
a_rows_sample.statement: Proposes a future-facing hypothesis that today's narrow KnowledgeOS Core could become the epistemic-integrity substrate of a much larger future cognitive system (perception/interpretation/reasoning/planning/action wrapped around it), while explicitly constraining that this future possibility must never be used to enlarge the present Kernel boundary -- the smallest correct epistemic core must be built now, regardless of future ambition.

b_rows_sample.anchor: The kernel creates the ecosystem; the company creates value around the ecosystem.
b_rows_sample.statement: Uses the Linux/Red Hat precedent to argue KnowledgeOS's moat is the kernel plus governance plus evidence model (not the AI model, which is commoditized), proposing a Community/Professional/Enterprise revenue-tier structure and a 10-year IPO roadmap.

b_rows_sample.anchor: KnowledgeOS Kernel = the minimal system responsible for creating, identifying, relating, governing, and preserving organizational knowledge objects.
b_rows_sample.statement: The proposed load-bearing definition of the 'KnowledgeOS Kernel', explicitly modeled after the Linux kernel's separation from applications: the kernel provides knowledge primitives (Identity, Lifecycle, Evidence, Authority) and must not know about specific technologies (SAP, Kubernetes, Jira).

b_rows_sample.anchor: Linus did not start by designing 'the operating system of the world.' He started by solving a concrete problem, created a small working kernel ... 'Can we create a trusted kernel that allows digitalization robots to operate safely?'
b_rows_sample.statement: Argues KnowledgeOS should not start with an AI-driven Digitalization Robot ambition; the correct starting question is the smallest trusted kernel that later allows robots to operate safely, mirroring Linux's incremental 0.01-kernel-first history.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Open-source the KnowledgeOS Kernel. Commercialize the Digitalization Robot Platform.
b_rows_sample.statement: Recommends an open-core business model (open KnowledgeOS Kernel for trust/ecosystem, commercial Digitalization Robot/Enterprise Platform for revenue), by analogy with Linux Kernel vs Red Hat Enterprise Linux.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Linux manages computer resources. KnowledgeOS manages organizational intelligence resources ... which knowledge is valid, who owns it, and how can it be trusted?
b_rows_sample.statement: States the deepest claimed difference between the Linux and KnowledgeOS kernel analogies: Linux answers 'which process can access which resource', while KnowledgeOS must answer 'which knowledge is valid, who owns it, and how can it be trusted.'

b_rows_sample.anchor: Rust for the KnowledgeOS Kernel, Kotlin/Spring for the Enterprise Runtime, Python for Intelligence, TypeScript for Experience.
b_rows_sample.statement: Recommends a multi-language technology stack (Rust kernel for memory-safety/correctness, Kotlin+Spring Boot enterprise runtime, Python intelligence layer, TypeScript studio/frontend) with an estimated 12-18 month timeline for a first Kernel v1.0 with a small expert team.

b_rows_sample.anchor: If you want IPO potential, do not position KnowledgeOS as 'AI chatbot' ... nor 'Documentation tool' ... Position as: The operating system for enterprise knowledge and digital transformation.
b_rows_sample.statement: Argues the commercial positioning category determines addressable market size; 'AI chatbot' is too easy to copy, 'documentation tool' is too small a category for IPO ambitions.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Kernel scope: 'minimal kernel, no AI' (S0167) vs the platform vision where an AI-driven Digitalization Robot is the top layer (S0171) — the corpus itself frames the robot as a distribution, keeping the kernel AI-free, so the tension is scope of the 'core' vs the 'product'.
b_rows_sample.statement: Surfaces T1: a minimal AI-free kernel proposal versus an AI-driven robot as the platform's top execution layer, resolved by the corpus's own framing (robot = distribution, kernel stays AI-free) but not formally decided.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Rust · Spring Boot · Gradle/Cargo · microservices · plugin architecture · Event Sourcing · Kafka are recommendations/hypotheses in the corpus, never adopted KnowledgeOS technology.
b_rows_sample.statement: Explicit preservation note keeping every named technology recommendation level-tagged as a hypothesis, never promoted to adopted architecture, while noting the existing PHP/Laravel + TypeScript/Vue platform is the ESTABLISHED current stack.

b_rows_sample.anchor: DI principle vs framework import: adopt the DI/composition-root principle without adopting Spring — the corpus wants the first, but the kernel file pairs the principle with the Spring runtime.
b_rows_sample.statement: Surfaces T4: the DI-principle proposal explicitly wants the principle without the Spring framework, yet the kernel-technology brainstorm pairs the same principle with a recommended Spring/Kotlin runtime.

b_rows_sample.anchor: KNOWLEDGEOS KERNEL protects: identity · evidence · provenance · lifecycle · authority · invariants · temporal state / higher layers provide: assurance · analytics · inference · simulation · AI · visualization · delivery ... a PROPOSED KERNEL BOUNDARY CANDIDATE, outline supported, provenance+temporal weak.
b_rows_sample.statement: H-10: tests the seven-concern kernel/higher-layer split against all three baselines per-concern; identity, evidence, lifecycle, authority, and invariants are supported, provenance and temporal state are weak, so the overall split is a candidate outline, not an established fact.

b_rows_sample.anchor: WHAT IS THE CORE DOMAIN ACT? ... Verification | Admission | Determination | Transformation | Epistemic Maintenance | Justification Preservation | Constitutional Transition
b_rows_sample.statement: Seven alternative formulations of KnowledgeOS's core domain act are compared (Verification, Admission, Determination, Transformation, Epistemic Maintenance, Justification Preservation, Constitutional Transition), each with its domain-meaning implication.

b_rows_sample.anchor: The core domain act is the constitutionally-gated transition from candidate to admissible knowledge state.
b_rows_sample.statement: Hypothesis: the Kernel's core domain act is the constitutionally-gated transition from candidate to admissible knowledge state, combining a candidate, a gate (constitutional rules), a verdict (admissibility), and a state change.

b_rows_sample.anchor: A knowledge claim cannot exist without: identity, evidence, justification, epistemic state, confidence, and history.
b_rows_sample.statement: Proposed aggregate invariant: a knowledge claim cannot exist without identity, evidence, justification, epistemic state, confidence, and history all present and consistent together; the Kernel is framed as 'the guardian of this aggregate invariant.'

b_rows_sample.anchor: Candidate -> Verification -> Admissibility -> Identity -> Epistemic State -> Knowledge
b_rows_sample.statement: Admission is modelled as a distinction chain (Candidate -> Verification[well-formed?] -> Admissibility[constitution?] -> Identity[stable anchor?] -> Epistemic State -> Knowledge) and as an 8-step process from candidate proposal to emission of KnowledgeCreated.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Identity assignment | ESSENTIAL ... Semantic interpretation | NOT ESSENTIAL ... Reasoning | NOT ESSENTIAL ... Workflow | NOT ESSENTIAL ... Projection | NOT ESSENTIAL
b_rows_sample.statement: A capability table classifies identity assignment, evidence admission, justification preservation, epistemic-state determination, confidence assignment, history recording, and constitutional evaluation as ESSENTIAL (each tied to a named invariant); candidate verification as SUPPORTING; and semantic interpretation, reasoning, workflow, and projection as NOT ESSENTIAL to the Kernel's minimum domain capacity.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Natural-language interpretation | Parsing | Normalization | Canonicalization | Reasoning | Candidate generation | Retrieval | Search | Ranking | Model inference | Orchestration | Workflow | Projection | UI | Infrastructure | Evidence acquisition
b_rows_sample.statement: A 15-item table enumerates responsibilities that belong OUTSIDE the Kernel, each with a DDD reason: natural-language interpretation, parsing, normalization, canonicalization, reasoning, candidate generation, retrieval, search, ranking, model inference, orchestration, workflow, projection, UI, infrastructure, and evidence acquisition -- summarized as the principle that the Kernel is representation-agnostic and does not perform semantic interpretation.

b_rows_sample.anchor: The Kernel is a domain boundary, not a component.
b_rows_sample.statement: Six candidate interpretations of what the Kernel 'is' are compared (aggregate boundary, domain decision boundary, admission boundary, consistency boundary, constitutional boundary, small domain core inside the aggregate); concludes the Kernel is best understood as the admission boundary + consistency boundary -- a conceptual domain boundary, not an implementation component, though it may be implemented inside the aggregate.

b_rows_sample.anchor: KnowledgeCreated is the domain event that signals the completion of admission.
b_rows_sample.statement: KnowledgeCreated is analyzed as the domain event signalling completion of admission -- the business moment the candidate becomes part of KnowledgeOS with identity, evidence, justification, epistemic state, confidence, and history all established; the Kernel's job is to produce this event on success and nothing/a rejection on failure.

b_rows_sample.anchor: KnowledgeOS is a governed knowledge-admission system.
b_rows_sample.statement: Four formulations of the knowledge/evidence relationship are compared (evidence registry, justified epistemic-state system, governed knowledge-admission system, constitutional knowledge machine); 'governed knowledge-admission system' is judged best supported -- evidence supports knowledge, knowledge requires evidence, evidence is admitted and preserved alongside knowledge, but evidence is not itself knowledge.

b_rows_sample.anchor: 99.7 — Observability provenance ... Source, Timestamp, Component, Version, CorrelationID where appropriate.
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines observability-provenance fields: Source, Timestamp, Component, Version, CorrelationID.

b_rows_sample.anchor: 99.8 — Experiment 4 ... Two services produce 'approval completed.' No correlation ID exists. Expected: it may be impossible to establish which request the event belongs to. Result: PASS
b_rows_sample.statement: Experiment 4: two identical 'approval completed' events without a correlation ID cannot be attributed to their originating request; result PASS.

b_rows_sample.anchor: 99.9 — Distributed tracing ... A→B→C→D. A trace gives TraceID connecting the causal path.
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines distributed tracing via TraceID connecting a multi-service operation path A→B→C→D.

b_rows_sample.anchor: 99.10 — Experiment 5 ... Request fails in service D. Trace shows A→B→C→D. Expected: the failure can be associated with the original operation. Result: PASS
b_rows_sample.statement: Experiment 5: a trace correctly associates a service-D failure with the original A→B→C→D operation; result PASS.

b_rows_sample.anchor: 99.11 — Trace is not causal proof ... A trace shows ordering A→B→C. It does not automatically establish A causes C. Temporal ordering ≠ Causal explanation.
b_rows_sample.statement: States Temporal ordering ≠ Causal explanation: a trace establishes ordering, not proven causation.

b_rows_sample.anchor: 99.12 — Experiment 6 ... CPU spike occurs before an application failure. Expected: trace establishes temporal relationship, but not necessarily CPUSpike→Failure as proven causation. Result: PASS
b_rows_sample.statement: Experiment 6: a CPU spike preceding a failure establishes temporal order, not proven causation; result PASS.

b_rows_sample.anchor: 99.13 — Metrics ... Latency, ErrorRate, Availability, QueueDepth, VerificationCoverage.
b_rows_sample.statement: Lists example runtime metrics: Latency, ErrorRate, Availability, QueueDepth, VerificationCoverage.

b_rows_sample.anchor: 99.14 — Experiment 7 ... Architecture requires AuthorizationFailureRate<1%. Observed 4%. Expected: operational invariant violation. Result: PASS
b_rows_sample.statement: Experiment 7: an observed 4% authorization failure rate against a required <1% is an operational invariant violation; result PASS.

b_rows_sample.anchor: 99.15 — SLOs ... Availability≥99.9%. SLOs are not necessarily absolute architectural invariants. They are service objectives.
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines SLOs (e.g. Availability≥99.9%) as service objectives, distinct from absolute architectural invariants.

b_rows_sample.anchor: 99.16 — Experiment 8 ... SLO: Availability≥99.9%. Actual: 99.7%. Expected: SLO breach. Not necessarily ArchitectureInvalid. Result: PASS. This distinction matters.
b_rows_sample.statement: Experiment 8: a 99.7% actual availability against a 99.9% SLO is an SLO breach, not necessarily ArchitectureInvalid; result PASS.

b_rows_sample.anchor: 99.17 — Hard invariants versus SLOs ... HardInvariant versus OperationalObjective. UnauthorizedDeployment=False may be a hard invariant. Latency<500ms may be an SLO.
b_rows_sample.statement: Distinguishes HardInvariant (e.g. UnauthorizedDeployment=False) from OperationalObjective/SLO (e.g. Latency<500ms).

b_rows_sample.anchor: 99.18 — Experiment 9 ... Latency reaches 600ms. Security authorization remains correct. Expected: performance objective may fail without implying security failure. Result: PASS
b_rows_sample.statement: Experiment 9: a latency SLO breach (600ms) alongside correct security authorization shows performance failure need not imply security failure; result PASS.

b_rows_sample.anchor: 99.19 — Runtime invariant monitoring ... KnowledgeOS should evaluate predicates I(S_t). UnauthorizedActionCount=0. If UnauthorizedActionCount>0, we have evidence of an invariant violation or attempted violation.
b_rows_sample.statement: Proposes evaluating runtime invariant predicates I(S_t) such as UnauthorizedActionCount=0, with any positive count evidencing a violation or attempt.
