a_rows_sample.anchor: STEP 060 Epistemic Algebra and Knowledge-State Ordering -- claimed partial order's antisymmetry fails via a definitional escape clause and concretely on the source's own carrier objects; transitivity fails because the 'compatibility' conjunct is not transitive. VE-8: 060 section60.16 demotes the already-committed core-algebra ordering symbol (frozen-algebra member since step-032 section32.76-77, PASS-stamped) to 'a candidate ordering' without naming 032, the algebra, or retracting the PASS. VE-11: 'Experiment 4'/'Experiment 5' numbering each occurs twice (section60.28/60.43; section60.29/60.45).
a_rows_sample.statement: Step 060's central claim that KnowledgeOS forms a partial order is re-derived line-by-line and found to fail: antisymmetry is not established (escaped via a definitional clause) and fails concretely on the file's own carrier objects, and transitivity fails because the 'compatibility' conjunct used in the ordering's definition is itself not transitive -- yet section60.70's boxed central finding asserts 'partially ordered' as if derived (VE-7). Separately, the ordering symbol used here silently downgrades an ordering symbol already committed as a member of the frozen core algebra (a step-032 result, PASS-stamped at section32.77) to merely 'a candidate ordering,' without naming step-032, the algebra, or retracting the earlier PASS (VE-8). Two experiment numbers ('Experiment 4', 'Experiment 5') are each independently used twice within the same file (VE-11). This verification independently confirms, and via TV-F-030 (S1508) partially corrects, an earlier subagent's overstated claim that transitivity 'fails' outright to the more precise 'not established.'

a_rows_sample.anchor: STEP 061 Information Gain, Uncertainty and Epistemic Quality -- entropy, Brier score, log-loss, and mutual-information arithmetic all independently verified correct. Documents three separate, unreconciled 'epistemic quality vector' objects (Q(E) 5-tuple section61.18; EQ(C) 7-tuple section61.30; EQC(C) 6-set section61.56) introduced within a single file.
a_rows_sample.statement: Step 061's quantitative claims (entropy, Brier score, log-loss, mutual information) are independently arithmetic-checked and found correct, and the file's discipline of treating epistemic quality as a structured, non-scalar object ('EpistemicQuality is generally a partial order, not necessarily a single number,' section61.39) is judged sound. However the file itself introduces three distinct, unreconciled 'epistemic quality vector' formalizations within its own scope -- Q(E)=(q_r,q_f,q_i,q_d,q_c) at section61.18 (5 components), EQ(C)=(EvidenceStrength,...,Calibration) at section61.30 (7 components), and EQC(C)={Evidence,...,Calibration} at section61.56 (6 components) -- with no stated mapping between them, and does not cite step-034's prior EVPI/EVSI/NVOI value-of-information vocabulary despite using EVPI itself (section61.47).

a_rows_sample.anchor: STEP 062 Decision Theory and the Knowledge-to-Action Boundary -- VE-2 intra-file symbol collision: U=utility in the decision-problem tuple D=(K,A,Theta,U,C,R) at section62.1, U=authorization in the boxed complete chain K->D->U->A->O at section62.68; A=available-action-set vs A=executed-action, both boxed and load-bearing in the same file. Line-number-verified wholesale, uncited re-derivation of content already present in steps 025H, 025R, 041, 042, 034, and 015.
a_rows_sample.statement: Step 062 contains an intra-file symbol collision (VE-2) in which the letter U denotes utility within the decision-problem tuple D=(K,A,Theta,U,C,R) (section62.1) but denotes authorization within the boxed complete decision chain K->D->U->A->O (section62.68), and A likewise shifts between the available-action set and the single executed action -- both usages are boxed and load-bearing within the same file. Separately, the verifier confirms via line-number comparison that Step 062 wholesale re-derives, without citation, content already present at steps 025H, 025R, 041, 042, 034, and 015, including its central 'Decision selection is not equivalent to Authorization' claim (section62.39), which is identical in substance to five other independently-named formulations scattered across three other files in this same band (058's authorization findings, 064's Model performance is not equivalent to Model authorization, and 065's AgentCapability is not equivalent to AgentAuthority).

a_rows_sample.anchor: STEP 063 Causal Reasoning and Intervention -- line-number-verified wholesale, uncited re-derivation of content already present in steps 025P, 043, and 014, including the specific finding that the file's own claim 'we are not adding mathematical concepts randomly' is judged false for this file since its content already existed at those earlier steps.
a_rows_sample.statement: Step 063's causal-reasoning apparatus (NotIdentified as a first-class state, Identifiability != Computability, the ObservedAssociation-to-CausalRelation invariant I_Causal) is verified line-by-line against source to be a wholesale, uncited re-derivation of content already present at steps 025P, 043, and 014. The verifier specifically judges the file's own self-assessment ('we are not adding mathematical concepts randomly') to be false as applied to this file, since the content in question already existed prior to Step 063's composition. The invariant I_Causal minted here (section63.51, 'ObservedAssociation cannot be promoted to CausalRelation without an explicit causal basis') is also shown to be the fourth independent statement of a rule already given by step-058 section58.33 (TemporalOrder does not imply Causality), step-056 Experiment 18, and step-061 Experiment 7 -- only step-063 gives it invariant status.

a_rows_sample.anchor: STEP 064 Model Uncertainty, Distribution Shift and Self-Validation -- DDD VERDICT: STRONG. section64.15 Executable != Validated, section64.29/64.61 Affected != Invalid, section64.34 rejecting an evidence item is not deleting it (Valid->Disputed->Invalidated chain), section64.47-48 HTTP 200 means ComputationExecuted not ModelCorrect, section64.53 Model performance != Model authorization, section64.55 retrain lands in Candidate never Production -- a coherent and genuinely useful MLOps governance layer.
a_rows_sample.statement: Step 064 is judged to deliver a coherent and genuinely useful MLOps governance layer for KnowledgeOS: a model-status lifecycle distinguishing execution from validation, an evidence-rejection status chain (Valid -> Disputed -> Invalidated) that preserves rather than deletes rejected evidence, a distinction between successful computation (HTTP 200 / ComputationExecuted) and model correctness, and a rule that model performance does not confer authorization (explicitly analogized by the source to Decision != Authorization), plus a governance rule that retrained models land in a Candidate state and never directly in Production.

b_rows_sample.anchor: each file's tail contains the agenda for the next step
b_rows_sample.statement: Structural observation, load-bearing for the whole verification: each file in the 208-215 band ends with the agenda section for the *next* step (e.g. the file titled 'Step 208' ends with a '# Step 209' section at line 1423 onward), so the band is a chain of overlapping documents and every 'Step N' agenda exists in two places (as the prior file's tail and the next file's own opening).

b_rows_sample.anchor: Prior-family acknowledgement in Step 209: NONE. ZERO.
b_rows_sample.statement: Probe (c-i): machine grep of Step 209 for the corpus's prior invariant-naming families (INV-n, AFR-0n, GT-0n, GG-/GE-/GC-/GA-, IR-0n, CM-0n, LA-0n, AAI, PLP, and bare C1-C7/S1-S6/K1-K7/V1-V10/I1-I20) finds zero matches of any kind; Step 209 cites exactly one prior step (Step 208, in its opening line) and nothing else. The prior families are independently confirmed present and locatable in the corpus (AFR-0* in 3 files, INV-1* in 1, GT-0* in 1, AAI in 2, PLP in 1, IR-0* in 1, CM-0* in 1, LA-0* in 1); none is reconciled, mapped, superseded, or mentioned. Also uncited: Step 048 (global invariants), Step 092 (invariant preservation), Step 025N (a prior 'algebra' -- Evidence Aggregation Algebra), Step 091 (safety/liveness ground for Step 209's own Sections 209.35-37).

b_rows_sample.anchor: IS IT AN ALGEBRA? NO.
b_rows_sample.statement: Probe (c-ii): an algebra requires a carrier set, closed operations, and laws. Step 209 supplies none of the three properly: the carrier ('an invariant') is never typed and is used interchangeably as a predicate on states (I(s)), a proposition (I_1 ∧ I_2), and a named object (I_identity) within one file; the only operation is unqualified conjunction (I_global = AND of I_i), imported from propositional logic and never defined on the carrier; no laws are stated (no associativity, commutativity, identity element, closure, absorption, or distributivity). The only other algebraic-looking object, A = {C,I,S,T,R} (Section 209.34), is ill-typed: written in set-brace notation for what the surrounding text treats as an ordered heterogeneous 5-tuple, so it cannot support the componentwise access the text assumes. Verdict: Step 209 is a taxonomy plus a conjunction, mislabelled an algebra -- a useful, well-organised three-level taxonomy of invariants (local/context/system), not an algebra.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Satisfiability is declared and never tested
b_rows_sample.statement: Step 209 Section 209.32 declares that I_global = AND(I_1..I_n) 'is only valid if the invariants are jointly satisfiable' and states SAT(I_1 ∧ I_2 ∧ ... ∧ I_n) 'is an important next mathematical direction' but never tests it: COMPUTABILITY verdict DEFINED, not CONSTRUCTIBLE (the I_i are natural-language predicates, not formulas in any decidable logic), not COMPUTED, not TESTED. Section 209.33 constructs a hypothetical unsatisfiable pair (Action->Approval vs Action->ImmediateExecution) and does not check it against the actual I_KOS set.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Cardinality drift: the 8-set I_KOS is silently superseded by a 15-list I1-I15 without amendment
b_rows_sample.statement: Probe (c-iii): Step 209 Section 209.42 boxes and freezes an 8-member invariant set I_KOS = {I_identity, I_version, I_provenance, I_temporal, I_epistemic, I_authority, I_decision, I_execution}. Step 210 Section 210.25 then tabulates 15 invariants I1-I15 with no mapping given between the 8 and the 15. Independently checked: I13 (illegal transitions rejected) and I14 (preconditions/postconditions) have no member of I_KOS to belong to, and I15 (no semantic strengthening) is likewise unhoused unless forced into I_epistemic. The 8-set is silently superseded by the 15-list without amendment; only Step 209's own caveat ('we should not freeze this yet') prevents this from being an outright contradiction.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Further arithmetic checks: 0.87>=0.80 correct; 0.91+/-0.08 within range at 1 sigma but 2-sigma bound exceeds 1; ratio checks disclaimed
b_rows_sample.statement: Additional independently-verified arithmetic in the band: Step 209 Section 209.15's 0.87 >= 0.80 evaluates to True (correct). Step 208 Section 208.14 / Step 210 Section 210.12's 0.91 +/- 0.08 gives [0.83, 0.99], within [0,1] at 1-sigma, but at 2-sigma the upper bound is 1.07 > 1 -- out of range for a quantity called 'confidence', though the corpus never commits this specific error since the interval's coverage level is left unlabelled. Step 215 Section 215.24's ratios (182/43=4.233, 43/17=2.529, 17/8=2.125, 8/4=2.0, total 45.5x) make no arithmetic claim and are correctly disclaimed as unknown. Step 209 Section 209.42 vs Step 210 Section 210.25: |I_KOS|=8 vs |{I1..I15}|=15, difference 7, mapping absent (unreconciled).

b_rows_sample.anchor: FORMAL OBJECTS: I_L(A), I_C(BC), I_S(System); Execution cannot manufacture authority; Semantic Laundering; I_KOS 8-set
b_rows_sample.statement: Step 209 ('Invariant Algebra') stratifies invariants into local/context/system levels (I_L, I_C, I_S); defines Verified(E)⇒Provenance(E)∧Integrity(E), Valid(A)⇒EvidenceBasis(A)∧ModelVersion(A), Final(D)⇒DecisionBasis(D)∧Authority(D), Executed(X)⇒Authorized(X) boxed as 'Execution cannot manufacture authority'; an epistemic partial order and knowledge lattice; 'Semantic Laundering' (a downstream context losing provenance/uncertainty of an upstream claim and treating the result as stronger than warranted); 'Determinism != Correctness'; architecture-as-CSP A={C,I,S,T,R}; safety properties P1-P4 and liveness properties L1-L2; and the boxed 8-member frozen set I_KOS={I_identity,I_version,I_provenance,I_temporal,I_epistemic,I_authority,I_decision,I_execution}.

b_rows_sample.anchor: PREVIOUS DEPENDENCY: 1 (Step 208 only); LATER RESPONSE: Step 210 replaces I_KOS with I1-I15 without amendment
b_rows_sample.statement: Step 209 cites exactly one prior step (Step 208) and zero prior invariant families. Later response in scope: Step 210 Section 210.25 replaces the 8-member I_KOS with a 15-row I1-I15 without amendment; Step 210 Section 210.9 restates Step 209's Section 209.25 semantic-strength principle as Strength(T(x))>Strength(x) requires Justified(T); Step 212 Section 212.4 reprints I1-I15.

b_rows_sample.anchor: EVOLUTION VERDICT: REFRAMES; DEFINITION VERDICT: PARTIALLY_CLEAR with one ILL-TYPED object
b_rows_sample.statement: Step 209 reframes scattered '!=' observations into a stratified system but does not resolve the SAT question it raises nor reconcile with any prior invariant family. CLEAR: the three-level stratification, Executed(X)⇒Authorized(X), semantic laundering, determinism!=correctness. ILL-TYPED: A={C,I,S,T,R} uses set-brace notation for an ordered heterogeneous 5-tuple, which has no positional structure though the surrounding text requires componentwise access. NOT_DEFINED: the type of 'an invariant' itself, used as a predicate on states, a proposition, and a named object within one file. INCOMPLETE: I_KOS's eight members are one-word labels with no formulas, unlike the file's own worked examples.

b_rows_sample.anchor: FIRST INVALID INFERENCE: Section 209.32 (conjunction written as established, satisfiability tested after, never run)
b_rows_sample.statement: I_global = AND_{i=1}^n I_i (Section 209.32) is written as an established equality, and the satisfiability precondition (SAT test) is stated only afterward, as future work, never run. If the I_i are not jointly satisfiable then I_global is identically false and the boxed I_global = AND(I_KOS) is an assertion of contradiction. Everything downstream that treats I_global as a satisfiable target -- Step 210's matrix, Step 211's AAG, Step 212's gap register -- is conditional on repairing this. Secondary: Section 209.14's determinism claim (SameState+SameCommand⇒SameDomainResult) is used inconsistently as assumption, requirement, and derived property without saying which.

b_rows_sample.anchor: COMPUTABILITY: nothing reaches CONSTRUCTIBLE; TEST VERDICT: NOT_EXECUTED
b_rows_sample.statement: I_L/I_C/I_S stratification is DEFINED; I_KOS's 8 members are DEFINED but not INPUTS_KNOWN (unformalized); SAT(I_1∧...∧I_n) and SAT(A) are DEFINED but not CONSTRUCTIBLE (natural-language predicates, no decidable-logic encoding, and A is ill-typed); P1-P4/L1-L2 are DEFINED, self-described as 'candidates, not yet final requirements'; delta(A_t,c), Pre, Post are DEFINED with no aggregate instantiated. The file's own Section 209.34 concedes 'this is not yet a complete formal verification system.' Test verdict NOT_EXECUTED -- P1-P4 are called 'excellent candidates for deterministic assurance tests', none written or run.

b_rows_sample.anchor: STATISTICAL VERDICT: STRONG; MEASUREMENT VERDICT: MIXED with a good refusal and a violation
b_rows_sample.statement: Step 209's separation of probabilistic inference from deterministic governance (Section 209.15), Determinism!=Correctness (Section 209.16), InvalidModelApplication!=LowConfidence (Section 209.17, a genuinely important distinction between model misspecification and wide posteriors), HighUncertainty!=KnownIncorrect / LowUncertainty!=GuaranteedTrue (Section 209.18), and ObservedCorrelation⇏Causation (Section 209.29, uncited against Step 074) are all statistically correct. Measurement: Section 209.21 correctly declines to universalize a total order on epistemic strength (Unknown≺Hypothesized≺Supported, 'should not be interpreted as a universal total ordering') -- a good refusal -- but Section 209.25 then writes S(T(x))>S(x), a strict comparison requiring exactly the order just declined, four pages later with no reconciliation. KnowledgeState=(EvidenceStrength,Consistency,Uncertainty) is correctly presented as a partial order/lattice admitting incomparable elements, with no arithmetic attempted (correct). I_global=AND(I_KOS) conjoins a nominal set of one-word labels that are not propositions -- a type gap.

b_rows_sample.anchor: DDD VERDICT: STRONG on structure, WEAK on consistency boundaries; UL: 'Semantic Laundering' the best-defined new term
b_rows_sample.statement: The I_L/I_C/I_S stratification is textbook-correct and the clearest statement of the aggregate/context/system-invariant distinction in the corpus; Section 209.6 correctly identifies Decision.AssessmentRef⇒Resolvable(AssessmentRef) as crossing aggregates, but DDD's standard remedy (a consistency-boundary decision -- strong vs eventual consistency, process manager/saga) is never offered, despite the corpus already containing '# Step 166 — Process Managers, Sagas' (uncited). 'Semantic Laundering' (Section 209.24: 'a downstream context loses the provenance or uncertainty of an upstream claim and treats the transformed result as stronger than its source warrants') is judged the single best-defined new term in the band; against this, I_KOS's eight members enter the language as labels without definitions.

b_rows_sample.anchor: ASSUMPTIONS / HIDDEN ASSUMPTIONS: conjunction cannot express the dependency graph the file itself draws
b_rows_sample.statement: Stated assumptions: invariants are propositions closed under AND; a single global conjunction is the right composition; governance transitions can be made deterministic. Hidden: that conjunction is the only composition operator needed, despite Section 209.31's dependency graph showing invariants depending on one another (a relation AND cannot express) -- Sections 209.31 and 209.32 are structurally inconsistent, a dependency graph is not a flat conjunction (Internal Contradiction #B); that the I_i are mutually independent, contradicted by 209.31; that I_KOS's eight members cover the space, with no completeness argument (Step 210 immediately produces 15). Undefined symbols: Integrity(E), EvidenceBasis(A), AssessmentMethod(A), DecisionBasis(D), ApplicablePolicy(D), Resolvable(.), Traceable(D,Basis(D)), Basis(D), S(x), EvidenceStrength/Consistency components, Eventually(.), and every member of I_KOS.

b_rows_sample.anchor: WHAT SURVIVES / WHAT DOES NOT SURVIVE — Step 209
b_rows_sample.statement: Survives: the three-level invariant stratification; Semantic Laundering; Determinism!=Correctness; InvalidModelApplication!=LowConfidence; Execution cannot manufacture authority; identity continuity independent of state continuity; the safety/liveness lens; the insight that a constitution should constrain invariants, not technologies. Does not survive: the title (it is not an algebra); A={C,I,S,T,R} as typed; SAT(A) as computable; I_global=AND(I_KOS) as a verified-satisfiable object (unverified, and structurally at odds with the dependency graph of Section 209.31); S(T(x))>S(x) as a well-formed comparison.

b_rows_sample.anchor: The symbol I is silently rebound between Step 208 (information measure) and Step 209 onward (invariant) with no announcement
b_rows_sample.statement: Step 208 uses I exclusively for an information measure (I(E), I(A), I_required, I_preserved); Step 209 onward uses I exclusively for invariants (I_L, I_C, I_S, I_i, I_identity, I1-I15, I(s)). The rebinding is never announced -- a reader comparing I(C(A)) (Section 208.4, information) to I(s)=True (Section 210.32, an invariant predicate) is reading two different symbols under one glyph.

b_rows_sample.anchor: The Evidence/Test ordering is reversed between files, and Step 210's own boxed conclusion contradicts Step 210's own tuple
b_rows_sample.statement: Step 209's tail agenda for 210 orders Invariant->Owner->EnforcementPoint->Test->Evidence->FailureMode; Step 210's own Section 210.1 tuple orders enforcement, monitoring, test, failure (test before the implied evidence); but Step 210's own boxed Section 210.40 conclusion states Invariant->Owner->Enforcement->Evidence->Test->Assurance (evidence before test); Step 211 Section 211.2 (boxed) and Step 214 Section 214.2 (boxed) both revert to Test before Evidence. Four sources agree that Test precedes Evidence; Step 210's one boxed conclusion disagrees with all of them, including with its own tuple -- the direction matters (Evidence->Test means evidence licenses the test; Test->Evidence means the test produces the evidence, which is what Steps 212-214 assume throughout). This is Contradiction #5.

b_rows_sample.anchor: A and Gap: eight bindings of A, four bindings of Gap with two different ordinal category sets
b_rows_sample.statement: A denotes: Assessment (208-212, throughout), an aggregate state A_t (209.13), the architecture-as-CSP set A (209.34), an assurance vector (211.9), an AI-artifact 7-tuple (211.21), a statistical-result 8-tuple (210.13), an architecture snapshot A_t (213.16-18), and an artifact A_j (213.4) -- eight bindings, with Section 209.13's aggregate-state A_t formally indistinguishable in notation from Section 213.17-18's architecture-state A_t (delta(A_t,c)=A_{t+1} vs A_0->A_1->...). Gap denotes: a numeric difference (211.4, 212.10), an ordinal category (211.4's {None,Low,Medium,High,Critical} vs 212.10's different {None,Partial,Significant,Critical,Unknown}), a class (212.11 G1-G5), and a register row (212.31 G-01-G-15) -- four bindings, with the two ordinal category sets differing from each other.

b_rows_sample.anchor: CONTRADICTION #2 — Provenance composition (208) excludes the authority Step 209 requires
b_rows_sample.statement: Step 208 Section 208.25 asserts as an equality P(G)=P(A)∪P(E), boxed as 'provenance must be closed under semantic transformation.' Step 209 Section 209.4 requires Final(D)⇒DecisionBasis(D)∧Authority(D). Since Authority(D), the governance grant that made a decision final, is in neither P(A) nor P(E), a governed decision's provenance under Section 208.25 cannot contain its own authority, yet Step 209's own traceability requirement (Basis(D) including authority) demands that it does -- the two cannot both hold. Independently checked, the equality is additionally vacuous if closure holds (P(A)⊇P(E) implies the union is just P(A)) and self-refuting if it does not. Severity HIGH.

b_rows_sample.anchor: CONTRADICTION #15 — Total order on epistemic strength declined in Step 209 Section 209.21 and then used in 209.25 and 210.9
b_rows_sample.statement: Step 209 Section 209.21 states Unknown≺Hypothesized≺Supported and explicitly declines a universal total ordering ('the actual epistemic lattice must be derived from the domain'). Step 209 Section 209.25 (S(T(x))>S(x)) and Step 210 Section 210.9 (Strength(T(x))>Strength(x)) both then use strict > on the same kind of quantity, presupposing the order that was just declined four sections earlier and never derived. Severity MEDIUM.

a_rows_sample.statement: Family 6 (REASONING), the largest family (9 rows): INV-KOS-Inference-001 Observation != Inference; INV-KOS-Justification-001 Nature of Justification (forbids Claim->Knowledge without justification); H-KOS-Reasoning-Separation-001 Generate vs Evaluate (forbids the black-box 'Evidence -> Magic AI -> Truth'; layered Kernel + Engine, the Validation Layer verdict vocabulary); H-KOS-Reasoning-Provenance-001 Reasoning Path Preservation (forbids Conclusion->Bare output); H-KOS-Vyapti-001 Inference-Warranting Relation (forbids Evidence->Conclusion without a preserved rule; SS32 = the 'decisive' re-derivation; subsumes proposed Reasoning-001/002 and the upadhi/defeaters facet); H-KOS-Fallacy-001 Invalid-Reasoning Detection (circularity/infinite regress/self-reference; COMPLEMENTARY to Failure-001); H-KOS-Failure-001 Failed-Reasoning Preservation (REJECTED as an explicit epistemic state); H-KOS-Lifecycle-Reasoning-001 Epistemic Inquiry Lifecycle (Observation->Question->Investigation->Reasoning->Challenge->Determination->Knowledge State, never Input->Fact); H-KOS-Intent-001 Purpose/Intent of Reasoning (Vada/Jalpa/Vitanda distinction, flagged Engine-layer, 'genuinely novel row').

a_rows_sample.statement: Ten named compression-test clusters, each resolved by ID/registration/validation-state (never resemblance), with no row added/removed/promoted: (1) Context-002<->SemanticBoundary<->Ontology-001<->type-model<->Abhava-Boundary -> SUBSUMES (one row + facets); (2) H-KOS-Agent-001 vs INV-KOS-Agent-001 vs Justification-001 vs Relationship-001 -> DISTINCT/SUPERSEDED; (3) Relation-001 subsumption test -> RELATED (principle/instance); (4) Pramana-001<->Reasoning-Separation-001<->Agent-001<->INV-001 -> DISTINCT; (5) Pramana source-role separation naming -> RESOLVED (row content, not a new row); (6) Vyapti-001<->Reasoning-001/002<->upadhi/defeaters -> SUBSUMES; (7) Fallacy-001<->Failure-001 -> COMPLEMENTARY; (8) Dialogue-001<->Contradiction-001<->Revisability-001<->Intent-001 -> COMPLEMENTARY; (9) Uncertainty-001<->Abhava-001 -> SUBSUMES; (10) Dimension Independence<->NonInterference-001 -> OVERLAPPING, carried to P5 as a possible consolidation pair, NOT resolved here.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Family 2.5 Reasoning family
a_rows_sample.statement: Reasoning-family validation decisions (9 rows): INV-KOS-Inference-001 STRONG -> KERNEL, SURVIVES (law 6); INV-KOS-Justification-001 STRONG -> KERNEL, SURVIVES (law 6); H-KOS-Reasoning-Separation-001 STRONG -> KERNEL(law)+ENGINE(the Validation Layer verdict vocabulary), SURVIVES (law 6, verdict vocabulary deferred as enforcement mechanism); H-KOS-Reasoning-Provenance-001 MODERATE-STRONG -> KERNEL, SURVIVES (law 6, 'the path is part of justification'); H-KOS-Vyapti-001 STRONG (subsumes Reasoning-001/002+upadhi) -> KERNEL, SURVIVES (law 6); H-KOS-Fallacy-001 STRONG -> KERNEL(state law)+ENGINE(detection machinery), SURVIVES (state content to law 7, detection deferred to ENGINE); H-KOS-Failure-001 STRONG -> KERNEL, SURVIVES (law 7); H-KOS-Lifecycle-Reasoning-001 MODERATE -> MECHANISM, DEFERRED (the lifecycle stages are the operational process executing law 6; constitutional content already expressed by law 6); H-KOS-Intent-001 MODERATE (flagged engine-layer) -> ENGINE, DEFERRED (its corruption already covered by law 6 + law 7 -- 'useful; not constitutional').

b_rows_sample.anchor: 1. Pratijna (Proposition) ... 2. Hetu (Reason) ... 3. Udaharana (Example) ... 4. Upanaya (Application) ... 5. Nigamana (Conclusion) ... Pakṣadharmatā ... Vyapti — invariable concomitance
b_rows_sample.statement: Describes the five-membered syllogism (Nyaya-Pararthanumana) and its two validity requirements: pakṣadharmatā (the reason must be present in the subject) and vyapti (invariable concomitance between reason and conclusion, e.g. smoke always accompanied by fire).

b_rows_sample.anchor: Candidate TARKA-002: Vyapti Confirmation — Inferences must establish invariable concomitance (vyapti) between reason and conclusion, confirmed through counterfactual testing.
b_rows_sample.statement: Candidate invariant TARKA-002: inferences must establish vyapti between reason and conclusion, confirmed through counterfactual testing; classified 'candidate', pending validation.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Forbidden Transitions: Knowledge claim without pramana grounding; Inference without vyapti; Tarka treated as independent knowledge source; Unstructured doubt; Reasoning contrary to authority without governed transition; Circular reasoning
b_rows_sample.statement: Tabulates six forbidden transitions derived from Tarka Shastra, each paired with the Nyaya parallel that forbids it (apramana, hetvabhasa, tarka-is-apramana, unclassified samsaya, dustarka, the five circular-tarka fallacies).

b_rows_sample.anchor: H-KOS-Vyapti-001: KnowledgeOS SHALL preserve the logical relationship that connects evidence to conclusion for every derived knowledge object.
b_rows_sample.statement: Proposes H-KOS-Vyapti-001, described as 'perhaps the most architecturally valuable concept': without the explicit rule connecting evidence to conclusion, 'Evidence -> Conclusion' remains opaque.

b_rows_sample.anchor: The book's central theme is the Indian concept of vyapti — the inference-warranting relation between evidence/reason and conclusion... how a relation between a reason and an inferred conclusion becomes rationally justified.
b_rows_sample.statement: States the reviewed book's central theme (vyapti, the inference-warranting relation) as directly giving KnowledgeOS 'several architectural principles', framing the book as probably one of the strongest philosophical sources for defining KnowledgeOS's reasoning architecture.

b_rows_sample.anchor: H-KOS-Vyapti-001: KnowledgeOS SHALL preserve the warranting relation that connects evidence to conclusion. A conclusion without an explicit inference relation SHALL remain a hypothesis.
b_rows_sample.statement: Argues the current Evidence->Reasoning->Conclusion model is incomplete and must add an explicit Inference-Warranting Relation (Vyapti) node between Evidence and Conclusion (smoke/fire example), with the added consequence that a conclusion lacking this explicit relation remains only a hypothesis.

b_rows_sample.anchor: evidence/reason functions as a logical sign (linga) and the inferred entity is the signified (lingin) ... CPU usage 95% -> Role: Possible sign -> Warrant: High CPU sustained > X minutes correlates with degradation -> Inference: Potential performance failure
b_rows_sample.statement: Introduces the sign (linga) / signified (lingin) distinction and applies it to an AI-monitoring worked example, arguing the sign-to-inference relationship itself must become a first-class, explicitly warranted object.

b_rows_sample.anchor: sound reasoning vs. sophistical reasoning... Reason Quality Analysis: Valid / Weak / Contradictory / Unsupported ... Reasoning Verification Engine. Input: Claim, Evidence, Inference, Context. Output: VALIDATED, QUESTIONABLE, CONFLICTED, INVALID, UNKNOWN
b_rows_sample.statement: Proposes a new kernel capability, a 'Reasoning Verification Engine', with a specified input schema (Claim/Evidence/Inference/Context) and a five-state output classification (VALIDATED/QUESTIONABLE/CONFLICTED/INVALID/UNKNOWN), motivated by the observation that LLMs generate arguments but KnowledgeOS must judge them.

type_signature.codomain: one of {VALIDATED, QUESTIONABLE, CONFLICTED, INVALID, UNKNOWN}

b_rows_sample.anchor: A valid sign must satisfy: 1. Present in the subject under consideration 2. Present in similar cases 3. Absent in dissimilar cases ... Service outage caused by memory leak ... Then confidence increases.
b_rows_sample.statement: Applies Dignaga's three-condition test for sign validity (trairupya) to a worked incident-investigation example (memory-leak-caused outage) and proposes an 'Inference Validation Matrix' architecture component scoring similar-vs-different cases.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Truth is not produced by storing more information. Truth emerges when evidence, reasoning relations, objections, and validation rules are preserved together... This book gives KnowledgeOS the missing 'logic of justification' layer between knowledge storage and truth discovery.
b_rows_sample.statement: Closing table maps eight Matilal-derived concepts (Vyapti, Linga/Lingin, Vada, Jalpa/Vitanda, Tarka, Hetvabhasa, triple sign-condition, debate tradition) to eight KnowledgeOS architectural impacts, and states the final insight that this book moves KnowledgeOS from a knowledge graph to an epistemic reasoning system.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Reality -> Observation/Language Input -> Semantic Kernel (Matilal, 'What does it mean?') -> Epistemic Kernel (Nyaya, 'Why should we trust it?') -> Knowledge Object -> Decision/Action ... The first book gives you the truth engine. This book gives you the meaning engine.
b_rows_sample.statement: Combines the two reviewed books (S0223's Nyaya 'Epistemic Kernel'/truth engine and this file's Matilal 'Semantic Kernel'/meaning engine) into a single pipeline from Reality through Semantic Kernel and Epistemic Kernel to Knowledge Object and Decision/Action, framed as a foundation for a true 'Knowledge Operating System'.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Knowledge is not located at one level of representation. It emerges from relationships between levels.
a_rows_sample.statement: Central discovery of the GEB first pass: knowledge emerges from relationships between levels of representation rather than residing at any one level, described as sitting between the consciousness model, the Zero lens, the Dhatu lens, and KnowledgeOS, and as more powerful than the prior chakra-to-knowledge mapping.

a_rows_sample.anchor: At which level does a particular knowledge structure become meaningful? ... Physical level -> signals -> symbols -> concepts -> models -> knowledge -> meta-knowledge
a_rows_sample.statement: Reframes the question from 'which level contains the knowledge' to 'at which level does a knowledge structure become meaningful', citing Hofstadter's Chapter X observation that the same system (cells/molecules/DNA/a person, or a TV image as pixels vs the represented person) can be understood at radically different levels; a physical->signals->symbols->concepts->models->knowledge->meta-knowledge chain is offered, stated to strongly validate the earlier Kosha idea with a more rigorous computational interpretation.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Knowledge core = representation invariant structure
a_rows_sample.statement: Combines Davidson's 'look for what remains invariant across representations' with Hofstadter's conceptual-skeleton definition into the hypothesis Knowledge core = representation-invariant structure, explicitly qualified as potentially the most fundamental part of knowledge rather than all of it.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Knowledge != stored propositions ... Declarative Knowledge + Procedural Knowledge + Structural Knowledge + Meta-Knowledge. This is a major correction to a conventional Knowledge Graph model.
a_rows_sample.statement: Distinguishes declarative knowledge (explicit facts, e.g. 'An octopus has eight tentacles') from procedural knowledge (embedded in a system's operation; a system may 'know how' without any explicit statement of what it knows), concluding Knowledge != stored propositions and that a knowledge model needs Declarative + Procedural + Structural + Meta-Knowledge components; explicitly flagged as a major correction to a conventional Knowledge Graph model.

a_rows_sample.anchor: A statistical model is a representation, not reality. ... that is a property of our model of the claim, not necessarily knowledge.
a_rows_sample.statement: Cites Hofstadter's point that chunked/statistical models necessarily sacrifice determinism for simplicity (predicting probabilities over abstract behavioral spaces rather than reproducing reality with physical precision), warning that a statistical Knowledge Index (e.g. P(claim is true)) must never be confused with knowledge itself -- it is a property of the model of the claim, reinforcing a prior epistemological conclusion.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Knowledge maturity = ability to transform raw state into useful higher-level structure ... A novice sees piece piece piece. An expert sees attack defense weakness structure pattern.
a_rows_sample.statement: Using Hofstadter's discussion of de Groot's chess research (experts perceive the board differently, recognizing higher-level chunks and implicitly pruning irrelevant possibilities rather than simply searching more), defines knowledge maturity as the ability to transform a raw state into useful higher-level structure, concluding knowledge is better representation, not merely more data.

a_rows_sample.anchor: K0 — Raw observations ... K7 — Self-model of knowledge ... This is not a hierarchy claimed by Hofstadter; it is our synthesis
a_rows_sample.statement: Defines an eight-level knowledge-state hierarchy K0 (raw observations) through K7 (self-model of knowledge), via K1 explicit facts, K2 relations, K3 patterns, K4 conceptual structures, K5 models/explanations, K6 meta-models, explicitly disclaimed as the author's own synthesis from Hofstadter's levels-of-description, knowledge-representation and self-reference discussions rather than a hierarchy Hofstadter himself asserts.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Critical Thinking + Multiple Representations + Invariant Extraction may be our strongest knowledge-extraction methodology so far.
a_rows_sample.statement: Extends the recurring critical-thinking interrogation chain (What is explicit? implicit? assumptions? relations? patterns? alternative representations? what remains invariant?) with Hofstadter's discussion of multiple representations, proposing 'Critical Thinking + Multiple Representations + Invariant Extraction' as possibly the strongest knowledge-extraction methodology found so far.

a_rows_sample.anchor: We should not assume that a knowledge item has a single physical location. ... rule + code + workflow + database constraint + human practice + documentation + tests
a_rows_sample.statement: From Hofstadter's claim that procedural knowledge can be spread throughout a system rather than existing in one retrievable location, derives the principle that a KnowledgeOS knowledge item should not be assumed to have a single physical location -- it may be jointly constituted by a rule, code, workflow, database constraint, human practice, documentation, and tests -- stated to be close to problems already encountered in the AI Engineering Platform.

a_rows_sample.anchor: SHRDLU ... parsing, internal representation, reasoning about the world, answering questions, etc. were deeply intertwined ... some knowledge relationships are inherently cross-cutting.
a_rows_sample.statement: Uses Hofstadter's SHRDLU discussion (parsing, representation, reasoning, question-answering deeply intertwined in its procedural knowledge) to warn against assuming knowledge is cleanly separable into its own module; some knowledge relationships are inherently cross-cutting (tangled among representation, reasoning and action), and the architectural response should recognize this rather than blindly reproduce the tangle.

a_rows_sample.anchor: INPUT/SIGNALS -> REPRESENTATION -> PATTERN/CHUNK -> CONCEPT -> MODEL -> SELF-MODEL -> META-KNOWLEDGE ... the self emerging through self-representation.
a_rows_sample.statement: Reinterprets the earlier Manas/Buddhi/Ahamkara consciousness mapping computationally as Input/Signals -> Representation -> Pattern/Chunk -> Concept -> Model -> Self-Model -> Meta-Knowledge, and defines the strange-loop mechanism: a knowledge system creates a representation of itself, that representation changes the system, the system changes its representation, recursively -- citing Hofstadter's proposal that higher and lower levels mutually influence each other and the self emerges through self-representation.

a_rows_sample.anchor: K(K) means the system has a representation of its own knowledge state. K(K(K)) would represent knowledge about its representation of knowledge. We should not assume this infinite hierarchy is useful.
a_rows_sample.statement: Introduces K(K) notation for meta-knowledge (a representation of the system's own knowledge state) and K(K(K)) for knowledge about that representation, explicitly warning against assuming an infinite such hierarchy is useful since it can become tangled instead (Knowledge -> knowledge about knowledge -> knowledge modifies knowledge -> self-reference -> strange loop), proposed as a possible foundation for a formal model of 'Knowledge Consciousness.'

a_rows_sample.anchor: Panini/Dhatu: How is structure generated from expression? Davidson: What remains invariant across representation? Critical Thinking: What survives systematic epistemic challenge? Pollock: What makes a belief rationally defensible and defeater-resistant? Fraser: What latent states and transitions can be statistically inferred? Consciousness traditions: ... Hofstadter: How do representations across levels recursively interact and produce self-reference?
a_rows_sample.statement: Synthesizes seven parallel research lenses (Panini/Dhatu, Davidson, Critical Thinking, Pollock, Fraser, Consciousness traditions, Hofstadter) as non-competing, each posing a distinct question about the same underlying research object.

a_rows_sample.anchor: REALITY -> OBSERVATIONS -> REPRESENTATIONS -> {LANGUAGE/PATTERNS/ACTION} -> CONCEPTUAL MODEL -> {EXPLICIT/IMPLICIT KNOWLEDGE} -> KNOWLEDGE STATE -> Critical Thinking -> {DEFEATERS/ALTERNATIVES} -> INVARIANT CORE (ZERO) -> META-KNOWLEDGE -> SELF-MODEL -> STRANGE LOOP -> updates knowledge
a_rows_sample.statement: Presents an integrated 'research architecture' diagram chaining Reality -> Observations -> Representations (via Language/Dhatu, Patterns/Chunking, Action/Procedure) -> Conceptual Model -> Explicit/Implicit Knowledge -> Knowledge State -> Critical Thinking -> Defeaters/Alternatives -> Invariant Core (ZERO) -> Meta-Knowledge -> Self-Model -> Strange Loop, which feeds back to update knowledge; described as becoming a real theory of knowledge dynamics.

a_rows_sample.anchor: KnowledgeState = (Representation, Relations, Patterns, Procedures, Evidence, Uncertainty, Invariants, SelfModel) ... KnowledgeState(t+1) - KnowledgeState(t) ... measures knowledge transformation, rather than simply knowledge accumulation.
a_rows_sample.statement: Rejects a scalar 'Knowledge = 83%' score in favor of a KnowledgeState tuple (Representation, Relations, Patterns, Procedures, Evidence, Uncertainty, Invariants, SelfModel), with six named measurement dimensions (RepresentationDiversity: how many independent representations express the same structure; InvariantStrength: how much structure survives representation change; PatternDepth: how many abstraction levels the system recognizes; ProceduralCompetence: can it use the knowledge; DefeaterResistance: does it survive critical challenge; SelfModelAccuracy: does the system accurately represent what it knows/doesn't know), and defines KnowledgeState(t+1)-KnowledgeState(t) as a measure of knowledge transformation rather than mere accumulation.

a_rows_sample.anchor: A knowledge system can exist simultaneously at multiple levels of representation, and the important structure may lie in the mappings between those levels rather than in any single level. ... This may be the missing bridge between our Zero lens and our Knowledge State theory.
a_rows_sample.statement: States the first-GEB-pass conclusion: the most important extraction is not 'strange loops = consciousness' but that a knowledge system exists simultaneously at multiple representation levels, with the important structure lying in the mappings between levels; citing Hofstadter's connection of meaning to structural mappings/isomorphisms, conceptual skeletons as invariant shared structures, the declarative/procedural distinction, and higher-level descriptions having explanatory power unavailable at lower levels; proposes this as the missing bridge between the Zero lens and the Knowledge State theory, recommending GEB be read specifically for levels -> representation -> invariant structure -> procedural knowledge -> self-reference -> strange loops.

a_rows_sample.anchor: before distinction -> "One" -> tapas -> kama -> differentiation -> manifested world -> knowledge of origin? -> unknown ... a very interesting structural isomorphism in the Hofstadter sense.
a_rows_sample.statement: Presents the Nasadiya Sukta (Rg Veda 10.129, per a 2023 Medium-article reading) as beginning before ordinary existence/non-existence, space, time, life/death and differentiation, moving through tad ekam ('That One'), tapas, kama, differentiation, manifestation, and a final question of whether the origin can be known; abstracts this into a chain isomorphic in structure (not claimed as historical connection) to GEB's level->representation->relation->higher representation->self-reference->strange loop chain, explicitly stating this is not proof the Vedic hymn anticipates GEB.

a_rows_sample.anchor: A knowledge system must represent its own epistemic boundary.
a_rows_sample.statement: Contrasts two independent routes to the same conclusion: GEB's formal-system -> metalevel -> limitation-of-formal-knowledge (citing Hofstadter's description of Godel's sentence as requiring a higher-level view, an 'intrinsically high-level fact'), versus Nasadiya's cosmological-question -> observer -> limits-of-observer's-knowledge; both converge on the boxed principle that a knowledge system must represent its own epistemic boundary.

a_rows_sample.anchor: REALITY/X -> observation -> REPRESENTATION -> abstraction -> PATTERN -> CONCEPT -> KNOWLEDGE -> reflection -> META-KNOWLEDGE -> self-reference -> SELF-MODEL -> EPISTEMIC BOUNDARY -> {KNOWABLE, UNKNOWN}
a_rows_sample.statement: Revises the prior Reality->Observation->Representation->Pattern->Concept->Knowledge->Meta-knowledge->Self-model pipeline by adding a terminal EPISTEMIC BOUNDARY node splitting into KNOWABLE and UNKNOWN, with Zero (invariant core across representations A/B/C) placed orthogonally to the whole architecture rather than as one of its stages.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Nasadiya contributes the epistemic-boundary dimension. GEB contributes the multi-level/self-reference dimension. Dhātu contributes the generative/transformation dimension. Critical thinking contributes the validation/defeater dimension. And KnowledgeOS becomes the engineering realization of the resulting knowledge-state model, rather than merely a repository of documents.
a_rows_sample.statement: Assigns each of four converging lenses a distinct contribution to one resulting knowledge-state model (Nasadiya: epistemic-boundary; GEB: multi-level/self-reference; Dhatu: generative/transformation; critical thinking: validation/defeater), concluding KnowledgeOS is the engineering realization of that model rather than a document repository.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Pramāṇa describes the route to knowledge. Verification/refutation describes how the resulting claim is tested.
b_rows_sample.statement: Distinguishes pramana (route to knowledge acquisition) from verification/refutation (how a resulting claim is subsequently tested), combining both into a pipeline: Knowledge Claim -> Pramana -> Epistemic Tests {Verify, Repeat, Refute} -> Knowledge State.

b_rows_sample.anchor: REALITY -> OBSERVATION -> PRAMĀṆA LENS -> {perception, inference, testimony} -> CLAIM -> CRITICAL THINKING -> {assumptions, alternatives, defeaters} -> EVALUATION -> {evidence, uncertainty, provenance} -> KNOWLEDGE STATE -> TIME -> K(t)->K(t+1)->K(t+2) -> META-KNOWLEDGE -> ZERO
b_rows_sample.statement: Synthesizes all lenses read so far into one combined pipeline from Reality through the Pramana lens (perception/inference/testimony), Claim, Critical Thinking (assumptions/alternatives/defeaters), Evaluation (evidence/uncertainty/provenance), Knowledge State evolving over time (K(t)->K(t+1)->K(t+2)), Meta-Knowledge ('what do we know about what we know?'), terminating in Zero (invariant structure).

b_rows_sample.anchor: EVIDENCE -> PRAMĀṆA/PROVENANCE -> EVALUATION -> {T, F, BOTH/NEITHER} -> KNOWLEDGE STATE -> LEGITIMACY -> GOVERNANCE ... Legitimacy should not manufacture a truth value.
b_rows_sample.statement: Extends the Evidence->Evaluation->Legitimacy architecture with an explicit T/F/Both-Neither evaluation branch feeding Knowledge State, then Legitimacy, then Governance, asserting Legitimacy must act on the epistemic state per constitutional rules rather than manufacture a truth value.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Lens 1 — Ganesha ... Lens 10 — Statistical
b_rows_sample.statement: Formalizes a ten-lens extraction engine, each with a name and defining question: Ganesha (definition -- what exactly is the proposition), Pramana (epistemic origin -- how did we obtain it), Leonardo (critical discovery -- assumptions/alternatives/contradictions), Krishna (purpose -- what decision this knowledge serves), Shani (invariants -- what must not be violated), Zero (invariant structure -- what remains across representations/perspectives), Dhatu (generation -- what transformations generate the observed state), Temporal (evolution -- how the knowledge state changes through time), Hofstadter (self-reference -- what the system knows about its own knowledge), Statistical (quantification -- evidence/uncertainty/convergence/contradiction measurement).

b_rows_sample.anchor: Textual quotation ≠ philosophical interpretation ≠ historical assertion ≠ scientist's personal opinion ≠ physical theory ≠ empirically established result ... "Multiverse exists only in Hindu Cosmology" is an article headline/claim, not something demonstrated by the material presented.
b_rows_sample.statement: Applies the Pramana lens to the source article itself, distinguishing six non-collapsible statement kinds it contains (textual quotation, philosophical interpretation, historical assertion, scientist's personal opinion, physical theory, empirically established result); a physicist's stated belief that a cyclical universe is 'most probable' is testimony/opinion, not established cosmology, and the headline claim 'multiverse exists only in Hindu Cosmology' is not demonstrated by the material presented.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Science -> Method/validation | Time -> Temporal knowledge | Logic -> Epistemic state space | Epistemology -> Knowledge acquisition | Cosmology -> World model | Eschatology -> Terminal state/transformation ... KnowledgeState = (Method, Time, Logic, Epistemology, WorldModel, TerminalState)
b_rows_sample.statement: Maps the six source articles processed across this series to six abstract dimensions (Science->Method/validation, Time->Temporal knowledge, Logic->Epistemic state space, Epistemology->Knowledge acquisition, Cosmology->World model, Eschatology->Terminal state/transformation), formalizing a series-closing tuple KnowledgeState=(Method,Time,Logic,Epistemology,WorldModel,TerminalState).

b_rows_sample.anchor: They weren't producing competing architectures. They were probing different dimensions of the same boundary. ... Dhātu ... Karaka ... Pramāṇa ... Statistical ... Topological ... DDD ... Shani ... Ganesha ... Leonardo ... Krishna ... a multi-dimensional boundary discovery methodology.
b_rows_sample.statement: Reframes the ten accumulated lenses (Dhatu/linguistic: how is meaning expressed; Karaka: what relationships exist between participants; Pramana: on what basis can something be accepted as knowledge; Statistical: how much uncertainty/evidence/structure can be inferred; Topological: shape/connectivity of the knowledge space; DDD: who owns which meaning/invariant; Shani: what must never be violated; Ganesha: do we actually understand the concept; Leonardo: what assumptions are hiding; Krishna: why does this boundary exist) as jointly constituting one multi-dimensional boundary-discovery methodology rather than competing architectures.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Preservation and inference are different obligations with different invariants. The Kernel is a preservation boundary. Possible-worlds semantics, pramāṇa, statistical inference and algorithmic knowledge are all regimes that read the record. That framing satisfies §28 while giving F-4 a real answer: the Kernel's non-negotiable job is to keep the record sufficient and un-foreclosing, not to adjudicate truth.
b_rows_sample.statement: Answers the F-4 open question directly: the Kernel's non-negotiable job is to keep the record sufficient and un-foreclosing, not to adjudicate truth; possible-worlds semantics, the Pramana regime, statistical inference, and algorithmic knowledge are all 'regimes that read the record' rather than parts of the Kernel itself, since preservation (what must be recorded so a model can be applied later) and inference (computing what is known given a model) are different obligations with different invariants.

a_rows_sample.anchor: the philosophical structure is that **Buddhi/intelligence must discriminate and govern the lower mental/sensory tendencies**
a_rows_sample.statement: Correction of a prior KnowledgeOS wording: the Gita does not literally say 'the mind is always busy determining what is right and wrong'; rather, in Gita 3.40-43 the philosophical structure is that Buddhi (intelligence) must discriminate and govern the lower mental/sensory tendencies (Senses < Mind < Intelligence/Buddhi < Self, concluding at 3.43 with instruction to use the higher faculty to control the lower forces).

a_rows_sample.anchor: \text{Observed activity} \neq \text{correct interpretation of activity}
a_rows_sample.statement: From Gita 4.17-18 (the intricacies of action are hard to understand; action-in-inaction/inaction-in-action paradox): observed activity is not equal to the correct interpretation of that activity, so the kernel cannot merely ask 'what happened?' but must also ask 'what does this mean?' and possibly 'was this the right action?'.

a_rows_sample.anchor: The KnowledgeOS kernel is conceptually analogous to a mind whose discriminative faculty must continuously evaluate the current epistemic state and possible transformations of that state.
a_rows_sample.statement: Refinement of the prior hypothesis 'the KnowledgeOS kernel is always busy determining right and wrong' into: the KnowledgeOS kernel is conceptually analogous to a mind whose discriminative faculty must continuously evaluate the current epistemic state and possible transformations of that state, formalized as K_t --Buddhi--> {accept, reject, qualify, revise, defer}.

a_rows_sample.anchor: an ungoverned state-transition mechanism can repeatedly transform K_t in the wrong direction
a_rows_sample.statement: Interprets the idea that 'without governance, the mind/kernel can become its own enemy' as meaning an ungoverned state-transition mechanism can repeatedly transform K_t in the wrong direction, connecting the Buddhi/discrimination hypothesis to a governance-failure warning.

a_rows_sample.anchor: I would therefore mark this as a **candidate R5/R6 hypothesis**, not canonical yet
a_rows_sample.statement: The Buddhi-governs/discriminates-rather-than-accumulates hypothesis is explicitly marked as a candidate R5/R6 hypothesis, not canonical; next test is to determine whether the function is independently derivable from the KnowledgeOS corpus (without the Gita lens) and whether 'right/wrong' should technically become 'valid/invalid', 'admissible/inadmissible', 'qualified/unqualified', or another precise DDD distinction. Explicit warning: moral vocabulary ('right/wrong') should not be imported into the kernel until the corresponding KnowledgeOS predicate is established.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Kernel \neq Buddhi ... Kernel contains/hosts the operations of Buddhi
a_rows_sample.statement: Kernel != Buddhi; rather, the Kernel contains/hosts the operations of Buddhi. Translation table: Mind/Manas -> continuously changing internal processing/state (philosophical lens); Buddhi -> discrimination: distinguish/evaluate/decide (strong candidate); Jnana -> acquired/recognized knowing (theoretical); Kshetra -> the field/state being processed (theoretical); Kshetrajna -> knower/observer of the field (theoretical); Karma -> operation/action (candidate correspondence); Phala -> consequence/result (candidate correspondence); Dharma -> correctness/order per governing principles (candidate correspondence); Sankalpa -> commitment/intention toward a decision (candidate); Viveka -> discrimination between alternatives (particularly relevant to Buddhi); Moksha -> limiting/transcendent epistemic condition (theoretical only).

a_rows_sample.anchor: B(K_t,x)\rightarrow d ... d \in \{\text{supported},\text{refuted},\text{contradictory},\text{unknown},\text{unqualified},\text{inadmissible}\}
a_rows_sample.statement: Mathematical correction to 'the kernel should always be busy determining right and wrong': right/wrong should not initially be binary. Buddhi should implement a discrimination function B(K_t,x) -> d with d in {supported, refuted, contradictory, unknown, unqualified, inadmissible}, not a Boolean truth oracle. Hence Buddhi = epistemic discrimination, not Buddhi = truth; the kernel does not create truth, it evaluates what can legitimately be concluded from its current state and evidence.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Kernel \neq K_t ... The kernel is the **persistent processing mechanism**, whereas K_t is the **current epistemic state**
a_rows_sample.statement: Kernel != K_t: since K_t != K_{t+1} (knowledge state changes with time), the Kernel is not any particular knowledge state; the Kernel is the persistent processing mechanism operating on successive knowledge states, analogous to Mind != one particular thought.

a_rows_sample.anchor: K_{t+1}=F(K_t,\;O_t,\;B_t) ... A defective B_t can therefore systematically produce defective future states.
a_rows_sample.statement: Reinterprets 'the mind can become its own enemy': under the philosophical lens the danger is not the kernel disappearing but the kernel's discrimination becoming misdirected, corrupted, or dominated by an invalid internal process (bad qualification -> bad discrimination -> bad decision -> K_{t+1} -> future reasoning built on bad state), i.e. the kernel becomes its own enemy through epistemic feedback. Formalized as K_{t+1}=F(K_t,O_t,B_t) where B_t is the Buddhi/discrimination operation; a defective B_t can systematically produce defective future states.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Philosophical correspondence \not\Rightarrow primitive
a_rows_sample.statement: DDD discipline (following Steps 285-287): do not yet create 'Buddhi' as a domain object or primitive. Ask instead whether the KnowledgeOS kernel already contains a necessary capability whose philosophical abstraction is best described as Buddhi -- if so the Gita is naming an existing architectural property, not inventing one. Required pipeline: Gita -> hypothesis -> existing KnowledgeOS requirement -> formal operation -> independent derivation -> architecture. Reframes the research question from 'Is Buddhi a KnowledgeOS primitive?' to 'Does KnowledgeOS necessarily require a discrimination capability that operates over its changing epistemic state, and does Buddhi provide a useful philosophical model for that capability?'.

a_rows_sample.anchor: \mathcal B: (K_t,O_t,E_t,C_t) \rightarrow D_t
a_rows_sample.statement: Proposes B:(K_t,O_t,E_t,C_t)->D_t (discrimination/decision result), enumerating what B must do: distinguish, compare, validate, detect contradiction, assess evidence, qualify, reject, accept, defer, update the knowledge state, preserve provenance, determine what remains unknown. Central hypothesis: KnowledgeOS Kernel ~philosophically~ Mind; Buddhi ~philosophically~ Kernel's discrimination capability; K_t = changing Knowledge State; K (calligraphic) = Knowledge Space. Four-level picture: Knowledge Space K -> Knowledge State K_t -> KnowledgeOS Kernel -> Buddhi -> epistemic operations -> K_{t+1}. Explicitly marked as hypothesis pending testing against actual Gita passages and the existing KnowledgeOS corpus, not yet canonical.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Buddhi is a critical control point
a_rows_sample.statement: The kernel/mind 'enemy' danger is not only bad data but can arise from: (1) incomplete observation, (2) overwhelming observation, (3) incorrect interpretation, (4) defective discrimination, (5) incorrect decision, (6) state transition based on that decision -- pipeline O_t -> B_t -> D_t -> K_{t+1}. Hence Buddhi is a critical control point in the kernel architecture. Observation != Understanding and Understanding != Discrimination.

a_rows_sample.anchor: B(x)= \begin{cases}\text{admissible}\\\text{inadmissible}\\\text{unknown}\\\text{conflicting}\\\text{requires qualification}\end{cases}
a_rows_sample.statement: Buddhi modelled as B: E -> D (epistemic alternatives to distinguishable outcomes) with candidate codomain {admissible, inadmissible, unknown, conflicting, requires qualification}; the 'requires qualification' category connects directly to the unresolved Qualify/G1 problem.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Kernel operates under changing conditions ... Buddhi discriminates within those conditions
a_rows_sample.statement: Explicitly corrects a possible direction before it becomes architectural: if Kernel=Mind, the Gita does not suggest Kernel=Sattva. Instead the Kernel operates under changing conditions and Buddhi discriminates within them; the gunas describe the condition in which the kernel operates, not kernel components -- assessed as a cleaner DDD model. Formalizes G_t=(s_t,r_t,m_t) with s_t,r_t,m_t >= 0, optionally normalized s_t+r_t+m_t=1 giving G_t in the 2-simplex Delta^2 -- explicitly flagged as the researchers' own mathematical abstraction, not a Gita-derived numerical value or normalization (Gita -> qualitative dynamics; Mathematics -> possible quantitative representation).

a_rows_sample.anchor: we should not say Buddhi=\delta ... B_t(K_t,o_t,G_t,R_t) \rightarrow d_t ... \delta(K_t,d_t)=K_{t+1}
a_rows_sample.statement: Careful mathematical separation: Buddhi != delta. B_t is Evaluation/Discrimination, delta is State Transition. Formalized as B_t(K_t,o_t,G_t,R_t) -> d_t, followed by delta(K_t,d_t)=K_{t+1}. Candidate (non-canonical) Buddhi decision codomain d_t in {Accept, Reject, Qualify, Defer, Transform, Escalate}; notes the philosophical lens does not solve the unresolved Qualify problem but may explain why qualification is a distinct act of discrimination.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Buddhi \neq unrestricted inference ... Governance becomes structurally distinct from the kernel
a_rows_sample.statement: Explains the 'kernel can become its own enemy' worry: if the kernel transforms its own state without constraints (K_t ->F-> K_{t+1} ->F-> K_{t+2}...), it can create self-reinforcing errors, circular reasoning, confirmation loops, unjustified certainty, loss of provenance, and contradiction propagation. Therefore Buddhi != unrestricted inference; it needs constraints, and this is where Governance becomes structurally distinct from the kernel. Also refines Buddhi's codomain away from TRUE/FALSE toward {supported, contradicted, unknown, insufficient evidence, conflicting}, framed as more compatible with the Zero/uncertainty/qualification theory.

a_rows_sample.anchor: \delta = \text{discrimination operator}
a_rows_sample.statement: Explicitly states delta = discrimination operator (i.e. Buddhi approx delta), proposing delta:X->D where D={accept,reject,uncertain,contradictory,needs evidence,needs qualification} -- an architectural hypothesis, not canonical. This directly conflicts with the same-session file S2233's explicit warning 'we should not say Buddhi=delta' (Buddhi is Evaluation/Discrimination B_t, delta is State Transition, with B_t(...)->d_t feeding a SEPARATE delta(K_t,d_t)=K_{t+1}); neither file cites or reconciles the other's position on whether Buddhi and delta are the same function or two composed functions.

a_rows_sample.anchor: B: K\times O\times C \rightarrow \{\text{Permit},\text{Reject},\text{Defer}\}
a_rows_sample.statement: From the divine quality dama (self-control): the kernel should not execute every available operation. Proposes a gatekeeper: B:KxOxC->{Permit,Reject,Defer} evaluated BEFORE delta(K,o)=K' executes (rather than delta:KxO->K' being unconditional), so delta(K,o) is applied only if permitted -- assessed as a very serious candidate for the formal kernel.

a_rows_sample.anchor: B_t: (E_t,K_t,M_t) \rightarrow \{\text{accept},\text{reject},\text{investigate},\text{suspend},\text{transform}\} ... DO NOTHING ... is itself a Buddhi decision.
a_rows_sample.statement: Formalizes Buddhi as mode-sensitive: B_t:(E_t,K_t,M_t)->{accept,reject,investigate,suspend,transform}. The same evidence E can lead to different actions depending on mode: in Sattva, E->B_S->investigate carefully; in Rajas, E->B_R->act/acquire immediately; in Tamas, E->B_T->ignore/suspend/block. Refines the earlier 'kernel always busy determining right and wrong' into: the kernel continuously evaluates the epistemic condition of its current state and determines which transitions are admissible under its current operational mode; a kernel may legitimately decide DO NOTHING because evidence is insufficient, and that itself is a Buddhi decision.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Having an evaluation mechanism \neq having correct discrimination ... B_t \neq \text{truth oracle}
a_rows_sample.statement: From Chapter 18's distinction between understanding that correctly distinguishes proper/improper action and understanding that fails to (per the modes): having an evaluation mechanism != having correct discrimination. Therefore B_t != truth oracle; Buddhi is an epistemic discriminator, not an omniscient truth machine -- assessed as much more compatible with KnowledgeOS than treating Buddhi as infallible.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Kernel correctness \neq knowledge quantity ... Kernel quality = f(\text{knowledge},\text{discrimination},\text{constraints},\text{purification})
b_rows_sample.statement: Refuses to model the 26 daivi (divine) qualities as 26 primitives; instead they reveal a quality space for kernel processing. Kernel correctness != knowledge quantity; Kernel quality = f(knowledge, discrimination, constraints, purification).

b_rows_sample.anchor: Knowledge State \downarrow Interpretation \downarrow Unqualified Proposition \downarrow False confidence \downarrow Reject contrary evidence \downarrow Knowledge State'
b_rows_sample.statement: Gives a formal interpretation of 'without governance the mind/kernel can become its own enemy': the demoniac model describes a system that forms its own conclusions, becomes attached to them, rejects external authority, acts on desire, cannot distinguish proper from improper action, and consequently reinforces its own erroneous state -- yielding a closed epistemic failure loop: Knowledge State -> Interpretation -> Unqualified Proposition -> False confidence -> Reject contrary evidence -> Knowledge State' (looping back). KnowledgeOS translation: K_t --bad discrimination--> P_t --self-reinforcement--> K_{t+1}. Hypothesis: Kernel failure superset epistemic self-reinforcement.

b_rows_sample.anchor: K\={a}ma \rightarrow goal contamination ... Krodha \rightarrow contradiction rejection ... Lobha \rightarrow knowledge accumulation without purification
b_rows_sample.statement: Reinterprets the Gita's three gates to degradation (Kama/desire, Krodha/anger, Lobha/greed) as a Zero-lens failure taxonomy, not literal software concepts: Kama -> goal contamination (Desired answer != qualified answer, reasoning optimizes for a desired answer rather than the correct one); Krodha -> contradiction rejection (K_t + not-P -> defend K_t, instead of K_t + not-P -> re-evaluate); Lobha -> knowledge accumulation without purification (|knowledge|-up does not imply knowledge-quality-up). Broadens Zero(K_t) from 'what is missing/unknown' to an epistemic-defect detector: Zero(K_t) = (missing knowledge, contradictions, uncertainty, qualification gaps, contamination) -- Zero as not merely a null-space detector but an epistemic-defect detector.

b_rows_sample.anchor: B: K\times O\times C \rightarrow \{\text{Permit},\text{Reject},\text{Defer}\}
b_rows_sample.statement: From the divine quality dama (self-control): the kernel should not execute every available operation. Proposes a gatekeeper: B:KxOxC->{Permit,Reject,Defer} evaluated BEFORE delta(K,o)=K' executes (rather than delta:KxO->K' being unconditional), so delta(K,o) is applied only if permitted -- assessed as a very serious candidate for the formal kernel.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Verify(P,E)\rightarrow \{\top,\bot,?\} ... ? \rightarrow Zero \rightarrow Gap
b_rows_sample.statement: From satyam (truthfulness), combined with Observation->Proposition->Evidence->Qualification: Verify(P,E)->{top(supported),bot(contradicted),?(unresolved)}. When the result is '?', it routes to Zero->Gap: Zero is not failure but the correct result of Buddhi refusing to pretend unresolved knowledge is resolved knowledge -- assessed as a very important KnowledgeOS principle.

b_rows_sample.anchor: \text{Śāstra/Dharma} \neq \text{KnowledgeOS Governance} ... Chapter 16 does not give us permission to put Governance inside the kernel.
b_rows_sample.statement: Distinguishes three things that must not be collapsed: Manas=processing (receives, organizes, attends), Buddhi=discrimination (true/false, supported/unsupported, admissible/inadmissible, do/not-do, known/unknown), Governance=external normative authority (determines authoritative constraints under which the kernel operates). Explicitly: Sastra/Dharma != KnowledgeOS Governance; the philosophical lens yields a normative-constraint hypothesis, while KnowledgeOS governance independently yields actual authority. Chapter 16 does not license placing Governance inside the kernel; it only suggests the kernel needs a relationship to externally defined normative constraints -- crucial given Steps 285/287.

b_rows_sample.anchor: 26 divine qualities as kernel primitives | REJECT ... Śāstra = KnowledgeOS Governance | REJECT ... Gītā establishes the KnowledgeOS algebra | REJECT
b_rows_sample.statement: Explicit findings-status table with three items marked REJECT (26 divine qualities as kernel primitives; Sastra=KnowledgeOS Governance; Gita establishes the KnowledgeOS algebra) alongside items marked strong corroboration/hypothesis/candidate (Buddhi as discrimination; kernel requires discrimination; kernel needs self-control; knowledge can degrade through self-reinforcement; Kama/Krodha/Lobha as contamination modes; Zero detects epistemic defects not only missing information; Purification != information accumulation; external normative constraint necessary but not source-derived; 26 divine qualities as kernel quality criteria, candidate).

b_rows_sample.anchor: The KnowledgeOS kernel is the smallest epistemic processing unit capable of receiving, discriminating, qualifying, and transforming knowledge-state transitions under constraints.
b_rows_sample.statement: Culminating candidate answer to 'what is the KnowledgeOS kernel actually for': the KnowledgeOS kernel is the smallest epistemic processing unit capable of receiving, discriminating, qualifying, and transforming knowledge-state transitions under constraints, with Manas=processing, Buddhi=discrimination, Zero=exposure of unresolved epistemic deficiency, delta=state transformation, and Governance=external authority/constraint (kept separate). Proposes a final operator hypothesis set: Omega:W->O (observation), M:O->X (Manas processing), B:XxC->D (Buddhi discrimination), Q:XxD->Q_t (qualification), V:Q_t->{top,bot,?} (verification), Z:X->G (Zero/gap detection), delta:KxO->K' (state transformation) -- explicitly candidate, not canonical; Chapter 16 supplies philosophical evidence and hypotheses only, mathematics/corpus/DDD/Governance still validate each candidate.

b_aliases: Chapter 16 divine vs demoniac qualities reading
kernel quality model / anti-pattern failure vector

group_evidence.why_grouped: explicit agent-stated uncertainty: 'hpa-gita-chapter16-daivi-asuri-kernel-quality-model' POSSIBLY relates to 'hpa-buddhi-discrimination-second-pass' (batch B0054). Note: Disciplined hpa reading of Gita Chapter 16 (divine vs demoniac qualities) treated as a candidate source of KERNEL CONTROL SEMANTICS, not new primitives. Explicitly rejects modeling the 26 divine qualities (or Sastra/Dharma=Governance, or the Gita establishing the algebra) as primitives/architecture, but proposes a kernel quality model (26-item Gita-term-to-KnowledgeOS-property table) and its corresponding anti-pattern failure vector F_t. Central contributions: a closed epistemic self-reinforcement failure loop explaining 'kernel can become its own enemy'; a Kama/Krodha/Lobha Zero-lens contamination taxonomy (goal contamination, contradiction rejection, unpurified accumulation); Zero broadened from a null-space detector to an epistemic-defect detector; a Buddhi-as-gatekeeper operator B:KxOxC->{Permit,Reject,Defer} preceding delta; a Verify(P,E)->{top,bot,?} operator with the principle ?->Zero->Gap (Zero as Buddhi correctly refusing to pretend unresolved knowledge is resolved); and a final formal operator hypothesis set {Omega,M,B,Q,V,Z,delta}.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Closure(K_4) size 18 of 29 blocked 15 unblocked 3. published: 18 constructs / 15 blocked -> REPRODUCED. ... Closure(K_9) size 20 of 29 blocked 17 unblocked 3. published: 20 constructs -> REPRODUCED. ... published: INCOMPARABLE -> REPRODUCED. ... reached ONLY via its own seed. The degeneracy warning
a_rows_sample.statement: Sections 1-5: the independent direct-import verification reproduces the published K4 control (18 of 29 constructs, 15 blocked), the published K9 closure under the review lane's declared mapping (20 of 29, 17 blocked, from 10 named seeds), the published incomparability finding (neither Closure(K4) nor Closure(K9) is a subset of the other, with K4\K9={History,Rejection,Replay}, K9\K4={Assessment,Authority,Authorization,Determination,Qualification}, 15 in the intersection, 6 reached by neither), confirms the Qualification degeneracy warning is correct (Qualification is reached only via its own C-7 seed, not independently), and reproduces all five published one-at-a-time mapping-sensitivity closure sizes (C-1->16, C-2->20, C-4->21, C-5->20, C-6->22).

a_rows_sample.anchor: Independent verification of 2026-09-06-KOS-K9-CLOSURE-CONDITIONAL-DEPENDENCY-COMPUTATION.md. Uses the SOURCE program's graph and closure procedure by direct import -- not the review lane's transcription -- so the check is independent of that transcription. Read-only. Asserts nothing about kernel min
a_rows_sample.statement: Header and structure: implements an independent verification of the K9-closure conditional-dependency computation document by directly importing the original minimum_implementable.py module's graph G and closure() function (bypassing any risk of a transcription error in the review lane's own copy of that graph), then re-derives K4 and K9 seed sets and reruns seven numbered checks against the document's own published numbers: (1) K4 control reproduces 18/29 with 15 blocked; (2) K9 closure under the declared mapping; (3) incomparability of Closure(K4) and Closure(K9); (4) whether Qualification's presence in Closure(K9) is definitional (tested by removing C-7's seed and rechecking); (5) one-at-a-time mapping sensitivity against five published per-row closure sizes; (6) the full product over all five perturbable rows, checking the published 15..22 range claim; (7) whether O_core enters the closure through a single row only.

b_rows_sample.anchor: This is NOT a proof of kernel minimality, and the result is NOT 'the minimum kernel.' ... K9 has necessity relative to the ratified canon ... Its sufficiency is untested, and 88 of the 99 contract cells ... are empty. ... The headline is negative. The computation does not converge on a kernel ... th
b_rows_sample.statement: Sections 0-1: computes the transitive dependency closure of the derived 9-capability basis K9={C-1..C-9} over the 29-construct graph G (reproduced verbatim from minimum_implementable.py) and compares it against the stipulated 4-capability basis K4's closure; states explicitly under what authorization this was permitted -- treated as a conditional dependency computation, never as a kernel-minimality proof, since K9 has necessity only relative to the ratified canon and its sufficiency is untested (88 of 99 contract cells empty); reproduces the source program's published control result exactly (Closure(K4)=18 constructs, 15 blocked), verifying the graph transcription; states the headline finding is negative -- the computation does not converge on a kernel, and shows the previously reported closure was an artifact of the stipulated basis, with the kernel requirement-set's size not determined by the corpus at all.
