a_rows_sample.anchor: The fundamental distinction ... Evidence Strength \neq Information Gain \neq Decision Value ... How strongly does an evidence item support a proposition? ... How much does the evidence reduce uncertainty? ... How much does acquiring the evidence improve the decision?
a_rows_sample.statement: Separates three related-but-distinct quantities: Evidence Strength (support magnitude), Information Gain (uncertainty reduction), and Decision Value (improvement to the decision from acquiring the evidence).

a_rows_sample.anchor: Can Nexus be migrated safely? ... Version = 3.69 ... Knowing the exact patch version may add little information. ... Is the production blob store backed up? ... may currently be completely unknown. A single answer could dramatically reduce the migration uncertainty. Highest Evidence Strength \neq Hi
a_rows_sample.statement: Illustrates with a migration-safety question that a strongly-evidenced fact (Nexus version) can add little new information, while an unknown backup-status question could dramatically reduce uncertainty with a single answer — Highest Evidence Strength ≠ Highest Information Gain.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Information gain in information theory ... H(P) = -\sum_x P(x)\log P(x) ... P(P)=0.5 then H(P)=1 bit ... P(P\mid e)=0.95 and H(P\mid e)<H(P) ... IG(e;P) = H(P)-H(P\mid e). This is a mathematically rigorous definition of information gain.
a_rows_sample.statement: Defines entropy-based information gain IG(e;P)=H(P)-H(P|e) using Shannon entropy H(P)=-Σ P(x)log P(x), worked with a 0.5→0.95 probability update as a rigorous but calculus-specific definition.

a_rows_sample.anchor: But this is not universal ... Entropy requires a probabilistic representation. ... unknown values; logical constraints; competing assertions; qualitative uncertainty; argument graphs; incomplete evidence. Therefore we should not define IG=EntropyReduction as a universal KnowledgeOS law. InformationG
a_rows_sample.statement: Corrects the previous entropy definition's universality: entropy requires a probabilistic representation, which KnowledgeOS often lacks (unknown values, logical constraints, argument graphs), so IG=EntropyReduction must not be a universal law — InformationGain_ρ is policy-specific.

a_rows_sample.anchor: General definition ... discrepancy function D(S,I,P) ... IG_D(e) = D(S_t,I_t,P) - D(S_{t+1}^{(e)},I_t,P) ... Information gain can be measured as reduction in discrepancy.
a_rows_sample.statement: Generalizes information gain beyond entropy: IG_D(e)=D(S_t,I_t,P)-D(S_{t+1}^(e),I_t,P), i.e. information gain measured as reduction in a discrepancy function relative to the Ideal State.

a_rows_sample.anchor: But there is an important complication ... We usually don't know in advance what evidence e will reveal. ... Yes; No; Unknown; "Backups exist but have never been tested." Therefore we need expected information gain. ... EIG(e) = \sum_{o\in O_e} Pr(o\mid e,K_t)[D(K_t,I_t,P)-D(K_{t+1}^{o},I_t,P)]
a_rows_sample.statement: Notes evidence outcomes are unknown in advance (e.g. a yes/no/unknown/qualified backup-status answer), requiring Expected Information Gain EIG(e)=Σ_o Pr(o|e,K_t)[D(K_t,I_t,P)-D(K_{t+1}^o,I_t,P)] over possible outcomes o.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Expected discrepancy reduction ... EDR(e) = \mathbb E[D(K_t,I_t,P)-D(K_{t+1},I_t,P)\mid e] ... This does not require us to call it information theory. It can be used with deterministic gap counts; probabilistic uncertainty; belief functions; argumentation; domain-specific discrepancy measures.
a_rows_sample.statement: Defines Expected Discrepancy Reduction EDR(e)=E[D(K_t,I_t,P)-D(K_{t+1},I_t,P)|e], deliberately framework-neutral so it can be instantiated with deterministic gap counts, probability, belief functions, argumentation, or other domain-specific discrepancy measures.

a_rows_sample.anchor: This is probably more fundamental for KnowledgeOS ... ExpectedDiscrepancyReduction more fundamental than EntropyReduction ... KnowledgeOS is not merely trying to reduce uncertainty. It is trying to move K_t toward I_t. Therefore the natural objective is K_t\rightarrow I_t and not merely H(K_t)\right
a_rows_sample.statement: Argues ExpectedDiscrepancyReduction is more fundamental to KnowledgeOS than EntropyReduction, since KnowledgeOS's real objective is moving K_t toward I_t, not merely driving entropy to zero.

a_rows_sample.anchor: A critical counterexample ... P(A)=0.5 and P(B)=0.5 ... A is irrelevant to the current decision. Then IG(A)>0 but EDR(A)\approx0. Meanwhile evidence about B might directly resolve a Critical Gap. InformationGain\neq PurposeValue. This is why purpose P must remain in the equation.
a_rows_sample.statement: Gives a counterexample where entropy-reducing evidence about an irrelevant proposition A has high IG but near-zero EDR, while evidence about a decision-relevant proposition B would resolve a critical gap — InformationGain ≠ PurposeValue, so purpose must remain in the equation.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Value of Evidence ... VOE_\rho(e\mid K_t,I_t,P,C) ... the expected value of acquiring evidence e ... VOE(e) = ExpectedDiscrepancyReduction(e) \times DecisionImpact(e) ... this multiplication is not a universal law. It is one possible policy.
a_rows_sample.statement: Defines Value of Evidence VOE_ρ(e|K_t,I_t,P,C) as the expected value of acquiring e, offering EDR(e)×DecisionImpact(e) as one possible (non-universal) policy decomposition.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Cost must also be included ... Evidence A ... 0.9 ... €10,000 ... Evidence B ... 0.7 ... €10 ... Clearly, "maximum information gain" alone is insufficient. We need Cost(e) and potentially Time(e), Risk(e), Effort(e)
a_rows_sample.statement: Shows via a cost/benefit contrast (Evidence A: EDR 0.9 at €10,000 vs Evidence B: EDR 0.7 at €10) that maximizing information gain alone is insufficient — Cost, Time, Risk, and Effort must also enter the evaluation.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Utility of evidence ... U_\rho(e) = Benefit_\rho(e) - Cost_\rho(e) ... U(e) = \alpha EDR(e) + \beta DecisionImpact(e) - \gamma Cost(e) - \delta Time(e) ... the coefficients \alpha,\beta,\gamma,\delta are policy parameters. They are not mathematical truths.
a_rows_sample.statement: Defines evidence utility U_ρ(e)=Benefit_ρ(e)-Cost_ρ(e), with a worked linear form U(e)=αEDR(e)+βDecisionImpact(e)-γCost(e)-δTime(e) whose coefficients are explicitly labeled policy parameters, not mathematical truths.

a_rows_sample.anchor: The evidence acquisition problem ... \mathcal Q ... Q1 = inspect filesystem ... Q8 = ask LLM to extract information ... q^* = \arg\max_{q\in\mathcal Q} U_\rho(q\mid K_t,I_t,P) ... This is potentially one of the most important equations in the whole KnowledgeOS theory.
a_rows_sample.statement: Formalizes Lord's core problem as q*=argmax_{q∈Q} U_ρ(q|K_t,I_t,P) over a candidate acquisition-action set Q (inspect filesystem, query API, read document, ask engineer, inspect backup config, run test, search internet, ask LLM) — called potentially one of the most important equations in the whole theory.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Lord's role becomes precise ... Lord(K_t,I_t,P,\rho) \rightarrow RankedCandidateAcquisitions ... Candidate 1 Inspect production backup configuration Expected discrepancy reduction: High Cost: Low Risk: Low
a_rows_sample.statement: Formalizes Lord as Lord(K_t,I_t,P,ρ)→RankedCandidateAcquisitions, illustrated with a ranked candidate list (inspect backup config / ask infra owner / search internet) each carrying EDR/Cost/Risk estimates.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Sarathi then chooses or guides ... Lord generates the candidate space. Sārathi considers current constraints; available capabilities; urgency; policy; safety; dependencies; human authority. Sārathi : Candidates \rightarrow NextAction ... Lord = option generation/ranking ... Sārathi = action guidance
a_rows_sample.statement: Distinguishes Lord (option generation/ranking) from Sārathi (Candidates→NextAction, factoring in constraints/urgency/policy/safety/dependencies/human authority) as separate roles.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Zero has a different role ... Zero(K_t,I_t) \rightarrow \Delta_t ... Lord(\Delta_t) \rightarrow Q ... Sārathi(Q,constraints) \rightarrow a_t ... This gives us a very elegant cycle: Knowledge K_t → Zero → Δ_t → Lord → candidates → Sārathi → action → Evidence Acquisition → New Knowledge K_t+1 → Zero
a_rows_sample.statement: Assembles the full Zero→Lord→Sārathi cycle: Zero(K_t,I_t)→Δ_t, Lord(Δ_t)→Q (candidates), Sārathi(Q,constraints)→a_t (action), producing new evidence and K_{t+1}, feeding back into Zero.

a_rows_sample.anchor: This is much more than RAG ... Question \rightarrow Retrieve \rightarrow Generate ... Purpose \rightarrow IdealState \rightarrow Discrepancy \rightarrow EvidenceValue \rightarrow AcquisitionPlan \rightarrow Evidence \rightarrow Assessment \rightarrow KnowledgeState. That is a fundamentally different
a_rows_sample.statement: Contrasts traditional RAG's Question→Retrieve→Generate pipeline with KnowledgeOS's Purpose→IdealState→Discrepancy→EvidenceValue→AcquisitionPlan→Evidence→Assessment→KnowledgeState pipeline as a fundamentally different architecture.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Human research fits naturally ... q=HumanInquiry ... HumanResponse\rightarrow Evidence ... Acquisition=Reported ... Source=Human ... The human's statement does not automatically become truth. It enters exactly the same evidence machinery.
a_rows_sample.statement: Shows human inquiry fits the same acquisition/evidence machinery (q=HumanInquiry → HumanResponse→Evidence with Acquisition=Reported, Source=Human), with the human's statement not automatically becoming truth.

a_rows_sample.anchor: LLM output also fits ... LLM(D)\rightarrow e ... Acquisition=Inferred ... Parent=D ... LLMOutput\neq GroundTruth ... LLMOutput\neq IndependentEvidence when it derives from existing evidence. This is one of the major architectural strengths of the model.
a_rows_sample.statement: Shows LLM output fits the same graph (LLM(D)→e with Acquisition=Inferred, Parent=D), reaffirming LLMOutput ≠ GroundTruth and LLMOutput ≠ IndependentEvidence when derived from existing evidence.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Experimental evidence ... Hypothesis: Nexus backup can be restored. Experiment: Restore backup to isolated environment. Observation: Restore succeeded. Evidence: e_exp ... Acquisition(e)=Observed with provenance Experiment\rightarrow Observation. This can have much higher relevance to a migration de
a_rows_sample.statement: Models experimental evidence (Hypothesis/Experiment/Observation/Evidence, e.g. restoring a backup to an isolated environment) with Acquisition=Observed and provenance Experiment→Observation, noted as potentially higher relevance than a textual claim.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Collect evidence that has high information value relative to the current uncertainty. ... Which observation would most reduce uncertainty? rather than: What documents can I find?
b_rows_sample.statement: Evidence acquisition should be directed by expected information value relative to current uncertainty (active-learning-like), grounded in the book's expert-perception discussion that experts know where useful information will appear; called possibly one of the most important design principles for future KnowledgeOS agents.

b_rows_sample.anchor: An AI agent can search 500 documents, extract 10,000 facts, generate 50 claims, and still reduce uncertainty by almost nothing. ... Activity ≠ Learning ... More evidence ≠ More knowledge.
b_rows_sample.statement: Chinese-lens warning against confusing movement with progress: high-volume AI agent activity can reduce uncertainty by almost nothing; the correct test is whether evidence changed justified understanding of the situation, not how much evidence was processed.

b_rows_sample.anchor: 82.46 — Value of information returns ... VOI=ExpectedImprovement-CostOfInformation. This links Step 75 and Step 82. KnowledgeOS can prioritize evidence acquisition based on its expected decision impact.
b_rows_sample.statement: Restates Value of Information VOI = ExpectedImprovement - CostOfInformation, explicitly linking Step 75's VOI concept to Step 82's uncertainty-propagation framework for prioritizing evidence acquisition.

b_rows_sample.anchor: 82.47 — Experiment 23 ... Investigation A costs €1,000, expected value €10,000 decision change. Investigation B costs €1,000 but almost never changes the decision. Expected: A has higher information value. Result: PASS
b_rows_sample.statement: Experiment 23: comparing two equal-cost investigations, A (high expected decision-change value) correctly has higher information value than B (rarely changes the decision); result PASS.

b_rows_sample.anchor: 90.37 — Computational economics ... C_compute. B_decision. VOI=ExpectedValueOfInformation. Compute further only when VOI>C_compute or when governance requires the computation regardless of economic value.
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines computational economics: compute further only when VOI>C_compute, or when governance mandates the computation regardless of economic value.

b_rows_sample.anchor: 98.13 — Value of information ... VOI(I)=ExpectedDecisionImprovement-Cost(I). If VOI(I)>0, additional information may be worthwhile.
b_rows_sample.statement: Restates Value of Information VOI(I)=ExpectedDecisionImprovement-Cost(I) as the criterion for seeking more information.

b_rows_sample.anchor: 98.14 — Experiment 6 ... Decision uncertainty is high. A 5-minute automated check can significantly reduce uncertainty. Expected: VOI>0. KnowledgeOS should consider performing it. Result: PASS
b_rows_sample.statement: Experiment 6: a cheap, high-uncertainty-reducing check has VOI>0 and should be performed; result PASS.

b_rows_sample.anchor: 98.15 — Experiment 7 ... A two-week investigation is required to reduce a tiny uncertainty in a low-impact decision. Expected: VOI<0. The investigation may not be justified. Result: PASS
b_rows_sample.statement: Experiment 7: an expensive investigation for a tiny uncertainty reduction in a low-impact decision has VOI<0 and may be unjustified; result PASS.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Authorization boundary. This lane is not authorized to canonize a KnowledgeOS kernel. No result below may be promoted to invariant, theorem, ADR or standard by this document.
a_rows_sample.statement: States the experiment's binding authorization boundary: it is explicitly research-only, not authorized to canonize a kernel, and no result may be promoted to invariant/theorem/ADR/standard by the document itself.

a_rows_sample.anchor: What this experiment is NOT: a naming exercise ... a retrofit of the current architecture: Part XXIV "existing class != domain primitive" — no architectural circularity ... a canonization.
a_rows_sample.statement: Enumerates six things the experiment explicitly is not (naming exercise, aesthetic minimization, a vote, a universal-necessity proof, an architectural retrofit/circularity, or a canonization), each tied to a concrete safeguard already built into the executed model.

a_rows_sample.anchor: They disagree for Select, Discriminate, and Revise. Those disagreements are results, not defects.
a_rows_sample.statement: Reports, as an executed finding, that the three distinct necessity notions (empirically necessary, formally necessary via the reach algebra, and DDD-necessary as a distinct domain responsibility) disagree for the operators Select, Discriminate, and Revise, explicitly framing the disagreement itself as a valid experimental result rather than a flaw in the model.

a_rows_sample.anchor: The experiment targets B + C. A result that improves A while worsening B/C is reported as a worse result, per the protocol's final principle.
a_rows_sample.statement: Confirms semantic minimality (B) and compositional minimality (C) as the experiment's primary targets, with cardinality (A) explicitly subordinate: an improvement in operator count that worsens semantic or compositional minimality is scored as a worse result overall.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Modification M-1 — C25 added [CORPUS]. ... Without C25, C10 is unrealizable in any model where a Verdict requires evidence ... This modification enlarges the required capability set and therefore makes minimization harder, not easier.
a_rows_sample.statement: Adds a new capability C25 ('admit an observation as evidence under a policy') to the protocol's original 24-item list, justified because the corpus's Qualify:Observation x Policy -> Evidence gap (G1) combined with prior constraint 9 (information != evidence) means no capability in C1-C24 covers the observation-to-evidence transition, making C10 (validate) unrealizable without it -- explicitly noted as making minimization harder, not more convenient.

a_rows_sample.anchor: C18 reclassified as NON-DISCRIMINATING [NEG]. ... no operator set can fail C18 in this simulator. ... This is a limitation of the instrument, not a finding about the kernel.
a_rows_sample.statement: Reclassifies capability C18 (preserve provenance) as non-discriminating because the reach engine structurally guarantees provenance via its derivation DAG for every artifact regardless of operator set, making it untestable by leave-one-out -- explicitly reported as a limitation of the measuring instrument, not a substantive finding about the kernel.

a_rows_sample.anchor: C20 given an explicit failure mode: the system must be able to hold >=2 hypotheses and return an UNDECIDED discrimination. It can then fail by overreach — producing a Determination while unable to represent the alternatives it is determining between.
a_rows_sample.statement: Operationalizes the under-specified capability C20 (support non-identifiability) with a concrete, falsifiable failure mode (overreach: producing a Determination without being able to represent >=2 held alternatives with an UNDECIDED verdict), preventing the capability from being trivially 'supported' by doing nothing.

a_rows_sample.anchor: merge C2 and C3 (meaning + representation) | corpus explicitly separates Observation != Proposition != Knowledge; merging is tested instead as robustness variant V1 ... merge C12 and C13 (determine + select) | different carriers, different inputs (Inquiry vs Objective); tested as V5
a_rows_sample.statement: Reports two considered-and-rejected capability-model modifications (merging meaning-construction with representation; merging determination with action-selection), each rejected on corpus-grounded or type-grounded reasons but retained as explicit robustness variants (V1, V5) to be tested rather than silently discarded.

a_rows_sample.anchor: An operator IS its declared set of semantic atoms ... 'redefine Y so that Y also does X' is mechanically detectable — it is a change to Y's atom set, i.e. a change to the model, not a composition within it -> SMUGGLING = TRUE.
a_rows_sample.statement: Defines the anti-circularity device at the heart of the executed experiment: an operator is identified purely by its declared set of semantic atoms, consulted by the reach engine to the exclusion of operator names, so that redefining one operator to secretly absorb another's function becomes a detectable change to the atom-set model itself (SMUGGLING=TRUE) rather than a legitimate composition.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Atoms are deliberately allowed to be shared. A 1:1 operator->atom assignment would make every operator irreducible by construction and the experiment vacuous. Two atoms are shared ... and that sharing is where all the interesting results live.
a_rows_sample.statement: Explains why two atoms (difference-decision, norm-comparison) are deliberately shared between operators rather than assigning each operator a unique atom: a strict 1:1 mapping would make every operator trivially irreducible by construction, rendering the whole ablation experiment vacuous -- the shared atoms are identified as the source of the experiment's most interesting results.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Structural concerns (context, time, uncertainty, assumption, provenance, alternatives) are modelled as invariants checked over the reach closure ... not as ownable powers. Making them ownable would have handed one operator a monopoly on, e.g., provenance, and rigged the result.
a_rows_sample.statement: States that structural concerns (context/time/uncertainty/assumptions/provenance/alternatives) are deliberately modelled as invariants checked over the whole reach closure rather than as atoms any single operator could own, to avoid rigging the ablation result by handing one operator an artificial monopoly on a cross-cutting concern.

a_rows_sample.anchor: difference-decision ∈ {Discriminate, DetectGap}; norm-comparison ∈ {DetectGap, Determine}. DetectGap holds no atom exclusively. ... it is the assumption most responsible for the headline result, and it is therefore attacked directly by robustness variant V4.
a_rows_sample.statement: Identifies DetectGap as the only operator in C0-union-Qualify holding no atom exclusively (both its atoms, difference-decision and norm-comparison, are shared with Discriminate and Determine respectively), flagging this modelling choice as the single assumption most responsible for the experiment's headline redundancy result, and explicitly scheduling it for direct attack under robustness variant V4.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Observe | world-contact | the sole channel for empirical content; nothing downstream may create it | STRONG ... Represent | symbolic-encoding | make semantic content manipulable without asserting it | WEAK ... Qualify | evidential-qualification | admit an observation as evidence under a policy | STR
a_rows_sample.statement: Reports the full per-operator contract table (13 C0 operators plus Qualify), each with its claimed atom(s), non-reducible responsibility, and a corpus-support grade from STRONG (Observe, Discriminate-as-family, Validate, Revise, Qualify) through MODERATE (Interpret, Infer, DetectGap, Challenge, Determine) to WEAK (Represent, Hypothesize, Relate, Select).

a_rows_sample.anchor: Discriminate and DetectGap are all-zero rows. Neither is required by any capability under leave-one-out, because each covers the other's shared atoms. That is not evidence that the capabilities are unneeded — it is evidence that the operator packaging is redundant.
a_rows_sample.statement: States the experiment's headline finding: Discriminate and DetectGap are both all-zero rows in the leave-one-out operator-capability matrix, since each can cover the other's shared atoms when the other is removed -- explicitly interpreted not as evidence the underlying capabilities are unneeded but as evidence that the CURRENT OPERATOR PACKAGING of those capabilities is redundant.

a_rows_sample.anchor: C5 | {Discriminate, DetectGap} both removed | the atom difference-decision. C8 | {Discriminate, DetectGap} or {DetectGap, Determine} removed | difference-decision + norm-comparison. A leave-one-out matrix alone would have declared C5 and C8 unnecessary. They are not.
a_rows_sample.statement: Reports that capabilities C5 (discriminate alternatives) and C8 (detect epistemic insufficiency) are all-zero columns under leave-one-out and become irreducible only under pairwise ablation (C5 lost only when both Discriminate and DetectGap are removed together; C8 lost when either {Discriminate,DetectGap} or {DetectGap,Determine} are removed together), concretely demonstrating that a leave-one-out-only analysis would have wrongly certified both capabilities as unnecessary.

a_rows_sample.anchor: A carrier kind is not stamped by the operator that produced it. It is derived from (multiset of input kinds, atoms introduced by this step) -> kind ... Otherwise 'only DetectGap can make a Gap' would be true by fiat and the ablation rigged.
a_rows_sample.statement: Defines a second anti-circularity device: a derived carrier's kind is determined purely by its input-kind multiset and the atoms introduced, never by which operator produced it, so that any operator set capable of introducing the required atoms over the required inputs can produce a given carrier -- preventing the ablation from being rigged by fiat operator-carrier ownership.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Claim is producible only via entailment — so its warrant kind is DEDUCTIVE by construction. A Verdict produced by generate-and-test is not a Claim. This is what keeps Infer =?= Validate-compose-Hypothesize an honest question rather than a definitional trick.
a_rows_sample.statement: Establishes, from the carrier-derivation table's type rules, that a Claim can only be produced via the entailment atom (making its warrant kind deductive by construction) while a Verdict produced by generate-and-test (Hypothesize then Validate) is a structurally different carrier -- keeping the composition question 'is Infer equivalent to Validate composed with Hypothesize' a genuinely open, honest question rather than one settled by definition.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Verdict requires Evidence. This is where the absence of Qualify from C0 becomes fatal. ... Determination requires both NormDelta (hence IdealState) and Inquiry — encoding prior constraint 5, that the Ideal State is inquiry-relative.
a_rows_sample.statement: Derives from the type system that a Verdict carrier requires an Evidence input, making the corpus's unimplemented Qualify operator (excluded from C0) fatal to realizing validation without it; separately derives that a Determination carrier requires both a NormDelta (itself requiring IdealState) and an Inquiry, formally encoding the prior constraint that the Ideal State is inquiry-relative directly into the type system rather than merely asserting it.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Reach(S) = mu A . AMBIENT union {k | exists o in S : k in derive(A, o.atoms)}. Monotone, terminating (finite carrier set), and independent of operator names.
a_rows_sample.statement: Formalizes Reach(S) as the least fixpoint (over a finite carrier set, hence terminating and monotone) of applying available operators' atoms to the ambient carriers, with a capability achieved iff its required carrier kinds and atoms are both covered by Reach(S) and the atom pool of S -- the operational definition of formal necessity used throughout the experiment.

a_rows_sample.anchor: No helper functions. ... No helper performs the work of a removed operator — a claim that is mechanically checkable, since helpers cannot introduce atoms.
a_rows_sample.statement: States that the reach engine's implementation contains only domain-operator applications plus generic data-structure operations (set union, fixpoint computation), with every helper function classified per the protocol's requirement, and that no helper can perform the work of a removed operator because helpers structurally cannot introduce atoms -- making the no-semantic-smuggling guarantee mechanically checkable rather than merely asserted.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Do not define Knowledge Space merely as an infinite set of knowledge elements, and do not define it directly as a probability space. Define it first as a measurable space of possible epistemic configurations. Probability, filtration, conditional assessment, and trajectories are additional structures built on top of it.
b_rows_sample.statement: States the file's central recommendation superseding earlier candidate definitions: Knowledge Space must be defined first as a measurable space of possible epistemic configurations, never directly as a probability space nor as a bare set of knowledge elements; probability, filtration, conditional assessment and trajectories are all additional structures layered on top.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Let \(J\) be an index set of admissible epistemic observables. For every j in J, define a measurable value space (V_j,B_j). An epistemic observable is a map $$Y_j:\Omega\rightarrow\mathcal V_j$$ ... observable != knowledge and observable != dimension automatically.
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines Epistemic Observable: for an index set J of admissible epistemic observables, each j in J has a measurable value space (V_j,B_j) and an observable map Y_j:Omega->V_j extracting an epistemically meaningful aspect of a state (worked examples: OS, RAM, Port); explicitly non-identical to knowledge or to dimension, preserving a Sentence->Proposition->Observable->Value chain.

b_rows_sample.anchor: define the **epistemic configuration space** $$\mathcal X=\prod_{j\in J}\mathcal V_j$$ with product σ-field $$\mathscr A=\bigotimes_{j\in J}\mathscr B_j.$$ Thus (X,A) is the **measurable Knowledge Space**. ... not (X,A,P). Probability comes later.
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines the Knowledge-State Space as the product X = product over j in J of V_j with the product sigma-field A = tensor product of B_j, giving the measurable Knowledge Space (X,A) explicitly WITHOUT a probability measure attached -- probability is deferred to a later, separate definition.

b_rows_sample.anchor: $$A_{\mathrm{RHEL9.8}}=\pi_{\mathrm{OS}}^{-1}(\{\mathrm{RHEL9.8}\}).$$ Proposition != Epistemic Event != Probability. A proposition has semantic content. An event is a measurable mathematical subset. A probability is a numerical measure assigned to that event.
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines an Epistemic Event as a measurable subset A in the sigma-field A (worked as a coordinate-projection preimage), giving a precise three-way non-collapse Proposition != Epistemic Event != Probability: a proposition has semantic content, an event is a measurable mathematical subset, and a probability is a numerical measure assigned to that event.

b_rows_sample.anchor: $$C_t=\{x\in\mathcal X: \pi_1(x)=a_1,\pi_2(x)=a_2,\pi_3(x)=a_3\}$$ ... a **finite-dimensional cylinder**. ... Unknown coordinate = coordinate not constrained by current epistemic information. Therefore: Unknown != False and Unknown != Zero probability.
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines Partial Knowledge via a finite-dimensional cylinder set C_t (constraining finitely many coordinates while leaving the rest of X unrestricted), giving a rigorous definition of 'unknown coordinate' as one not constrained by current epistemic information -- reinforcing Unknown != False and Unknown != Zero-probability with a concrete measure-theoretic construction, stronger than merely storing an 'unknown' database value.

b_rows_sample.anchor: define a representation map $$\Gamma:\mathcal K\rightarrow\mathscr A$$ ... $$\Gamma(K_t)\in\mathscr A$$ as the set of epistemic configurations compatible with K_t. ... possible configuration != current epistemic knowledge about that configuration.
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines the Knowledge State via a representation map Gamma: K -> A mapping each admissible Knowledge State K_t (from the separate space K of admissible Knowledge States) to its compatibility region Gamma(K_t) in A (the set of epistemic configurations consistent with it) -- a major improvement over simply writing K_t in X, since it distinguishes a possible configuration from current epistemic knowledge ABOUT that configuration.

b_rows_sample.anchor: $$\mathcal F_t=\sigma(\text{all epistemically available observables through }t).$$ Then F_0 subset F_1 subset ... is a filtration. ... Evidence is a collection. F_t is the **closure of measurable information generated by that collection**.
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines Epistemic Information as a sigma-field filtration F_t=sigma(all epistemically available observables through t) with F_0 subset F_1 subset ..., explicitly distinguished from a bare evidence collection E_t={e_1,...,e_n}: F_t is the closure of measurable information generated by that collection, a strictly stronger object.

b_rows_sample.anchor: $$\Pi_t=\mathcal L(Z\mid\mathcal F_t).$$ Here Pi_t is a conditional distribution. ... but: Pi_t != K_t. This is crucial. Probability describes uncertainty. Knowledge describes the semantically determined epistemic state.
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines Epistemic Assessment Pi_t=L(Z|F_t) as the conditional distribution of a latent measurable state variable Z given available information F_t, on an underlying probability space (Omega,G,P) -- explicitly Pi_t != K_t: probability describes uncertainty while Knowledge describes the semantically determined epistemic state.

b_rows_sample.anchor: $$K_t=\Phi(\mathcal F_t,\Pi_t,Q_t,C_t,S_t,M_t,H_t)$$ ... this equation must remain **[PROP]**, not theorem. ... measure theory does **not** derive the semantic transformation Phi.
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines Knowledge Construction as K_t = Phi(F_t, Pi_t, Q_t, C_t, S_t, M_t, H_t) (information, probabilistic assessment, inquiry, context, knower standpoint, model/assumptions, alternatives), explicitly held as [PROP] not theorem since measure theory does not and cannot derive the semantic transformation function Phi itself.

b_rows_sample.anchor: $$P_t(A)=P(Z\in A\mid\mathcal F_t)$$ for A in A. But we must **not** write: P_t(K)=amount of knowledge. Nor: P_t(K)=truth. Nor: P_t(K)=confidence. ... Probability != Knowledge.
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines Knowledge Probability P_t(A)=P(Z in A|F_t) for measurable A, while explicitly forbidding the interpretations P_t(K)=amount-of-knowledge, P_t(K)=truth, or P_t(K)=confidence -- restating Probability != Knowledge as a standing constraint on this new formal apparatus.

b_rows_sample.anchor: $$I_t=I(Q_t,C_t,S_t,EC_t)$$ ... Thus I_t in K rather than necessarily I_t in X. ... Ideal Knowledge State != complete Knowledge Space. The ideal state is what is sufficient for an inquiry. It is not "everything that could possibly be known."
b_rows_sample.statement: Types the Ideal Knowledge State I_t=I(Q_t,C_t,S_t,EC_t) as living in the space of admissible Knowledge States K (not necessarily in the raw configuration space X), explicitly reinforcing Ideal Knowledge State != complete Knowledge Space: the ideal state is what is sufficient for an inquiry, not everything possibly knowable.

b_rows_sample.anchor: The improved definition is a typed discrepancy operator: $$\Delta_t=D(K_t,I_t;Q_t,C_t,EC_t)$$ with codomain Delta_t in G ... We should **not yet assume** that G=R. A candidate decomposition is: $$\Delta_t=(\Delta_t^{content},\Delta_t^{uncertainty},\Delta_t^{model},\Delta_t^{observability},\Delta_t^{requirement})$$
b_rows_sample.statement: Replaces the invalid S_t*-K_t set-subtraction Knowledge Gap formula with a typed discrepancy operator Delta_t=D(K_t,I_t;Q_t,C_t,EC_t) whose codomain G is explicitly not assumed to be the real numbers, with a candidate five-component decomposition (content, uncertainty, model, observability, requirement) offered as [PROP].

b_rows_sample.anchor: $$Zero(K_t,I_t,EC_t)\iff K_t\models EC_t$$ or equivalently: $$Zero_t=1\iff Adequate(K_t,Q_t,C_t,EC_t).$$ Zero is therefore a **predicate**, not a probability. ... Zero != P(A)=0.
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines Zero formally as an indicator predicate: Zero(K_t,I_t,EC_t) iff K_t satisfies (models) the epistemic contract EC_t, equivalently Zero_t=1 iff Adequate(K_t,Q_t,C_t,EC_t) -- explicitly a predicate, not a probability, reinforcing Zero != P(A)=0 using the infinite-coin-toss warning against conflating point-probability-zero with epistemic absence.

b_rows_sample.anchor: $$T_t:(K_t,\mathcal F_t,E_{t+1},Q_t,C_t)\longrightarrow K_{t+1}.$$ If the transition is deterministic ... If it is uncertain, define a probability kernel: $$T_t(k,A)=P(K_{t+1}\in A\mid K_t=k,\mathcal F_t,E_{t+1},Q_t,C_t).$$
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines Epistemic Transition T_t either as a deterministic function (K_t,F_t,E_{t+1},Q_t,C_t) -> K_{t+1} or, if uncertain, as a probability transition kernel T_t(k,A)=P(K_{t+1} in A | K_t=k, F_t, E_{t+1}, Q_t, C_t), directly compatible with Tulcea's-theorem-style construction of an infinite process from an initial distribution and successive kernels.

b_rows_sample.anchor: $$\Omega_K=\prod_{t=0}^{\infty}\mathcal X_t.$$ A trajectory is omega_K=(K_0,K_1,K_2,...). ... coordinate projection is pi_t(omega_K)=K_t. ... History != Current State. ... (Omega_K, A_K, P_K) is the **Knowledge-process probability space**. ... rather than calling Knowledge Space itself a probability space.
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines the Knowledge Trajectory Space Omega_K = product over t of X_t with trajectories omega_K=(K_0,K_1,...) and coordinate projections K_t=pi_t(omega_K), giving History != Current State a rigorous construction; the resulting (Omega_K, A_K, P_K), when a trajectory probability law exists, is named the Knowledge-process probability space -- the correct place for the phrase 'infinite probability space', never Knowledge Space (X,A) itself.

b_rows_sample.anchor: For a knower S, define $$\mathcal F_t^S=\sigma(Y_s^S:s\le t)$$ ... F_t^A != F_t^B can hold even when A and B observe the same underlying object. Therefore: K_t^A != K_t^B does not imply that one is necessarily wrong.
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines an observer-specific Epistemic Filtration F_t^S=sigma(Y_s^S : s<=t) for a knower S, giving a formal version of 'the knower's available information changes over time' and formalizing that two knowers' filtrations F_t^A != F_t^B (hence K_t^A != K_t^B) can both hold without either knower being wrong -- preserving the 'knower owns the epistemic frame' principle with mathematical structure.

b_rows_sample.anchor: we need a semantic equivalence relation $$r_1\equiv_{\mathrm{sem}}r_2$$ iff they preserve the same required epistemic meaning ... if B_r(K,W,Q,E,C) is the observable epistemic behaviour of representation r, then: r1=_sem r2 iff B_r1=B_r2 over the admissible test domain. This is not supplied by measure theory. It is the mathematical object demanded by the latest kernel experiment.
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines Semantic Equivalence r1 =_sem r2 for two admissible representations of epistemic states as agreement of an observable-behaviour function B_r(K,W,Q,E,C) over the admissible test domain, explicitly noting this is NOT supplied by measure theory but is exactly the mathematical object the kernel-reduction experiment's instability demands.

b_rows_sample.anchor: $$X\sim_PY\iff P(X\neq Y)=0.$$ But: equiv_sem != ~_P. ... syntactic equality != representation equality != semantic equivalence != almost-sure equality.
b_rows_sample.statement: Formally separates semantic equivalence (=_sem, agreement of observable behaviour) from measure-theoretic almost-sure equivalence (X ~_P Y iff P(X!=Y)=0), giving a four-way non-collapse: syntactic equality != representation equality != semantic equivalence != almost-sure equality, judged extremely important for the kernel research.

b_rows_sample.anchor: This new formulation explains **why the previous 13-vs-8 kernel experiment became unstable**. The experiment was effectively asking: What is the smallest operator set? before completely fixing: X, A, =_sem, K, D, T. ... The correct research order is now: Epistemic observables -> X -> A -> K_t -> semantic equivalence -> adequacy -> transition -> invariants -> kernel minimality.
b_rows_sample.statement: Explains the kernel-reduction experiment's 13-vs-8 instability as a direct consequence of attempting to answer 'what is the smallest operator set' before fixing X (carrier), A (sigma-field), =_sem (semantic equivalence), K (Knowledge-State space), D (gap operator) and T (transition); prescribes a corrected nine-stage research order: Epistemic observables -> X -> A -> K_t -> semantic equivalence -> adequacy -> transition -> invariants -> kernel minimality.

b_rows_sample.anchor: > ### **Definition — Knowledge Space** > A **Knowledge Space** is a measurable epistemic state space $$\mathsf{KS}=(\mathcal X,\mathscr A)$$ ... Probability describes uncertainty over epistemic possibilities or trajectories; it does not by itself define semantic knowledge, truth, justification, or epistemic adequacy.
b_rows_sample.statement: States the file's final, most authoritative recommended definition: a Knowledge Space is a measurable epistemic state space KS=(X,A); a current Knowledge State K_t induces a measurable compatibility region Gamma(K_t); available information is a filtration; a probability law may optionally be defined over (X,A) or over trajectories Omega_K; the resulting (Omega_K,A_K,P_K) is the Knowledge-process probability space; and probability by itself never defines semantic knowledge, truth, justification or epistemic adequacy.

a_rows_sample.statement: States the theory's scientific workflow as Pattern -> Candidate representation/operator -> Preservation test -> Algebraic-law test, with a candidate entering the theory only once it survives explicit experimentation and audit.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Representation: D -> R ... Transformation: T: D -> R ... Observation: Pi: R -> O, or Q: D -> Y ... Preservation: a preservation requirement specifies what the transformation is required to retain ... C = (Q,Pi,R,...) rather than being an intrinsic property of a representation.
a_rows_sample.statement: Formally defines the theory's four fundamental layers that must not be collapsed prematurely: Representation (D->R, how information is encoded), Transformation (T:D->R, what operation changes the representation), Observation (Pi:R->O or Q:D->Y, what aspect we care about), and Preservation (a contract C=(Q,Pi,R,...) specifying what must remain unchanged, rather than an intrinsic representation property).

a_rows_sample.anchor: A representation is adequate only relative to a defined inquiry and preservation requirement. ... Information matters relative to a specified purpose.
a_rows_sample.statement: States the theory's central principle: a representation is adequate only relative to a defined inquiry and preservation requirement, so information should never be described as mattering absolutely but only relative to a specified purpose -- the basis of the contract-relative view of information.

a_rows_sample.anchor: H(Q(D)|T(D))=0 ... H(T(D)|Q(D)) ... H(T(D)) = H(Q(D)) + H(T(D)|Q(D)) ... A representation can therefore be adequate but large, adequate and reduced, inadequate but compact, or highly detailed yet still unsuitable for the required inquiry.
a_rows_sample.statement: Formalizes representation adequacy as H(Q(D)|T(D))=0 and a second quantity H(T(D)|Q(D)) measuring information beyond what the inquiry determines, related by the decomposition H(T(D))=H(Q(D))+H(T(D)|Q(D)) hence H(T(D))>=H(Q(D)); notes these are different dimensions, so a representation can be adequate-but-large, adequate-and-reduced, inadequate-but-compact, or detailed-yet-unsuitable.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Zero(x|D1) != Zero(x|D2) ... Question: Does the same information behave differently in different contexts? ... Can Zero(S) be derived from Zero-status of proper subsets? These are different questions.
a_rows_sample.statement: Restates and formalizes the two separate dimensions of Zero (Dimension A: context dependence, Zero(x|D1)!=Zero(x|D2); Dimension B: determination order, whether Zero(S) can be derived from proper-subset Zero-status) as genuinely different questions whose relationship (whether contextual Zero causes higher-order Zero) remains open.

a_rows_sample.anchor: An invariant describes something that remains unchanged under transformation: Inv_T(D) = Inv_T(T(D)). Zero asks a different question: Pi(T(D)) = Pi(T(E_S(D))). The first asks: What survives transformation? The second asks: What can be eliminated without changing the observation? Invariant != Zero.
a_rows_sample.statement: Introduces a new formal distinction between an invariant (Inv_T(D)=Inv_T(T(D)), asking what survives transformation) and Zero (Pi(T(D))=Pi(T(E_S(D))), asking what can be eliminated without changing the observation), concluding Invariant != Zero even though the two may interact.

a_rows_sample.anchor: E_S(D) removes S. It should not automatically be called a projection. A projection normally carries algebraic properties such as idempotence: P(P(D))=P(D). Unless those properties are established, the safer terminology is: elimination operator rather than projection.
a_rows_sample.statement: Introduces a new terminological discipline: the elimination operator E_S(D) should not automatically be called a 'projection' since projections normally carry algebraic properties such as idempotence (P(P(D))=P(D)) that have not been established for E_S, so the safer term 'elimination operator' should be used instead.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Redundancy Zero: Information can be removed because equivalent information remains. Contextual Zero: Information is Zero in one context but not another. Cancellation Zero: A group becomes Zero because its combined effect cancels, even though individual members are not Zero. These should currently be
a_rows_sample.statement: Names three descriptive Zero-mechanism categories -- Redundancy Zero (removal because equivalent information remains), Contextual Zero (Zero(x|D1)!=Zero(x|D2)), and Cancellation Zero (a group becomes Zero via combined-effect cancellation despite individual members not being Zero) -- explicitly warning these are descriptive categories/hypotheses, not established ontological kinds, and that the ~90% singleton-determined empirical result does not prove all such cases are 'Redundancy Zero'.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Zero was neither necessary nor sufficient for adequacy in the tested regime. The four cells were populated: Z+A, Z+I, NZ+A, NZ+I. ... Zero !=> Adequacy and Adequacy !=> Zero. This is one of the strongest current separations in the theory.
a_rows_sample.statement: Consolidates the KR-BRIDGE-01 result into a canonical theory statement: Zero was neither necessary nor sufficient for adequacy in the tested regime (all four cells Z+A, Z+I, NZ+A, NZ+I were populated), giving Zero!=>Adequacy and Adequacy!=>Zero as one of the strongest current separations in the theory.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Within the tested deduplication regime, redundancy behaved as a common structural factor associated with both Zero occurrence and loss of adequacy. ... Observed correlation != established mechanism. ... an AI system must not convert an observed correlation into a knowledge rule without controlling f
a_rows_sample.statement: Draws the general methodological principle 'observed correlation != established mechanism' from the BRIDGE redundancy finding, arguing this is directly relevant to KnowledgeOS because an AI system must not convert an observed correlation into a knowledge rule without controlling for structural factors.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Only one redundancy stratum was genuinely informative for the direct within-transformation association. Other strata were structurally uninformative because adequacy or Zero was saturated. ... The natural imbalance should not simply be 'fixed' after the fact because that would alter the experimental
a_rows_sample.statement: Restates the single-informative-stratum limitation of KR-BRIDGE-01 as a general experimental-design lesson: a natural stratum imbalance (other strata structurally uninformative due to saturation) should not be 'fixed' after the fact, since doing so would alter the experimental design rather than genuinely address the limitation.

a_rows_sample.statement: Clarifies precisely what the KR-ZERO _|_ KR-REP-REDUCTION governance conclusion means: analytically separated / not unified by current evidence, i.e. there is currently no sufficient evidence to define a single common reduction operator or algebra containing both -- explicitly not a claim that the two areas can never interact.

a_rows_sample.statement: Consolidates four candidate Vedic-inspired operators into formal notation: reference-relative encoding encode_B(K)=(B,delta_K) with predeclared base-selection to avoid overfitting and correctness condition Q(decode(B,delta_K))=Q(K); structure-preserving composition f(a otimes_A b)=f(a) otimes_B f(b), with a 'homomorphic defect' quantity defined when it fails rather than assuming structure preservation; guarded specialized rewrite operators P(x)=>O_special(x)===O_general(x); and local transformation T(D)=Reconstruct(T(W_1(D)),...,T(W_n(D))) testing whether no information crosses locality boundaries.
