a_rows_sample.anchor: K0 = {...} ... G(...) = 1 (admissible) ... K1 = {...} ... provenance = {...} ... equality family: structural=False semantic=False observational=True ... nonidentifiable(K0,K1,H,Q) = True ... RESULT: transition COMPUTED. |K0|=1 -> |K1|=2
a_rows_sample.statement: Executes and reports verbatim a concrete state transition: K0 contains one Supported item (Nexus version 3.69); an Add of version 3.70 with new evidence, under policy P-infra-v1 and architect authority in context infra, is admissible (G=1); K1 results with two items (3.69 superseded, valid_to closed; 3.70 added) plus a generated provenance record; the three equality relations disagree on the pair (structural=False, semantic=False, observational=True) and nonidentifiable(K0,K1,H,Q)=True (H cannot distinguish them, Q can). Establishes the transition is computable end to end with authority/policy/evidence/context as decidable guards, provenance generated by the transition rather than stored ad hoc, and non-identifiability computable in practice.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Real artifact read from disk: GovernanceLineageNode ... GovernanceLineageEdge ... Theory requires 5 edge attributes; the implementation supplies 1 fully.
a_rows_sample.statement: Reads real production PHP classes (GovernanceLineageNode: decisionId, integrityHash, decidedAt; GovernanceLineageEdge: fromNodeId, toNodeId, edgeReason) and compares them against the theory's required lineage edge e=(T,A,E,C,tau) (Step 230.13): T(transformation) maps to edgeReason as a bare string; A(authority), E(evidence), C(context) are ABSENT from the implementation; tau(time) exists but on the node, not the edge. Concludes the theory requires 5 edge attributes and the implementation fully supplies only 1.

a_rows_sample.anchor: integrityHash -- cryptographic integrity -- has NO SLOT in the theory's lineage tuple (Step 230.12's {(K_i,T_i,A_i,E_i,tau_i,C_i)}). The theory's lineage edge and the implemented lineage edge DIVERGE IN BOTH DIRECTIONS. Neither is a superset of the other.
a_rows_sample.statement: The real implementation's integrityHash (cryptographic integrity) has no corresponding slot in the theory's Step-230.12 lineage tuple {(K_i,T_i,A_i,E_i,tau_i,C_i)}; combined with the prior comparison this establishes the theory's edge and the implemented edge diverge in both directions, neither a superset of the other.

a_rows_sample.anchor: my own model is refuted by the real artifact ... decisionId: NO IDENTITY FIELD in my tuple ... integrityHash: NO INTEGRITY FIELD in my tuple ... My proposed K cannot represent a real node either.
a_rows_sample.statement: Tests the verifier's own repaired Item tuple (q,s,e,c,t,u) against the real GovernanceLineageNode fields: decisionId has no matching identity field, integrityHash has no matching integrity field, and decidedAt only partially maps to t.known_from (a single timestamp vs. the tuple's bitemporal design). Records this as a refutation of the verifier's own proposal by running code -- characterized as the strongest available class of evidence against it.

a_rows_sample.anchor: BLOCKER 1 -- ITEM IDENTITY ... Identity is upstream of equality, and equality is upstream of four of the nine operations. The implementation already solves this: decisionId. The theory is behind its own code.
a_rows_sample.statement: Ranks item identity as the highest-leverage blocker: no K-candidate in the corpus (nor the verifier's own proposal) carries an item identity field, without which 'the same item at a later time' is inexpressible, which supersession, replay, merge and deduplication (four of nine operations) all require; identity is upstream of equality. Notes the running implementation already solves this via decisionId -- the theory is behind its own code.

a_rows_sample.anchor: BLOCKER 2 -- EPISTEMIC-STATUS VOCABULARY ... Eleven competing vocabularies; none designated. UNDERDETERMINED BY CORPUS. This is a normative/domain decision, not a mathematical one -- a declared STOP condition. I will not choose it.
a_rows_sample.statement: Declares the epistemic-status vocabulary blocker a normative/domain decision (eleven competing vocabularies exist in the corpus, none designated) rather than a mathematical one, and explicitly refuses to choose on the verifier's own authority -- a declared STOP condition.

a_rows_sample.anchor: BLOCKER 3 -- INTEGRITY ... absent from every late kernel. Step 230-232 dropped a concept the corpus had already built and the code already uses. ... BLOCKER 5 -- TRANSITION AT SCALE ... unmeasured.
a_rows_sample.statement: Blocker 3: integrityHash exists in production code and in Step 073's cryptographic-provenance work but is absent from every late-stage (Step 230-232) kernel formulation -- a concept the corpus had already built and the code already uses was dropped. Blocker 5: the kernel only computes on 1-2 items; complexity/behavior at realistic scale is unmeasured. Also notes the ~25 registries, the four E-scales, and the two kernel lineages are NOT theory gaps but documentation/naming issues -- the underlying mathematics is unaffected by how many times it was renamed.

a_rows_sample.anchor: F. Is the theory empirically validated against KnowledgeOS? -- PARTIAL. Confirmed by execution: a typed provenance graph exists, with branching, 47 tests passing. Refuted by execution: the theory's edge tuple != the implemented edge, in both directions. Untested: everything else.
a_rows_sample.statement: Runs a lettered decision tree (A-J): (A) mathematical theory NOT complete (K undefined in corpus, identity/integrity absent, status underdetermined); (B) central knowledge-state object NOT formally defined in the corpus, only in the verifier's own proposal, itself refuted on identity/integrity; (C) computable YES under conditions (designated status vocabulary, identity field, integrity field); (D) at least one real state instantiated YES (K0); (E) at least one real transformation executed YES (T(K0,Add(3.70),...)->K1 with provenance); (F) empirical validation against KnowledgeOS PARTIAL -- confirmed by execution: a typed provenance graph exists with branching and 47 passing tests; refuted by execution: the theory's edge tuple does not equal the implemented edge, in both directions; everything else untested; (G) DDD Ubiquitous Language NOT stable (eleven status vocabularies, four E-scales, ~25 registries, zero crosswalks); (H) architecture PARTIALLY derivable (provenance graph, bitemporal validity, transition-with-guards, Validation->Assessment derivable; anything requiring K/identity/equality not derivable); (I) smallest remaining blocker = ITEM IDENTITY, already answered by decisionId in running code; (J) the resolving experiment: extend the tuple to (id,q,s,e,c,t,u,integrity), re-run the kernel, round-trip a real GovernanceLineageNode through it and assert field-for-field equality -- if it round-trips the theory and implementation are the same object with an empirical anchor; if not, the divergent field is the next blocker.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Nothing here relies on Steps 236 or 239 (FEEDBACK-CONTAMINATED). ... Did the corpus improve? Yes ... Did the corpus independently prove the claim? No -- and it is not counted as having done so.
a_rows_sample.statement: States an explicit source-independence discipline: this analysis derives only from Steps 073, 081, 175, 185, 230, 231, 232 and direct reads of production code, deliberately excluding Steps 236 and 239 as feedback-contaminated (they responded to prior audit). Separates two distinct questions kept apart per an earlier protocol section: did the corpus improve (yes, Steps 236/239 revised prior conclusions in response to audit) versus did the corpus independently prove the claim (no) -- the latter is explicitly not counted as demonstrated.

a_rows_sample.anchor: What I did NOT do: Did not choose a status vocabulary ... Did not promote my kernel to theory ... Did not merge the two kernel lineages. Did not repair the corpus's K ... Did not call the executable kernel empirical validation of KnowledgeOS
a_rows_sample.statement: Explicitly scopes the deliverable's limits: did not choose a status vocabulary (declared normative STOP condition); did not promote the executable kernel to theory status (it remains 'VERIFIER PROPOSAL', refuted on two fields); did not merge the two competing kernel lineages; did not repair the corpus's own unconstructible K, only built and reported an alternative; did not characterize the executable kernel as empirical validation of KnowledgeOS itself, only of a model. Ends with an explicit STOP awaiting supervision before an identity/integrity extension.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Do NOT proceed as if the proposed repair Item = (id, q, s, e, c, t, u, integrity) is now the theory. It is only a verifier proposal.
a_rows_sample.statement: Explicitly blocks promoting the prior file's proposed repaired Item tuple (id,q,s,e,c,t,u,integrity) to theory status, reasserting it remains only a verifier proposal to be adversarially re-tested against the complete corpus and the real KnowledgeOS implementation.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Do not simply add id. Determine: Where did the need for identity first arise? Trace the evolution ... first problem -> proposed concept -> refinement -> later formulation -> current implementation. Do NOT assume the latest formulation is correct merely because it is newer.
a_rows_sample.statement: Mandates a full historical derivation search across the corpus for every treatment of identity/identifier/decisionId/equality/deduplication/supersession/lineage/replay/merge, to be organized as an explicit chain (first problem -> proposed concept -> refinement -> later formulation -> current implementation), with change-of-meaning over time preserved rather than collapsed, and an explicit refusal to assume recency implies correctness.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Do NOT assume that the identifier belongs to an Item. Test at least these possibilities: A. identity of a proposition ... H. identity of an occurrence/version. For each, determine: what entity receives the identity; whether identity is persistent; whether identity survives supersession/re-ingestion/
a_rows_sample.statement: Requires testing 8 distinct candidate referents for 'what bears identity' (a proposition, a knowledge item, an evidence assertion, a state element, a decision, a lineage node, an observation, an occurrence/version) against 7 properties each (persistence, survival under supersession/re-ingestion/serialization, semantic-vs-technical nature, and whether distinct IDs can legitimately denote the same knowledge) -- explicitly refusing to assume identity attaches to 'an Item' by default.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Now determine whether the addition of identity changes their definitions [eq_struct, eq_sem, eq_obs]. ... Construct explicit counterexamples showing cases where: IDs equal but content differs; IDs differ but semantic content is equal; structure is equal but observation differs; observation is equal
a_rows_sample.statement: Requires re-deriving the equality family (adding identity equality to eq_struct/eq_sem/eq_obs from the prior file) with four explicit counterexample patterns (equal-IDs-differing-content; differing-IDs-equal-semantics; equal-structure-differing-observation; equal-observation-differing-state) and a matrix mapping each of 9 operations (Add, Update, Supersede, Merge, Replay, Deduplicate, Validate, Query, Compare) to its actually-required equivalence relation.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Do NOT automatically add integrity to K. Determine what integrity actually is. ... investigate whether h = Hash(Serialize(K)) is preferable to storing h as a primitive component. Do not choose until the derivation and implementation evidence justify it.
a_rows_sample.statement: Blocks automatically adding an integrity field to K; requires first determining integrity's ontological placement by testing whether it is a property of an Item, a serialized representation, a state, a lineage edge, a cryptographic commitment, a property of provenance, or a verification result, and whether it belongs inside K, T, E, A, or lineage, or is better expressed as a derived function h=Hash(Serialize(K)) rather than a stored primitive -- deferring the choice until derivation and implementation evidence justify it.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Now perform the experiment proposed in the previous audit. ... Compare field by field. The result must explicitly classify every field: exact correspondence, derived correspondence, lossy correspondence, theory-only, implementation-only, semantic mismatch. ... If round-trip fails, identify the exact
a_rows_sample.statement: Escalates the prior file's proposed single-artifact round-trip into a required multi-artifact protocol: perform implementation->theory->implementation and theory->implementation mappings against at least 3 structurally different real artifacts (a simple lineage node, a transition/supersession node, a node carrying integrity/provenance), classifying every field into one of 6 explicit categories (exact correspondence, derived correspondence, lossy correspondence, theory-only, implementation-only, semantic mismatch), producing an actual executable assertion rather than a compatibility claim, and identifying the exact first divergent field on failure.

a_rows_sample.anchor: For every component answer: Why does it exist? What problem requires it? ... Can it be removed without breaking a required capability? ... For every proposed component x in K: Calculate/test K_without_x. Then determine which formally defined capabilities fail. ... Do not call a component necessary m
a_rows_sample.statement: Requires a second, more rigorous minimality test on any revised Item type: a 10-question justification checklist per component (existence reason, problem requiring it, corpus derivation, implementation location, computability, serializability, comparability, transition participation, primitive-vs-derived status, and safe removability), plus an explicit K_without_x removal test per component recorded in a Component/Remove-it/Broken-capability/Counterexample/Necessary table, with the rule that usefulness alone never establishes necessity -- only breaking a formally required capability does.

b_rows_sample.anchor: S_0=100. History A: 100→80. History B: 120→80. The current state is identical: S_1=80. But: S_0^A ≠ S_0^B. ... History→CurrentState is many-to-one. ... Historical state is not identifiable from current state alone.
b_rows_sample.statement: Proves via a minimal numeric counterexample (History A: 100->80; History B: 120->80, both yielding CurrentState=80 but different prior states S_0) that the mapping History->CurrentState is many-to-one, so its inverse (reconstructing history from current state) is not uniquely defined -- 'historical state is not identifiable from current state alone.'

b_rows_sample.anchor: identifiable when different parameter values cannot generate the same observable distribution. Analogously ... H1 ≠ H2 ⇒ Current(H1) ≠ Current(H2). Real systems rarely satisfy this. ... 'Architecture Status = APPROVED' ... does not necessarily tell us: who proposed it; what evidence existed; which version was reviewed; which alternatives were rejected...
b_rows_sample.statement: Explicitly borrows the statistical concept of identifiability (a parameter is identifiable if distinct values always produce distinct observable distributions) as the correct lens for the architecture question, formalizing history-identifiability as H1!=H2 => Current(H1)!=Current(H2), noted to rarely hold for real systems. Grounds this in a concrete KnowledgeOS example: 'Architecture Status = APPROVED' alone reveals nothing about who proposed it, what evidence existed, which version was reviewed, which alternatives were rejected, what the Board knew, which determination supported the decision, or which authorization allowed implementation.

b_rows_sample.anchor: R1 -- non-identifiability is NOT a field... R2 -- structural equality is insufficient... R3 -- the status type is mine, not the corpus's.
b_rows_sample.statement: Three of the ten attacks refute the original proposal: R1, non-identifiability must be a relation over (K1,K2,H,Q) -- two states observationally equivalent under an observation map -- not a label-valued attribute of one item; R2, structural equality is insufficient, shown by an executed counterexample where identical knowledge re-ingested under a new evidence id (E-001 -> E-001-dup) is structurally unequal, so equality must be a FAMILY of relations, not one; R3, the STATUS_VOCAB type is the verifier's own invention -- the corpus has eleven competing vocabularies and designates none, so status is UNDERDETERMINED BY CORPUS.

a_rows_sample.anchor: We therefore construct a minimal candidate: K_0=(C_0,Q_0,Gamma_0) where C_0 = content, Q_0 = epistemic qualification, Gamma_0 = governing/contextual qualification. This is a construction hypothesis, not yet the final kernel.
a_rows_sample.statement: Proposes a minimal candidate Knowledge State as a three-part construction hypothesis K0=(C0,Q0,Gamma0) (content, epistemic qualification, governing/contextual qualification), with the requirement that each component itself receive a mathematical type before further construction.

a_rows_sample.anchor: C_0=(V_0,E_0) ... C_0 in Graph with V_0 subseteq Node and E_0 subseteq Node x RelationType x Node. This gives us a concrete structural representation without yet claiming that all KnowledgeOS knowledge must be a graph.
a_rows_sample.statement: Defines Content C0=(V0,E0) as a typed graph (V0 subseteq Node, E0 subseteq Node x RelationType x Node), explicitly scoping the claim to 'a concrete structural representation' without asserting that all KnowledgeOS knowledge must be graph-shaped.

a_rows_sample.anchor: We must not collapse o=p. Instead o in Observation while p in Proposition. And the semantic relation is Supports(o,p). ... Otherwise the theory cannot distinguish 'The proposition is true' from 'We observed evidence supporting the proposition.'
a_rows_sample.statement: Establishes, via the worked example, that Observation and Proposition must be distinct typed objects related by Supports(o,p) rather than identified (o=p); without this distinction the theory cannot separate 'the proposition is true' from 'evidence was observed supporting the proposition' -- flagged as critical for the later epistemic theory.

a_rows_sample.anchor: A candidate status space is: Sigma = {Observed, Supported, Inferred, Validated, Rejected, Unknown}. This is not yet accepted as the canonical vocabulary. It is merely a candidate domain derived from the concepts already under reconstruction.
a_rows_sample.statement: Proposes a candidate 6-value epistemic status space Sigma={Observed, Supported, Inferred, Validated, Rejected, Unknown}, explicitly disclaiming canonical status -- a candidate domain only.

a_rows_sample.anchor: theta(p) in Interval ... the possibility remains that temporal validity belongs to an assertion instance, rather than to the proposition itself. That distinction must remain open.
a_rows_sample.statement: Defines temporal validity as theta:Proposition -> Interval (not a scalar), but leaves open whether temporal validity actually belongs to the proposition itself or to a separate 'assertion instance' concept.

a_rows_sample.anchor: lambda subseteq Artifact x Artifact ... The direction must eventually be frozen because a->b and b->a have completely different semantics. So: Lineage direction = OPEN DESIGN QUESTION at this stage.
a_rows_sample.statement: Defines lineage as a directed relation over artifacts (lambda subseteq Artifact x Artifact, e.g. e->o->p from the worked example) but flags the direction convention itself (e.g. o->p vs p<-o<-e) as an open design question since the two directions carry different semantics.

a_rows_sample.anchor: we should resist immediately embedding context into every proposition. An alternative is: Interpret: Proposition x Context -> Meaning. This preserves separation. ... this is a design hypothesis requiring later testing.
a_rows_sample.statement: Considers two alternatives for context: embedding it directly into each proposition (p_c=(p,c)) versus keeping propositions context-free and defining a separate Interpret:Proposition x Context -> Meaning function; prefers the latter to preserve separation of concerns, flagged as a design hypothesis needing later testing.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Validate: Proposition x Evidence x Policy -> Assessment. This is much better than making policy itself part of the proposition.
a_rows_sample.statement: Defines governance/policy application as Validate:Proposition x Evidence x Policy -> Assessment, arguing this is preferable to embedding policy directly into the proposition object.

a_rows_sample.anchor: K_0=(C_0,sigma_0,theta_0,lambda_0,pi_0) where C_0=(V_0,E_0) [concrete worked values] ... This is now an actual mathematical object, rather than merely a symbolic kernel.
a_rows_sample.statement: Assembles a fully concrete K0=(C0,sigma0,theta0,lambda0,pi0) with actual worked values: V0={s,v1,p,o,e}, E0={(s,hasVersion,v1),(o,supports,p),(e,produces,o)}, sigma0(p)=Observed, theta0(p)=[t0,infinity), lambda0={e->o->p}, pi0 in Policy -- explicitly characterized as an actual mathematical object rather than a merely symbolic kernel notation, directly instantiating the K5=(G,sigma,theta,lambda,pi) shape with concrete content.

a_rows_sample.anchor: we need a validity predicate Valid(K). Thus: K = {K | Valid(K)}. And we must define Valid(K_0). ... Type validity ... Referential validity ... Relation validity ... Status validity ... Temporal validity ... Lineage validity. These are genuine candidate invariants.
a_rows_sample.statement: Defines the Knowledge-State space as K={K | Valid(K)} and proposes six candidate validity conditions for K0: type validity of V0/E0, referential validity (every edge references existing nodes), relation validity (relation types are well-typed), status validity (sigma0(p) in Sigma), temporal validity (theta0(p) in Interval), and lineage validity (every lineage reference points to an existing artifact).

a_rows_sample.anchor: T_addObservation(K_0,o_2)=K_1. If o_2 is correctly typed and all references remain valid, then Valid(K_1). Thus: K_0 in K and Valid(o_2) => T_addObservation(K_0,o_2) in K. This gives us the first concrete candidate closure theorem. But it is only proved for this restricted transformation. It does no
a_rows_sample.statement: States and proves a first, restricted closure theorem: K0 in K and Valid(o2) implies T_addObservation(K0,o2) in K, for the single add-observation transformation only -- explicitly not a proof of global transformation closure over K.

a_rows_sample.anchor: T_addObservation is naturally a partial function: T_addObservation: D -> K where D subseteq K x Observation. The domain condition could be Pre(K,o)=true. Then T(K,o) is defined iff Pre(K,o). This is a major result for the eventual transition algebra.
a_rows_sample.statement: Establishes that state transformations are naturally partial functions (T_addObservation: D -> K, D subseteq K x Observation) defined only where a precondition Pre(K,o) holds -- e.g. an observation referencing an absent entity makes the transformation undefined -- flagged as a major result for the eventual transition algebra (transformations are not assumed total).

a_rows_sample.anchor: PASS -- Candidate Knowledge State successfully constructed but FORMAL CLOSURE -- NOT YET PROVEN and FINAL KERNEL -- NOT YET SELECTED. ... Can K_0 survive identity, equality, contradiction, uncertainty, and competing evidence without introducing ad-hoc rules? That is the next serious mathematical tes
a_rows_sample.statement: Records the Step-245 verdict (PASS on constructing a candidate K0; FORMAL CLOSURE not yet proven; FINAL KERNEL not yet selected) and sets the next mandatory test: whether K0 can survive identity, equality, contradiction, uncertainty, and competing evidence without ad-hoc rules, rather than being extended blindly.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Identity: PASS at representation level. Equality: FAIL/OPEN. Contradiction: PARTIAL PASS. Uncertainty: PARTIAL/OPEN.
a_rows_sample.statement: Scores the Step-245 candidate K0 on the four stress tests: object identity PASS at the representation level; Knowledge-State equality FAIL/OPEN (no canonical K1=K2 established); contradiction PARTIAL PASS (representable but requires context+time+domain constraints, not intrinsic); uncertainty PARTIAL/OPEN (representable via an external regime, numeric semantics unresolved).

a_rows_sample.anchor: whether K1=K2 depends partly on whether provenance is semantically constitutive. We therefore cannot yet decide whether lambda is merely metadata or part of identity. Provenance minimality = OPEN.

a_rows_sample.statement: Proposes a candidate signature for Accept and Reject (Assessment x Authority x Policy -> Decision, following the command/event/state model) while explicitly keeping both UNRESOLVED rather than establishing them, since the corpus's lifecycle vocabulary (Approved/Rejected) does not settle whether they are state mutations or assessment-to-decision mappings.

a_rows_sample.statement: Reclassifies Remove as CORPUS-ESTABLISHES (a partial operation Remove_x:K-harpoonup->K, since removing one item may invalidate dependent knowledge) -- the file explicitly calls this 'a stronger result than we had at Step 249', where the same operation was instead rated UNDEFINED at signature level (S1613); the two adjacent same-day step files disagree on Remove's status without either citing the other's specific verdict.

a_rows_sample.statement: Keeps Merge, Split, Withdraw, and Commit all OPEN: Merge's dependencies (conflict, provenance, temporal validity, identity, epistemic status) are named but not resolved; Split has no established signature at all; Withdraw could mean 6 mathematically distinct things (projection removal, governance-status change, assertion invalidation, supersession, authorization retraction, or historical-preservation-with-changed-applicability); Commit could belong to persistence, governance, event publication, lifecycle, or transaction semantics -- none corpus-derived, so none classified.

a_rows_sample.statement: Identifies 'Transformation' as a 3-way overloaded ubiquitous-language term (epistemic transformation Candidate->Knowledge; state transformation K->K'; representation/regime transformation K->Y_R, matching the earlier Projection_R concept), warning it cannot be used canonically without qualifying which of the three is meant, until the corpus demonstrates they are genuinely one concept.

a_rows_sample.anchor: We cannot yet remove Merge, Supersede, Split, Withdraw because the corpus may require them for capabilities that have not yet been tested. Therefore the minimality status is: NOT YET TESTABLE rather than: minimal set found.

a_rows_sample.statement: Confirms Step 031's epistemic-reasoning function R(K,E,C,M,V,T) (6-valued status output: Accepted/Unknown/Underdetermined/Conflicted/Invalid/RequiresValidation) types a result status, not a resulting state, and must not be collapsed into Step 232's state-transition T -- reinforcing the Reasoning/Assessment != State-Transition separation independently reached in Step 250.

a_rows_sample.statement: Traces the root cause of 'Transformation' polysemy to treating mathematically distinct functions (delta, tau, T, R) as though identical despite differing domains, codomains, arities, semantics, failure models and context treatment -- confirming and explaining the polysemy S1614 flagged as a term-overload problem.

a_rows_sample.anchor: The candidate kernel cannot yet contain merely (K,T). It must at least distinguish State from Transition from Assessment from Decision from Event and History/Lineage. Whether these are all primitives of one final mathematical object is still open. ... Transition System = typed family of related tran
a_rows_sample.statement: States the step's final conclusion and the most important kernel-design consequence: the candidate kernel must distinguish at least 6 roles (State, Transition, Assessment, Decision, Event, History/Lineage) rather than collapsing to (K,T); the strongest current hypothesis is that the Transition System is a typed family of related structures, not one closed algebra, though final mathematical closure remains unproven -- directly aligning with the parallel verifier track's typed-family conclusion (S1603, S1612).

b_rows_sample.anchor: Add, Remove, Revise, Merge, Split, Supersede, Validate, Reject, Transform. ... What invariants survive these operations?
b_rows_sample.statement: Step 232 (tail) asks whether knowledge states form an algebraic structure under nine operations (Add, Remove, Revise, Merge, Split, Supersede, Validate, Reject, Transform), posing Add(K,x)?, Merge(K1,K2)?, Revise(K,x,x')?, Transform(K_A,C_A,C_B)?, and the key question of what invariants survive these operations.

b_rows_sample.anchor: \mathbb K=\{(G,\sigma,\theta,\lambda,\pi)\mid \text{state satisfies the domain invariants}\}. ... (\mathbb K,\mathcal O)
b_rows_sample.statement: The knowledge-state SPACE mathbb K (all admissible states satisfying domain invariants) is distinguished from a particular STATE mathfrak K_t at time t; rather than assuming a classical algebraic structure (ring/field/vector space), the appropriate initial object is a state-transition algebra (mathbb K, mathcal O) where mathcal O is the set of admissible operations.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Transformation\neq Validation. Validation:\mathbb K\times X\rightarrow Assessment while Transformation:\mathbb K\times Parameters\rightarrow\mathbb K.
b_rows_sample.statement: State-changing vs state-classifying operations: Transformation != Validation -- Validation: mathbb K x X -> Assessment (may merely produce an assessment) while Transformation: mathbb K x Parameters -> mathbb K (changes the state); validation may subsequently trigger a transition, corresponding to the DDD chain Command->Decision->Event->State, rated a much better model than treating CRUD as the architecture.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Add_x(\mathfrak K) is a partial operation. ... Remove_x:\mathbb K\rightharpoonup\mathbb K. ... Remove(E) may require Reassess(A).
b_rows_sample.statement: Addition Add_x:mathbb K -> mathbb K is a PARTIAL operation, defined only if Invariant(K')=True; Removal Remove_x:mathbb K -|-> mathbb K is likewise partial since an accepted item may depend on the removed one (A-dependsOn->E), so Remove(E) may require Reassess(A).

b_rows_sample.anchor: x_t\xrightarrow{revisedTo}x_{t+1}. Revision=new state+historical relation.
b_rows_sample.statement: Revision must not be modeled as overwriting (x_t <- x_{t+1}, destroying history) but as x_t -revisedTo-> x_{t+1}, giving Revision = new state + historical relation, naturally supporting lineage.

b_rows_sample.anchor: \sigma(x_1)=Superseded and \sigma(x_2)=Accepted. Currentness\neq Truth.
b_rows_sample.statement: Supersession differs from revision: x1 is retained as historical knowledge marked Superseded (sigma(x1)=Superseded) while x2 is Accepted, again demonstrating Currentness != Truth.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Merge\neq SetUnion. ... Merge(K_1,K_2,C,P) ... compatible, redundant, complementary, contradictory, superseding. ... TextMerge\neq SemanticMerge.
b_rows_sample.statement: Merge is a partial, semantic operation Merge:mathbb K x mathbb K -|-> mathbb K, not naive set union (Merge != SetUnion) since sources may contain contradictory claims; a proper Merge(K1,K2,C,P) classifies relationships as compatible/redundant/complementary/contradictory/superseding -- giving the DDD principle TextMerge != SemanticMerge (a repository-level/Git merge is not necessarily a domain merge).

b_rows_sample.anchor: Split(Merge(K_1,K_2))\neq(K_1,K_2). ... non-invertible knowledge transformation.
b_rows_sample.statement: Split:mathbb K -|-> mathbb K x mathbb K is not a true mathematical inverse of Merge -- Split(Merge(K1,K2)) != (K1,K2) in general because merge may introduce derived information, reconciliation decisions, normalization, or conflict resolution -- an example of non-invertible knowledge transformation.

b_rows_sample.anchor: (\mathcal T,\circ) has the structure of a transformation semigroup, assuming closure. ... (\mathcal T,\circ,I) is at least monoid-like. ... We should not claim it yet as a theorem.
b_rows_sample.statement: The set of admissible transformations mathcal T with composition forms a candidate transformation semigroup (mathcal T, o) assuming closure, with an identity transformation I_K(K)=K making (mathcal T,o,I) at least monoid-like -- explicitly not yet claimed as a proven theorem, but architecturally useful for representing pipelines K3=(T3 o T2 o T1)(K0).

b_rows_sample.anchor: T_2\circ T_1 may be mathematically composable but not governance-valid. MathematicalComposition from GovernedComposition.
b_rows_sample.statement: Governance breaks naive composition: T1 authorized in context C1 composed with T2 (requiring ungranted authority) may be mathematically composable but not governance-valid, requiring MathematicalComposition to be distinguished from GovernedComposition.

b_rows_sample.anchor: \mathcal T_G\subseteq\mathcal T ... T\in\mathcal T_G only if Authority(T)\land Policy(T)\land RequiredEvidence(T). ... we should not automatically call \mathcal T_G a semigroup.
b_rows_sample.statement: Governed transformations mathcal T_G subseteq mathcal T require Authority(T) and Policy(T) and RequiredEvidence(T); mathcal T_G is NOT necessarily closed under composition (T1,T2 in T_G but T2 o T1 not in T_G if the combined transformation crosses a governance boundary) -- an important mathematical correction against assuming T_G is a semigroup.

b_rows_sample.anchor: G(T,K,C,A,P)\in\{0,1\}. K'=T(K) only if G(T,K,C,A,P)=1. ... Evidence is a condition of admissibility, not merely metadata.
b_rows_sample.statement: Governance is formalized as a boolean constraint system G(T,K,C,A,P) in {0,1}: a state transition K'=T(K) is valid only if G(T,K,C,A,P)=1, and separately E(T) |= ReqEvidence(T,P) must hold -- evidence is a condition of admissibility, not merely metadata. Together these give the core transition rule K_{t+1}=T_t(K_t) subject to G(...)=1 and E_t |= ReqEvidence(T_t,P_t).

b_rows_sample.anchor: M_C(\Delta_t)\Rightarrow Governed(T_t). ... U_t=\varnothing. A governed knowledge system may transform information, but material semantic changes may not occur silently.
b_rows_sample.statement: Material-change condition, rated potentially one of the most important invariants in the entire architecture: M_C(Delta_t)=1 (materiality of the diff between K_t and K_{t+1}) implies Governed(T_t); reformulated elegantly as U_t = empty set where U_t is the set of undeclared material changes -- a governed knowledge system may transform information, but material semantic changes may never occur silently.

b_rows_sample.anchor: K_t\subseteq K_{t+1} ... Clearly not. ... HistoricalKnowledge(K_t)\subseteq HistoricalKnowledge(K_{t+1}). ... HistoricalMonotonicity.
b_rows_sample.statement: Knowledge is NOT monotonic (K_t subseteq K_{t+1} fails since knowledge can be corrected/withdrawn/superseded/invalidated), but a weaker HistoricalMonotonicity holds: HistoricalKnowledge(K_t) subseteq HistoricalKnowledge(K_{t+1}) -- the system should not erase the fact that a knowledge state existed, even though Current(K_t) need not be monotonic while History(K_<=t) should normally grow.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Do not assume KnowledgeOS is a lattice. It may become a partial order over particular classes of knowledge states, but this requires proof.
b_rows_sample.statement: Whether knowledge states form a lattice under an information ordering K1<=K2 (K2 contains at least as much accepted information) is explicitly left open and cautioned against assuming, since contradictions complicate a least-upper-bound K1 join K2; likewise no universal statistical information ordering should be assumed given multiple incompatible candidates (entropy, KL divergence, Fisher information, posterior concentration).

b_rows_sample.anchor: F_Y=F_X\circ T^{-1}. ... Y must remain linked to X. This is exactly what lineage is supposed to preserve.
b_rows_sample.statement: Distributional transformation is a rigorous statistical-layer example of knowledge transformation: for X~F and measurable T, Y=T(X) induces F_Y = F_X o T^-1; when KnowledgeOS derives an engineering indicator Y from observed metric X, Y must remain linked to X via provenance/uncertainty/assumptions -- exactly what lineage is meant to preserve.

b_rows_sample.anchor: q_1,q_2\xrightarrow{f}q. ... Validity(q)=g(Validity(q_1),Validity(q_2),f).
b_rows_sample.statement: Derived knowledge q=f(q1,q2) gives a knowledge derivation graph q1,q2-f->q; dependency preservation proposes Validity(q) = g(Validity(q1),Validity(q2),f) so that invalidating q1 makes q suspect -- a candidate for deterministic validity propagation, illustrated by Requirement->ArchitectureDecision->ImplementationConstraint where superseding the Requirement triggers Supersession->ImpactAnalysis on the ArchitectureDecision, not necessarily invalidation.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Impact(q)=Descendants(q). ... Reassessment(Impact(q)). This may become one of the most important practical capabilities of KnowledgeOS.
b_rows_sample.statement: Knowledge impact propagation: Impact(q) = Descendants(q) in the provenance/semantic graph, so a material change to q triggers Reassessment(Impact(q)) -- rated potentially one of the most important practical capabilities of KnowledgeOS, and making the transformation algebra explicitly dependency-aware: Input+Context+Evidence+Authority+Dependencies -> Output.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Law 1 -- Traceability ... Law 2 -- Governance ... Law 3 -- Evidence ... Law 4 -- Semantic accountability ... Law 5 -- Historical preservation ... Law 6 -- Epistemic separation.
b_rows_sample.statement: Six candidate algebraic laws, rated much closer to architectural invariants than the earlier broad principles: L1 Traceability (exists L(T) for every material transformation), L2 Governance (Material(T)=>Authorized(T)), L3 Evidence (RequiredEvidence(T)=>Evidence(T)), L4 Semantic accountability (MaterialSemanticChange(T)=>Declared(T)), L5 Historical preservation (historical state not silently destroyed), L6 Epistemic separation (Status(q) != Content(q)).

b_rows_sample.anchor: All changes require human approval is a policy. It is not necessarily a universal architectural invariant. ... Every consequential transformation requires an authority mechanism appropriate to its risk and policy.
b_rows_sample.statement: Crucial distinction between invariant and policy: 'all changes require human approval' is a policy, not a universal invariant; the more general, robust invariant is 'every consequential transformation requires an authority mechanism appropriate to its risk and policy' (human approval, delegated authority, deterministic policy, or automated rule).

a_rows_sample.anchor: We need to distinguish three claims: Representable, Derivable, Primitive. They are not equivalent. If X=f(T) then X may be derivable. But that does not establish that X is unnecessary. Conversely, if X can be encoded inside T, that does not prove that the semantic concept represented by X can be eli
a_rows_sample.statement: States a 3-way non-equivalence governing the whole removal-test methodology: Representable, Derivable, and Primitive are distinct claims, so encoding X inside another structure T neither proves X is unnecessary nor eliminates the semantic concept it represents.

a_rows_sample.anchor: A component is removable only if there exists a reconstruction function r_i: K^-i -> K such that all required semantics are preserved. For every valid operation T, we require a commuting condition: r_i o T^-i = T o r_i. ... This is the formal version of the state-sufficiency criterion already develo
a_rows_sample.statement: Formalizes the component-removal criterion as a commuting-diagram condition (r_i o T^-i = T o r_i for a reconstruction function r_i), explicitly identified as the same state-sufficiency congruence criterion developed in Step 248 (S1608), now applied component-wise rather than to the whole state abstraction.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Minimality(K|T) not Minimality(K). ... if T2 superset T1 adds Merge, Supersede, Replay, ConflictResolution and provenance-sensitive operations, the same representation may cease to be sufficient. ... There may be no context-free minimal Knowledge State.
a_rows_sample.statement: Reaffirms and applies Step 248's transformation-relative minimality principle (Minimality(K|T), not Minimality(K)) as the governing frame for the Step-254 removal tests, since expanding the transformation set can make a previously-sufficient representation insufficient.

a_rows_sample.anchor: T mentioning K =/=> K derivable from T. Verdict: K is NOT shown removable. But importantly: K is also NOT proven primitive. ... C cannot currently be removed. But again: C is not thereby proven primitive. Context appears semantically necessary to some formulations, but its formal type remains unreso
a_rows_sample.statement: Executes removal tests on K and C from the Step-230 kernel (K,C,T,E,A): K appearing inside T's signature does not prove K is derivable from T, so K is neither shown removable nor proven primitive; Context similarly cannot currently be removed (no established C=f(K,T,E,A) function, and any generic projection would silently pick one of Context's several overloaded meanings) but is also not thereby proven primitive.

a_rows_sample.anchor: At t=0, external evidence may exist before any transformation occurs. Therefore Evidence_0 cannot generally be reconstructed from History(T) alone. This is structurally analogous to the provenance failure. Verdict: Evidence cannot presently be shown removable. ... there is no valid general function
a_rows_sample.statement: Executes removal tests on Evidence and Authority: initial (t=0) external evidence cannot generally be reconstructed from History(T) alone (structurally analogous to the provenance base-case failure), so Evidence is not removable; Authority likewise has no general reconstruction function from the remaining components since it originates from an external actor/governance act (evidence, assessment and source do not self-authorize), so Authority is not removable either.

a_rows_sample.anchor: T=f(K,C,E,A) ... The corpus explicitly warns that the theory cannot simultaneously claim T primitive and T=f(K,C,E,A) without specifying the direction of primitiveness. ... T may be primitive OR derived, but the corpus has not chosen. This is not a minor issue. It determines the ontology of the enti
a_rows_sample.statement: Runs the reverse removal test on Transformation T itself, finding the corpus has never chosen a direction for T's primitiveness (T could be primitive, or derived as T=f(K,C,E,A)), and warns this ambiguity is not minor -- it determines the ontology of the entire kernel.

a_rows_sample.anchor: At least four components appear inside the definition/signature of T. ... kernel independence classified as refuted for both Step 230 and Step 232. ... Kernel component count != number of independent primitives. A five-tuple is not automatically a five-primitive ontology.
a_rows_sample.statement: States the central negative conclusion of the removal tests: since at least 4 of the 5 K230=(K,C,T,E,A) components appear inside T's own signature, kernel component count is not the same as the number of independent primitives -- a five-tuple candidate kernel is not automatically a five-primitive ontology, confirmed as refuted independence for both Step 230 and Step 232.

a_rows_sample.anchor: History(T)=empty. Yet Provenance(H1) != Provenance(H2). Therefore History(T) cannot reconstruct all provenance. This is already recorded as a formal base-case failure. Provenance cannot be declared derived from T in general. This is one of the strongest findings in the entire reconstruction.
a_rows_sample.statement: Gives the step's decisive counterexample: two initial histories with identical knowledge content but different externally-sourced evidence (e1 vs e2) both have History(T)=empty (no transformation has yet occurred) yet distinct Provenance, proving History(T) cannot universally reconstruct provenance -- named one of the strongest findings in the entire reconstruction.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Event=History(T) cannot automatically be universal [if events represent externally observed occurrences]. Event is not proven derivable from T. ... an observation cannot simply be reconstructed as 'whatever evidence exists.' ... Observation remains a live primitive candidate. ... Proposition has str
a_rows_sample.statement: Runs further removal tests: Event is not proven derivable from T (externally observed events may exist independently of KnowledgeOS transformations); Observation cannot simply be reconstructed as evidence and remains a live primitive candidate; Proposition retains strong primitive status but its irreducibility is not proven, only that its removal is unjustified -- extending Step 253's (S1618) primitive audit with explicit removal-test rigor.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Relation = structurally necessary candidate but Relation = primitive ontology is not established. ... if all relations are removed, the remaining objects become semantically disconnected ... Is Relation itself primitive, or is relation structure part of the mathematical representation of objects? Th
a_rows_sample.statement: Runs the removal test for Relation, finding it structurally necessary (its removal disconnects all remaining objects semantically) but not established as primitive ontology, leaving open whether Relation is itself primitive or merely part of how mathematical structure represents objects -- consistent with Step 253's (S1618) ontological-vs-structural-primitive distinction.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Transformation is the strongest historically supported kernel role [8/9]. We cannot yet say Transformation is mathematically primitive. ... Provenance in I* across all nine historical phases, yet it is absent from the latest kernels. Transformation: kernel-prominent, historically near-universal vers
a_rows_sample.statement: Identifies a striking historical asymmetry: Transformation is the strongest historically-supported kernel role (present in 8 of 9 kernel candidates across the corpus's history) yet not proven mathematically primitive, while Provenance is the ONLY concept invariant across all 9 historical kernel phases (I*={Provenance}) yet is absent from the latest (Step 230/232) kernels -- historically-universal does not equal kernel-prominent, and vice versa; this asymmetry is a reason the current exclusion of Provenance cannot be justified by the History(T) argument, though it is not yet grounds to insert Provenance into the kernel.

a_rows_sample.anchor: K* = argmin_{K_i} Complexity(K_i) subject to: forall T in T: F o That = T o F, and Identity, Provenance, Admissibility, History being preserved whenever the domain requires them. This is much stronger than the historical 'smallest tuple' approach. ... Mathematical minimality != smallest number of fi
a_rows_sample.statement: Redefines the minimality target as a constrained optimization K*=argmin Complexity(K_i) subject to the congruence criterion holding for all transformations plus preservation of Identity/Provenance/Admissibility/History where required, explicitly rejecting cardinality (fewest fields) as a valid minimality criterion -- two models of equal or smaller size are not automatically better if they lose required semantics.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Content-only: Falsified as universal candidate. Structured state (Content,Qualification,Governance,...): remains viable. History-inclusive state (State,Lineage,Provenance,...): also remains viable. No candidate has yet passed all requirements.
a_rows_sample.statement: Consolidates candidate state representations into 3 groups: content-only is falsified as a universal candidate; a structured (Content,Qualification,Governance) model and a history-inclusive (State,Lineage,Provenance) model both remain viable, with neither yet passing all requirements -- narrowing but not resolving the architecture question.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Lineage is insufficient as a universal substitute for provenance. It may still be sufficient for internal transformation lineage. That narrower claim survives. ... The Step-232 reconstruction ... fixed only one of nine properties and did not establish typing, determinism, composability, computabilit
a_rows_sample.statement: Confirms lineage (History(T)) is insufficient as a universal substitute for provenance but remains sufficient for internal transformation lineage under explicit assumptions; separately notes Step 232's addition of Policy fixed only 1 of 9 required kernel properties (leaving typing, determinism, composability, computability, minimality, independence unaddressed) and that Policy being required for transformation-closure does not imply Policy is part of the Knowledge State -- governance may constrain transformations externally without becoming knowledge content.

a_rows_sample.anchor: MINIMAL KERNEL NOT FOUND but also MINIMALITY TEST IS NOW FORMALLY SPECIFIED and THE FIRST IMPORTANT COUNTEREXAMPLE EXISTS: provenance at t=0. ... Semantic sufficiency -> congruence -> minimality, not: small tuple -> assumed sufficiency.
a_rows_sample.statement: States the step's final verdict: no minimal kernel found, but the minimality test itself is now formally specified and a concrete counterexample (provenance at t=0) exists; reframes the correct methodological order as semantic-sufficiency-then-congruence-then-minimality, never starting from an assumed-sufficient small tuple.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Decision 1 -- Is provenance semantically part of Knowledge? [Interpretation A: Provenance subseteq KnowledgeState; B: separate audit substrate] ... Decision 2 -- Must KnowledgeOS support exact historical reconstruction? [exact Replay vs observationally-equivalent] ... Decision 3 -- Is governance/aut
a_rows_sample.statement: Invokes the governing mandate's escalation rule and stops to name 4 genuinely normative REQUIRES-USER-DECISION items with their alternative interpretations and consequences spelled out (provenance's constitutive status; exact vs observationally-equivalent replay; whether governance participates in semantic equality; which operations are mandatory, since minimality is relative to the transformation set), explicitly stating that without these decisions the mathematical attack can continue but no final minimal kernel can be legitimately declared.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Step 255 -- State/History Congruence and Counterexample Catalogue ... construct explicit pairs (H1,H2) and systematically test F(H1)=F(H2) against every mandatory operation. The decisive experiment will be: F(H1)=F(H2) but T(H1)!=T(H2)? If such a case exists, state-only semantics fail.
a_rows_sample.statement: Sets Step 255 as a systematic State/History Congruence and Counterexample Catalogue, requiring construction of history pairs and testing every mandatory operation against the congruence criterion, with the decisive falsification pattern being a pair where the state abstraction collapses (F(H1)=F(H2)) but a legitimate operation still distinguishes them (T(H1)!=T(H2)).

a_rows_sample.anchor: External provenance at t=0: STRONGEST [formally established]. Content-only vs epistemic status/authority/evidence: CONDITIONAL. Conflict history, transformation lineage, withdrawal/reintroduction, merge history, policy regime, time-dependent policy: CANDIDATE. Only the first should currently be trea
a_rows_sample.statement: Produces a 10-class counterexample catalogue against content-only state sufficiency (external provenance, epistemic standing, authority, evidence, conflict history, transformation lineage, withdrawal/reintroduction, merge history, policy regime, time-dependent policy), rating only the external-provenance-at-t=0 class (from S1620) as formally established, with the other 9 explicitly downgraded to conditional or candidate pending an authoritative operation definition -- an honest strength-graded inventory rather than treating all counterexamples as equally proven.

a_rows_sample.anchor: That does not logically imply Provenance subseteq K. There are at least three possibilities: P subseteq K or P subseteq H or P subseteq ExternalAudit. The formal result is only: P must be preserved somewhere if provenance semantics are required. This is a much stronger and cleaner conclusion.
a_rows_sample.statement: Resolves an apparent contradiction from S1620: proving provenance cannot be reconstructed from History(T) does NOT logically imply provenance must be inside K; instead 3 placements remain possible (inside K, inside H, or inside a separate external audit substrate), and the only proven result is that provenance must be preserved SOMEWHERE if provenance semantics are required -- a cleaner, weaker, and more defensible conclusion than the earlier framing.

a_rows_sample.anchor: K should encode exactly the distinctions required by future semantics. Minimality = coarsest operationally valid equivalence. This is a much more powerful mathematical definition.
a_rows_sample.statement: States the field-independent minimality reformulation: minimality equals the coarsest operationally valid equivalence on histories (K should encode exactly the distinctions required by future semantics, nothing more and nothing less), superseding the earlier 'how many fields' framing and directly instantiating S1620's constrained-optimization minimality target.

b_rows_sample.anchor: We must distinguish at least three relations: =_X object equality, equiv_K Knowledge-State equivalence, ~_H history equivalence. They answer different questions ... These must not be collapsed into one relation.
b_rows_sample.statement: Formalizes 3 distinct sameness relations for KnowledgeOS -- object equality (are two knowledge objects the same per the object model), Knowledge-State equivalence (are two states indistinguishable for all semantically relevant operations), and history equivalence (are two histories equivalent with respect to resulting semantic behavior) -- explicitly forbidding their collapse into one relation.

b_rows_sample.anchor: x1=(id=42,content=A) and x2=(id=42,content=B). They may represent different versions of the same knowledge entity. Identity persistence != value equality. This is exactly what Revision requires.
b_rows_sample.statement: Proves identity persistence and value equality are distinct via a minimal worked example (same id, different content = two versions of the same entity), noting this is exactly the distinction Revision requires to exist.

b_rows_sample.anchor: x=(i,v,s,p,m) [identity, value, status, provenance, metadata] -- not yet the final Knowledge Object definition. It is a diagnostic model. ... =_I identity equality, =_V content equality, =_S full structural equality, =_E semantic equality [the least trivial to define].
b_rows_sample.statement: Proposes a diagnostic (not final) 5-field Knowledge Object model x=(identity,value,status,provenance,metadata) and defines 4 candidate object-equality relations over it (identity-only, content-only, full-structural, and semantic equality -- the last flagged as most important and least trivial to define).

b_rows_sample.anchor: =_I cannot by itself be the semantic equality relation [fails Revise, which requires semantic change while identity persists]. ... Content equality cannot replace identity [fails Merge/Supersede, which must distinguish independently-created identical-content objects].
b_rows_sample.statement: Proves both identity-only equality and content-only equality are individually insufficient as the semantic equality relation: identity-only equality cannot represent Revise (which needs semantic change while identity persists); content-only equality cannot represent Merge/Supersede (which must distinguish two independently-created objects with identical content).

b_rows_sample.anchor: K1 equiv_K K2 iff no mandatory KnowledgeOS observation or transformation can distinguish them. Formally: forall O in mathcal-O: O(K1)=O(K2). For transitions we need the stronger congruence condition: K1 equiv_K K2 => T(K1,c) equiv_K T(K2,c) for all admissible common contexts c.
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines Knowledge-State equivalence observationally (agreement on every semantically relevant observation), then states the stronger transformation-congruence requirement that equivalence must be preserved by every valid transformation -- the critical test for whether the proposed equivalence is too coarse.

b_rows_sample.anchor: H1 ~_H H2 iff all permitted future operation sequences produce equivalent states. Formally, for every admissible sequence sigma=Tn o ... o T1, we require F(sigma(H1)) equiv_K F(sigma(H2)). ... If sim_H is a valid behavioral equivalence relation, then Knowledge State can potentially be understood as
b_rows_sample.statement: Strengthens history equivalence beyond the naive current-state-collapse definition into full behavioral equivalence (agreement of outcomes under every admissible future operation sequence, not just the current state), reaffirming Step 247's (S1609) candidate quotient definition K=[H]_{~_H} as a powerful but still unproven formulation.

b_rows_sample.anchor: F(H1)=F(H2) iff H1 ~_H H2 would mean that the state representation exactly captures the behavioral equivalence classes. That would be a major theoretical result. We have not demonstrated this yet.
b_rows_sample.statement: States the ideal biconditional quotient criterion (F(H1)=F(H2) iff H1 and H2 are behaviorally equivalent) as the major unproven theoretical result the whole state-abstraction programme is aiming at.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Counterexample class A (provenance) ... if a future operation TraceOrigin(x) must return different results, H1 not-similar H2. ... Different provenance does not automatically imply different Knowledge State. Class B (revision history): conditional on ExplainRevision being required. Class C (identity
b_rows_sample.statement: Applies the counterexample-class methodology (from S1621) to 4 specific classes -- provenance, revision history, identity-vs-content, identity-vs-status -- each showing content-only or identity-only state abstractions fail whenever some mandatory operation actually observes the discarded distinction, with each case's status remaining conditional on which operations are mandatory.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Identity -> Object equality -> State equality/equivalence -> Behavioral/history equivalence. But this should not be interpreted as a strict mathematical hierarchy where each relation is automatically derived from the previous one. They are separate semantic constructs connected by explicit rules.
b_rows_sample.statement: Presents a suggestive but explicitly non-derivational ordering of 4 sameness concepts (identity, object equality, state equivalence, behavioral/history equivalence), warning against treating it as a strict hierarchy where each is automatically derivable from the last -- they remain separate constructs connected only by explicit rules.

b_rows_sample.anchor: OperationalIdentity(x) if exists T in T such that changing id(x) can change T(K,c). ... Relevant(p) if there exists a mandatory operation T and states K1,K2 differing only in p such that T(K1,c) not-equiv_K T(K2,c). Then p cannot be discarded from the semantic state representation unless it is suppl
b_rows_sample.statement: Generalizes identity-relevance into a fully general 'operational relevance' test for any candidate property p: p is Relevant if some mandatory operation and a pair of states differing only in p produce non-equivalent outcomes, in which case p cannot be discarded from the semantic state unless supplied externally -- giving a single principled, uniform criterion applicable to identity, provenance, policy, evidence, or any other candidate field.

b_rows_sample.anchor: K* = minimum information sufficient to preserve all mandatory behavioral distinctions. Not: K*=everything ever observed. And not: K*=smallest tuple someone can invent. This is the mathematically meaningful notion of minimality.
b_rows_sample.statement: States the minimal-state principle in its final form: K* is the minimum information sufficient to preserve all mandatory behavioral distinctions -- explicitly neither an unbounded record of everything ever observed nor an arbitrarily small invented tuple.

b_rows_sample.anchor: pi(T_H(H,c)) = T_bar(pi(H),c) ... The diagram must commute. This is the formal test that the state abstraction correctly represents the history semantics. ... Proposition 258-A: A candidate Knowledge-State abstraction F is semantically admissible only if every mandatory transformation factors throug
b_rows_sample.statement: States the formal admissibility criterion (Proposition 258-A) as the definitive version of the congruence/commuting-diagram requirement first developed in Step 248 (S1608): a state abstraction F is semantically admissible only if every mandatory transformation factors through it via a corresponding state-level function.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Does provenance belong in K? can now be answered experimentally. We do not ask philosophically. We ask: exists T: F(H1)=F(H2) but F(T_H(H1)) != F(T_H(H2))? If yes, F is insufficient. Then either: enrich K; supply the missing information as explicit context; remove the operation from the semantic cor
b_rows_sample.statement: Converts the recurring philosophical provenance-placement question into a purely operational test, and gives an explicit 3-way resolution menu when the test fails (enrich K, supply the information as explicit external context, or remove the offending operation from the semantic core) -- noting only the first two options preserve the operation itself.

b_rows_sample.anchor: K should be defined extensionally through behavioral sufficiency, not compositionally through an arbitrary tuple. ... Do not start with K=(a,b,c,d). Start with: Which distinctions must survive for all valid operations? Then derive the minimal state.
b_rows_sample.statement: States the step's deepest and most general finding: Knowledge State should be defined EXTENSIONALLY through behavioral sufficiency (what distinctions must survive for all valid operations) rather than COMPOSITIONALLY by inventing a tuple of fields and justifying it afterward -- a reversal of the corpus's dominant historical methodology for proposing kernels.

b_rows_sample.anchor: The earlier candidate K=(K,C,T,E,A) should therefore be treated as a meta-structure, not automatically as the mathematical state itself. ... K must first be derived from observational equivalence. Only afterward should we decide whether C,E,A,P,... belong inside K, outside K, or are parameters of tr
b_rows_sample.statement: Demotes the long-standing (K,C,T,E,A) candidate from a proposed mathematical state to a mere meta-structure/naming convention, since the derivation order must instead begin from observational equivalence and only afterward assign each component (C,E,A,P,...) to inside-K, outside-K, or transformation-parameter status.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Identity != Equality. Object equality != State equivalence. State equivalence != History equivalence. A valid state abstraction must satisfy transformation congruence. Operation dependence does not imply state membership. Minimality must be defined behaviorally.
b_rows_sample.statement: Consolidates 6 established results from Step 258: Identity!=Equality; Object equality!=State equivalence; State equivalence!=History equivalence; valid state abstractions must satisfy transformation congruence; operation dependence never implies state membership; minimality must be defined behaviorally, not by inspection.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Operations -> Observations -> Equivalence -> State quotient -> Minimal K, rather than: Invent K -> try to justify it afterward. ... Step 259 -- First Concrete Congruence Experiment ... using the smallest possible states -- ideally two objects and one transformation -- so that any failure can be attr
b_rows_sample.statement: States the final derivation-order principle (Operations -> Observations -> Equivalence -> State quotient -> Minimal K, reversing the corpus's typical Invent-K-then-justify approach) and sets Step 259 as the first executable congruence counterexample, deliberately using the smallest possible states (two objects, one transformation) so any failure isolates exactly one missing semantic dimension.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Det(E) != Truth != Knowledge != Belief ... Det != Truth: Truth is an objective or ontological state; Det is a bounded computation under a specific threshold vector tau. Det != Knowledge: Knowledge implies justified true belief; Det requires only actionable sufficiency relative to a specified policy. Det != Belief: Belief represents subjective internal alignment; Det is a deterministic, auditable, and reproducible mapping function over EVal.
a_rows_sample.statement: Formalizes the epistemological firebreak Det(E) != Truth != Knowledge != Belief with a per-pair rationale: Truth is objective/ontological while Det is a bounded threshold computation; Knowledge implies justified true belief while Det requires only actionable sufficiency under a policy; Belief is subjective internal alignment while Det is a deterministic, auditable, reproducible mapping over EVal.

a_rows_sample.anchor: tau = <tau_accept+, tau_refute-, tau_margin, omega_prov> ... d_state(E,tau) piecewise: DETERMINED_TRUE if S+>=tau_accept+ and S-<tau_refute- and (S+-S-)>=tau_margin ; DETERMINED_FALSE symmetric; DETERMINED_CONTRADICTION if S+>=tau_accept+ and S->=tau_refute- ; UNDERDETERMINED if both below threshold ; AMBIGUOUS otherwise.
a_rows_sample.statement: Defines the decision threshold vector tau=<tau_accept+,tau_refute-,tau_margin,omega_prov> and the piecewise d_state mapping from Standing (S+,S-) and tau into five discrete determination states (DETERMINED_TRUE, DETERMINED_FALSE, DETERMINED_CONTRADICTION, UNDERDETERMINED, AMBIGUOUS), requiring a margin of dominance |S+-S-|>=tau_margin to resolve TRUE/FALSE ambiguity.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Action Mapping Matrix: DETERMINED_TRUE -> EXECUTE (Proceed with downstream workflow) ; DETERMINED_FALSE -> HALT/REJECT ; DETERMINED_CONTRADICTION -> ESCALATE (Trigger isolation per SPEC-CONTR-2026-v1.0) ; UNDERDETERMINED -> DEFER (Request additional evidence) ; AMBIGUOUS -> DEFER (Request evidence refinement to satisfy tau_margin).
a_rows_sample.statement: Defines the action-mapping matrix tying each DeterminationState to a concrete operational action: EXECUTE (proceed), HALT/REJECT (abort/reject), ESCALATE (trigger SPEC-CONTR isolation and alert a triage supervisor), and DEFER (request additional evidence or evidence refinement) for both UNDERDETERMINED and AMBIGUOUS -- directly wiring Determination's output to the Contradiction spec's isolation mechanism.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Partiality of Determination: Determination can be partial. If an evaluation E lacks sufficient provenance authority (Weight(P) < omega_prov), Det returns PARTIAL_DETERMINATION with an explicit missing requirement vector M = {UnmetThresholds} subseteq tau.
a_rows_sample.statement: Formalizes partial determination: when provenance authority weight falls below the required omega_prov threshold, Det returns PARTIAL_DETERMINATION together with an explicit UnmetThresholds vector M subseteq tau naming which specific thresholds were not met, rather than silently defaulting to a full determination state.

type_signature.domain: evaluation E with insufficient provenance weight

a_rows_sample.anchor: Non-Destructive Thresholding Test: Verify that executing Det under varying threshold vectors tau1 and tau2 produces distinct actions without altering the underlying EVal tuple or state graph R. Epistemological Separation Audit: Verify that no system output or logs treat DETERMINED_TRUE as equivalent to absolute ontological Truth. SPEC-DET-2026-v1.0 is hereby RATIFIED.
a_rows_sample.statement: Specifies two compliance tests for SPEC-DET (Non-Destructive Thresholding -- varying tau must not mutate the underlying EVal/state; Epistemological Separation Audit -- no system output may treat DETERMINED_TRUE as ontological Truth) and issues a self-contained ratification sign-off, the fifth such self-declared RATIFIED spec in this batch's cascade.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Determination is completely missing from the actual document ... the attached document never actually supplies the corresponding SPEC-DET. Therefore: Det remains OPEN. And this is not a minor issue. If Determination is undefined, we cannot honestly say the formal epistemic pipeline is closed.
a_rows_sample.statement: Observes that the reviewed document set, despite its roadmap explicitly requiring Det(EVal,Gamma)->Determination, never actually supplies the corresponding SPEC-DET specification; concludes Det remains OPEN and that the formal epistemic pipeline cannot honestly be called closed while Determination is undefined. Notably, this observation is in apparent tension with another file in this same batch that DOES contain a complete, self-ratified SPEC-DET-2026-v1.0.

a_rows_sample.anchor: O1 Determination (Det): No formal specification exists ... O2 Semantic Equivalence: No formal specification exists ... O3 Canonical Operations (O_core): candidate operations need reduction, split into State-transforming (Assert, Retract, Supersede, Merge, Split, Support, Refute), Observational (Query, Trace, Explain, Compare), and Governance (Authorize, Validate) ... O4 Transition (delta): Only signature exists.
a_rows_sample.statement: Formally records four items as fully OPEN with no formal specification existing: Determination (Det), Semantic Equivalence (equiv_sem), Canonical Operations (O_core, now explicitly pre-classified into State-transforming / Observational / Governance sub-groups pending reduction), and Transition (delta, for which only the bare signature exists).

a_rows_sample.anchor: Package C1 -- EVal + Determination: Key Achievement: Evaluation no longer collapses different failure modes into a single value ... Det mapping defined: Det(EValResult,Gamma) -> Decision.
a_rows_sample.statement: Summarizes Package C1's claimed achievement: EVal now has a typed-boundary domain (5 modes) and no longer collapses different evaluation-failure causes into one value, and Det is defined as a mapping EValResult x Gamma -> Decision that can emit ABSTAIN/DEFER with an attached TypedBoundary rather than a forced UNDERDETERMINED/REFUTED verdict.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Determination is still the biggest genuine missing semantic layer ... this is not something we should solve by inventing: if score > threshold -> determined, because that would collapse Evaluation -> Determination -> Decision into one numerical threshold. We need to establish: Det: EVal x Q x Gamma -> Determination and preserve: Truth != Evaluation != Determination != Decision. ...
